AoU:sdoh_intro.name: sdoh_intro
AoU:sdoh_intro.text:
Thank you (again) for being a part of the All of Us Research Program. Many things can make us sick or keep us healthy. Where you were born or where you live, go to school, or work can affect your health. These are sometimes referred to as social factors, or the "social determinants", of health. Help us learn more by completing this survey about your neighborhood, social life, stress, and feelings about your everyday life. This survey will take less than 10 minutes to complete.

Please answer each question as honestly as possible. It is important that you answer as many questions as you can. We are looking for your own answers, and not what you think your doctors, family, or friends want you to say.

Don't feel like you have to spend a long time on each question. The first answer that comes to you is usually the best one. If you aren't sure how to answer a question, choose the best answer from the options given. Some of the questions may be sensitive. You can choose not to answer.

Help us learn more by completing this survey about your neighborhood, social life, stress, and feelings about your everyday life. This survey will take less than 10 minutes to complete.

Please answer each question as honestly as possible. It is important that you answer as many questions as you can. We are looking for your own answers, and not what you think your doctors, family, or friends want you to say.

Don't feel like you have to spend a long time on each question. The first answer that comes to you is usually the best one. If you aren't sure how to answer a question, choose the best answer from the options given. Some of the questions may be sensitive. You can choose not to answer.

UKBB:Degree to which abdominal pain/disc.name: Degree to which abdominal pain/discomfort/altered bowel habits affect/interfere with life in general
UKBB:Degree to which abdominal pain/disc.text:
Question asked: "Please indicate how much abdominal pain or discomfort or altered bowel habits are affecting or interfering with your life in general."

Participants were asked to move a slider to choose a number between 0 to 10, with 0 meaning "not at all" and 10 meaning "completely". Participants using an older browser were asked to select a button from 0 to 10.

The question in this field was taken from the IBS Severity Scoring System used with the authors' permission.

Francis CY, Morris J, Whorwell PJ. The irritable bowel severity scoring system: a simple method of monitoring irritable bowel syndrome and its progress. Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics 1997;11(2):395-402

UKBB:Income score (England).name: Income score (England)
UKBB:Income score (England).text:
This domain measures the proportion of the population in an area experiencing deprivation related to low income. A combined count of income deprived individuals per LSOA is calculated by summing the following five indicators:
  • Adults and children in Income Support families
  • Adults and children in Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance families
  • Adults and children in Pension Credit (Guarantee) families
  • Adults and children in Child Tax Credit families (who are not in receipt of Income Support, Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance or Pension Credit) whose equivalised income (excluding housing benefits) is below 60 per cent of the median before housing costs
  • Asylum seekers in England in receipt of subsistence support, accommodation support, or both.

UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Engl.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (England)
UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Engl.text:
The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at the small area level. The model of multiple deprivation which underpins the Indices of Deprivation 2010 is based on the idea of distinct domains of deprivation which can be recognised and measured separately. These domains are experienced by individuals living in an area. People may be counted in one or more of the domains, depending on the number of types of deprivation that they experience.

Each domain represents a specific form of deprivation experienced by people and each can be measured individually using a number of indicators. Seven distinct domains have been identified in the English Indices of Deprivation; Income Deprivation, Employment Deprivation, Health Deprivation and Disability, Education Skills and Training Deprivation, Barriers to Housing and Services, Living Environment Deprivation, and Crime. Individual domains can be used in isolation as measures of each specific form of deprivation. They can also be combined, using appropriate weights, into a single overall Index of Multiple Deprivation which can be used to rank every small area in England according to the deprivation experienced by the people living there. Along with two supplementary indices, Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index and Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index, they form the English Indices of Deprivation. These statistics allow the most, and least, deprived areas of the country to be identified as well as providing information about the issues faced by people living in different parts of the country.

UKBB:Income score (Wales).name: Income score (Wales)
UKBB:Income score (Wales).text:
The purpose of this domain is to capture the extent of deprivation relating to income at a small area level across Wales. It focuses on the proportion of people living in households with income below a defined threshold or claiming benefits relating to low incomes. The indicators used for the income domain were:
  • Adults & children in income support households
  • Adults & children in pension credit households
  • Adults & children in income-based job seekers allowance households
  • Adults & children in tax credit (child tax credit and working tax credit) households below a low income threshold
  • National Asylum Support Service (NASS) supported asylum seekers in Wales in receipt of subsistence only and accommodation support

UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time.name: Pulse wave peak to peak time
UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time.text:
peak to peak time in milliseconds

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. peak to peak time is the difference between the peak values of direct and reflected components.

UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wale.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wales)
UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wale.text:
The Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation 2008 is the official measure of deprivation for small areas in Wales. It was developed for the Welsh Assembly Government by the Assembly's Statistical Directorate and the Local Government Data Unit (Wales).

The WIMD 2008 is made up of eight separate domains (or kinds) of deprivation: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety.

Each of them was based on a range of different indicators which meant that they were measured in different ways using different units. So before they could be combined the measurements had to be transformed to make them compatible. For example, if the height of something had been measured in metres and the weight in kilograms it would not make sense simply to add them together.

Income and employment were classed as the most important factors, and they were given the biggest weighting in the overall index. Although there is more to deprivation than poverty, not having enough money or a job is a big part of it.

UKBB:Position of the pulse wave peak.name: Position of the pulse wave peak
UKBB:Position of the pulse wave peak.text:
position of the peak

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. This field is the time when the peak occurs in the waveform.

UKBB:Position of pulse wave notch.name: Position of pulse wave notch
UKBB:Position of pulse wave notch.text:
position of the notch

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. This is the time when when notch occurs in the waveform.

reflection index is a measure of reflection

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. if 'b' is the height of direct wave peak and 'a' is the height of reflected wave peak the reflected index = (a/b) * 100%

returned to your current address for another 5 years, then you would
enter 8 years.

UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time res.name: Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time res.text:
Wave data containing 3 waveforms, each consisting of one direct and one reflected component.

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. Each waveform is actually a single pulse with 100 points. Since the heart rate is in beats per minute, a single beat takes 60seconds / Heart Rate and time between two beats is (60/Heart Rate)/100.

The data is formatted as follows:

  • The first number (i.e. digits before the first '|' character)indicate the number of points X,Y for the curve.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated by a '|' character from the preceding/succeeding pair.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated internally by a ',' character.
The X-axis is the time in milliseconds and the Y-axis is the Pulse signal strength in arbitrary units.

Only asked if one or more of ~F120001~, ~F120007~, ~F120008~ was answered yes.

The question in this field was taken from the Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument (MNSI) licensed by MAPI Research Trust.

Thank you (again) for being a part of the All of Us Research Program. Many things can make us sick or keep us healthy. Where you were born or where you live, go to school, or work can affect your health. These are sometimes referred to as social factors, or the "social determinants", of health. Help us learn more by completing this survey about your neighborhood, social life, stress, and feelings about your everyday life. This survey will take less than 10 minutes to complete.

Please answer each question as honestly as possible. It is important that you answer as many questions as you can. We are looking for your own answers, and not what you think your doctors, family, or friends want you to say.

Don't feel like you have to spend a long time on each question. The first answer that comes to you is usually the best one. If you aren't sure how to answer a question, choose the best answer from the options given. Some of the questions may be sensitive. You can choose not to answer.

  • Public library

unassignedFields.variable: Degree to which abdominal pain/discomfort/altered bowel habits affect/interfere with life in general
unassignedFields.text:
Question asked: "Please indicate how much abdominal pain or discomfort or altered bowel habits are affecting or interfering with your life in general."

Participants were asked to move a slider to choose a number between 0 to 10, with 0 meaning "not at all" and 10 meaning "completely". Participants using an older browser were asked to select a button from 0 to 10.

The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at the small area level. The model of multiple deprivation which underpins the Indices of Deprivation 2010 is based on the idea of distinct domains of deprivation which can be recognised and measured separately. These domains are experienced by individuals living in an area. People may be counted in one or more of the domains, depending on the number of types of deprivation that they experience.

Each domain represents a specific form of deprivation experienced by people and each can be measured individually using a number of indicators. Seven distinct domains have been identified in the English Indices of Deprivation; Income Deprivation, Employment Deprivation, Health Deprivation and Disability, Education Skills and Training Deprivation, Barriers to Housing and Services, Living Environment Deprivation, and Crime. Individual domains can be used in isolation as measures of each specific form of deprivation. They can also be combined, using appropriate weights, into a single overall Index of Multiple Deprivation which can be used to rank every small area in England according to the deprivation experienced by the people living there. Along with two supplementary indices, Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index and Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index, they form the English Indices of Deprivation. These statistics allow the most, and least, deprived areas of the country to be identified as well as providing information about the issues faced by people living in different parts of the country.

The Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation 2008 is the official measure of deprivation for small areas in Wales. It was developed for the Welsh Assembly Government by the Assembly's Statistical Directorate and the Local Government Data Unit (Wales).

The WIMD 2008 is made up of eight separate domains (or kinds) of deprivation: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety.

Each of them was based on a range of different indicators which meant that they were measured in different ways using different units. So before they could be combined the measurements had to be transformed to make them compatible. For example, if the height of something had been measured in metres and the weight in kilograms it would not make sense simply to add them together.

Income and employment were classed as the most important factors, and they were given the biggest weighting in the overall index. Although there is more to deprivation than poverty, not having enough money or a job is a big part of it.

unassignedFields.variable: Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
unassignedFields.text:
Wave data containing 3 waveforms, each consisting of one direct and one reflected component.

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. Each waveform is actually a single pulse with 100 points. Since the heart rate is in beats per minute, a single beat takes 60seconds / Heart Rate and time between two beats is (60/Heart Rate)/100.

The data is formatted as follows:

  • The first number (i.e. digits before the first '|' character)indicate the number of points X,Y for the curve.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated by a '|' character from the preceding/succeeding pair.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated internally by a ',' character.
The X-axis is the time in milliseconds and the Y-axis is the Pulse signal strength in arbitrary units.

conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of mental health and substance use conditions (blood relatives): A multi-part CDE capturing whether any blood relative has ever been diagnosed with specific mental health or substance use disorders, and if so, which family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, or other blood relative) are affected for each condition. The screening question asks whether any blood relative has ever received a diagnosis from a defined list of conditions (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety reaction/panic disorder, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and others); for each condition endorsed, a follow-up question identifies which specific biological family relationship(s) carry that diagnosis. Answer type: two-tier checkbox structure — Tier 1: multi-select categorical list of mental health/substance use condition categories (select all that apply); Tier 2: for each selected condition, a multi-select categorical list of biological family member relationship types (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, other blood relative). No laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified. Note: the source concept also includes a separate, distinct field capturing self-reported sleeping pill use in the past 2 weeks (ordinal frequency: No / A few days [<1 day/week] / Some days [1–2 days/week] / Most days [3–4 days/week] / Every day; with a 'Decline to answer' option), which carries a different qualifier (self, past-2-week window) and measures a different construct (own medication behavior) from the family history fields.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Current treatment/medication status, diagnosis details, and free-text specification for mental health and substance use conditions
conceptGroups.coherenceAxis: mental health or substance use condition

conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical Activity Assessment: A multi-dimensional CDE capturing self-reported frequency and intensity of physical activity across multiple domains (light/home-based exercise such as stretching, calisthenics, or yoga; moderate activity such as carrying light loads, bicycling at regular pace, or doubles tennis; and vigorous activity such as hiking, jogging, heavy lifting, aerobics, or fast bicycling), as well as objective physical activity monitor data availability. The CDE answers: 'How frequently does the participant engage in physical activity at each intensity level, and was objective activity monitor data collected?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale for self-reported items (e.g., daily/almost daily, irregular/1–2 times per week, rarely/none; or days per week with duration thresholds such as ≥30 min on ≥3 days/week), binary yes/no for vigorous and moderate activity participation in the past 7 days, and binary yes/no for physical activity monitor data download status; units: categorical frequency categories or days per week, with intensity stratified into light/home-based, moderate, and vigorous tiers.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Able to walk or cycle unaided for 10 minutes
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Total physical activity energy expenditure expressed in MET-minutes per week, covering moderate and/or vigorous activity across the full week.

conceptGroups.concept: Survey/form completion or start date and time (instrument-qualified)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Survey/form completion date and time: the date (and, where applicable, time) on which a specific survey or consent form was completed or submitted by the participant. Answers the question: 'When was this instrument completed?' Expected answer type: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) or datetime (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss) string, with the specific instrument (e.g., paper consent, CES-D-10, dietary survey) identified as a qualifier. Note: member fields carry different instrument qualifiers (paper consent form, CES-D-10 questionnaire, dietary survey) and some distinguish start vs. completion timestamps; each instrument-specific date/datetime should be captured as a separate CDE instance qualified by instrument name and event type (started vs. completed).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Timestamps or dates recording when a survey or consent form was started or completed within a study data collection system.

conceptGroups.concept: CES-D individual item — self-reported frequency of specific depressive symptom in past week
conceptGroups.idealCde: CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) individual item response — Concept: Self-reported frequency of a specific depressive or psychological symptom experienced by the respondent during the past week, as measured by a single CES-D scale item (e.g., feeling bothered by things, trouble concentrating, feeling depressed, effortfulness of activities, feeling fearful). Question: 'How often during the past week did you experience [specific symptom]?' Answer type: Ordinal radio-button selection scored 0–3, where 0 = Rarely or none of the time (<1 day), 1 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 2 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 3 = All of the time (5–7 days); self-report, past-7-day reference window.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported depressive symptom experiences (e.g., feeling depressed, lonely, effortful, bothered, hopeless, or inattentive) as measured by CES-D-style items

conceptGroups.concept: Miscellaneous unrelated fields (anthropometric measures, diabetes survey metadata, birth weight, bone density, etc.)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Age at first diagnosis of a specified condition (self-reported): captures the life-stage age category at which the respondent was first told by a healthcare provider that they had a given medical condition. The question asked is 'About how old were you when you were first told you had [condition]?' with [condition] being a condition-specific qualifier (e.g., congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, high cholesterol). Answer type is an ordinal categorical variable with values: Child (0–11), Adolescent (12–17), Adult (18–64), Older Adult (65–74), and implicitly an oldest adult category (75+). Each condition constitutes a distinct CDE instance sharing this structure. Subject is self (the survey respondent). Note: the source concept also includes heterogeneous fields (diabetes survey date as free-text date, and waist-to-hip ratio as a calculated numeric value) that do not share this measurement construct and represent separate CDEs.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of specific cancer type: which biological relatives have been diagnosed (multi-select relative per cancer type)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of cancer by cancer type and affected biological relative: For each specific cancer type (e.g., bladder cancer, blood/soft tissue cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, and other cancer types), identifies which first- and second-degree biological relatives have been diagnosed with that cancer. The question asked is 'Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.' The answer is a multi-select checkbox response where each selectable option represents a specific biological relative relationship (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent, and potentially other relatives). Answer type: categorical multi-select (select all that apply); one such CDE per cancer type, with response options representing distinct biological relative categories (e.g., Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent).

conceptGroups.concept: Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Highest level of educational attainment (degree, diploma, or grade) completed by the respondent

conceptGroups.concept: Seated diastolic blood pressure reading (mmHg), by reading sequence (1st/2nd/3rd)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Blood pressure measurement (seated position) — captures both systolic and diastolic components at a specified reading number (1st, 2nd, etc.) during a seated blood pressure assessment. Question: 'What was the [systolic/diastolic] blood pressure value recorded at the [1st/2nd] reading while the subject was seated?' Answer type: integer or numeric; units: mmHg. The CDE should be structured as a paired systolic/diastolic measurement with reading-sequence qualifier (1st reading, 2nd reading) and posture qualifier (seated), yielding four discrete values: seated systolic 1st reading, seated diastolic 1st reading, seated systolic 2nd reading, seated diastolic 2nd reading — each expressed in mmHg.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Seated diastolic blood pressure readings (individual measurements) in mmHg

conceptGroups.concept: Exertional leg/buttock pain claudication screening (Rose/Edinburgh Questionnaire items)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication screening): a structured assessment capturing the presence, characteristics, and behavior of leg or buttock pain during walking. Answers the questions: (1) Does the subject experience pain in the leg or buttock while walking? (Yes/No); (2) Does the pain include the calf/calves? (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves); (3) Does the leg pain ever disappear while continuing to walk? (Yes/No); (4) On which side is the leg pain predominant? (Right | Left | Both); (5) Does leg pain occur when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground? (Yes/No). Answer type: categorical/binary responses per sub-item, collectively forming a standardized claudication symptom questionnaire (consistent with Rose/Edinburgh Claudication Questionnaire methodology). No units; responses are nominal/ordinal coded values.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Leg pain when standing still or sitting
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Assessment of leg pain characteristics during walking, including location, onset, and relief — consistent with claudication/peripheral artery disease screening

conceptGroups.concept: Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Body Mass Index (BMI) measurement across cohort visits and sub-studies

conceptGroups.concept: Number of cigarettes smoked per day (average or current)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and marijuana use history — a composite set of substance use history fields capturing: (1) lifetime cigarette use threshold (whether the respondent has smoked ≥100 cigarettes in their lifetime; binary Yes/No); (2) age at smoking initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started smoking cigarettes; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (3) total duration of cigarette smoking (number of years the respondent has smoked; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (4) average daily cigarette consumption (typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, expressed as an ordinal banded count in increments up to >50 cigarettes/day, with pack equivalents noted); and (5) age at marijuana use initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started using marijuana; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years). All fields are self-reported, refer to the respondent themselves, and carry no specific time-window qualifier beyond lifetime/habitual use. Answer types: binary radio for lifetime threshold; ordinal dropdown bands (integer-anchored, self-referent) for age-at-initiation and duration fields; ordinal dropdown bands with pack-equivalent annotations for daily cigarette quantity.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported number of cigarettes smoked per day (current or average)

conceptGroups.concept: Specific cancer type(s) diagnosed (multi-select checklist per cancer type)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Cancer diagnosis history (any type): A CDE capturing whether the participant has ever been diagnosed with cancer of any type, as reported by a physician. The primary question is: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you had cancer (any type)?' Answer type: categorical/boolean (Yes / No). Supplementary component: multi-select checklist of specific cancer types diagnosed (e.g., bladder cancer [cct_cantp_bl], breast cancer [cct_cantp_br], and additional types), each as a binary Yes/No indicator. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified in the source fields; the concept is lifetime/ever diagnosis with no restricted time window.

conceptGroups.concept: Sex of subject/participant (general, binary)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sex and Gender Identity — A composite concept capturing two related but distinct self-reported attributes: (1) Sex assigned at birth: the biological sex recorded at birth, answering 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' with a categorical response (Male | Female | Intersex | Other/None of these); and (2) Gender identity: the gender the participant currently identifies with, answering 'What is your current gender identity?' with a categorical response (Man/Male [including transgender men] | Woman/Female [including transgender women] | Non-binary | Genderqueer | Genderfluid | Trans man/FTM | Trans woman/MTF | Other) — ideally collected as two separate fields: one radio/select for sex assigned at birth and one multi-select checkbox for gender identity (allowing selection of a closer descriptor), both self-reported by the participant with an 'Other' or 'None of these describe me' write-in option. conceptGroups.concept: Frequency/servings of vegetable consumption
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Frequency or amount of vegetable consumption, covering various vegetable subgroups (other vegetables, cruciferous, green leafy, dark yellow) or total vegetables.

conceptGroups.concept: Seated systolic blood pressure reading (mmHg), by reading sequence (1st/2nd/3rd)

The CDE should be structured as a paired systolic/diastolic measurement with reading-sequence qualifier (1st reading, 2nd reading) and posture qualifier (seated), yielding four discrete values: seated systolic 1st reading, seated diastolic 1st reading, seated systolic 2nd reading, seated diastolic 2nd reading — each expressed in mmHg.

conceptGroups.concept: Physical functional mobility — walking and ambulatory activity ability

Expected answer type: ordinal categorical scale reflecting difficulty or independence level (e.g., No difficulty / A little difficulty / Moderate difficulty / Extreme difficulty / Unable; or Yes/No for unaided walking; or a graded frequency/extent scale). Note: member fields carry heterogeneous qualifiers — some assess general walking ability (unaided ambulation, yes/no), some assess difficulty with stairs and everyday physical activities, one specifically qualifies walking difficulty as attributable to eyesight (vision-related peripheral awareness while walking), and one captures fatigue-related inability to initiate movement ('get going'); these represent distinct sub-constructs (functional mobility, vision-related mobility limitation, fatigue-related initiation) that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than collapsed into one.

conceptGroups.concept: Body weight numeric value
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Waist circumference measurement in cm

conceptGroups.concept: Chest pain or discomfort screening (presence, exertional triggers, relief)

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of circulatory/cardiovascular conditions (which blood relatives have had specific heart/blood conditions)

conceptGroups.concept: Specific activity types prevented by pain or discomfort (multi-select checklist)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Pain/Discomfort Activity Limitation: Captures the extent to which pain or discomfort prevents participation in activities, including both a summary frequency/severity rating and identification of specific activity types affected. Primary question: 'How many activities does your pain or discomfort prevent?' with ordinal response options (none, a few, some, most); supplemented by a multi-select checklist or free-text enumeration of specific prevented activities (e.g., sitting, bending/crouching, handling objects, and other activities), allowing multiple responses. Answer type: composite — (1) ordinal categorical scale [none / a few / some / most] for overall activity limitation count, and (2) multi-select categorical list of specific activity types prevented, coded as binary indicators per activity domain.

conceptGroups.concept: Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary Yes/No
conceptGroups.idealCde: This source concept clusters several distinct circulatory/medical-history elements that should ideally be represented as separate CDEs: (1) Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had high blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had high blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (2) Low blood pressure lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had low blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had low blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (3) Age at first hypertension diagnosis — self-reported age category at which the participant was first told they had hypertension; question: 'About how old were you when you were first told you had hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Ordinal categorical (Child [0–11], Adolescent [12–17], Adult [18–64], Older adult [65–74], Older adult [75+]). (4) Current hypertension treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (5) Current peripheral vascular disease treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No).

conceptGroups.concept: Participant's age in completed years (numeric value)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Age at time of assessment — numeric value representing the participant's age in completed years. Question: 'What is your age?' Expected answer: integer, units = years. Note: one member field (Q3 HOW OLD ARE YOU) captures interviewer-rated accuracy of age recall rather than age itself (ordinal accuracy scale: correct / missed by 1–3 years / missed by >3 years / not attempted); this accuracy-rating variant should be treated as a distinct CDE from the direct age-value CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Currently still seeing a doctor/health care provider for a specific condition (CHF, coronary artery disease, high cholesterol, hypertension, STIs)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current Medical Management Status: A composite concept capturing whether an individual is currently under active medical care or treatment for cardiovascular and metabolic conditions, and what medications they are currently taking. Specifically addresses: (1) whether the person is currently seeing a doctor or health care provider for each of the following conditions — congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, and high cholesterol; and (2) whether the person is currently taking any medications (prescription, over-the-counter, vitamins, or herbal supplements) not otherwise captured, along with free-text entry of medication names. Answer types: binary Yes/No radio responses for each current-care question (one per named condition); binary Yes/No radio for additional medication presence; free-text string for medication name(s). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; subject is the self-reporting participant.

conceptGroups.concept: Heart rate in beats per minute
conceptGroups.idealCde: This source concept is heterogeneous and conflates multiple distinct measurements: (1) Heart Rate — the resting pulse rate in beats per minute (bpm), captured as a numeric value; question: 'What is the subject's heart rate?'; answer type: integer or decimal, units: beats per minute (bpm). (2) Eidon CFP Mosaic Image Creation — whether a color fundus photography mosaic image was created using the Eidon device; question: 'Was an Eidon mosaic CFP image created?'; answer type: boolean (Yes/No). (3) OD Autorefractor Axis — the axis of the refractive correction for the right eye (oculus dexter) as measured by autorefractor; question: 'What is the autorefractor-measured axis for the right eye?'; answer type: integer, units: degrees (0–180). (4) OD Autorefractor Cylinder — the cylindrical (astigmatic) refractive power for the right eye as measured by autorefractor; question: 'What is the autorefractor-measured cylinder power for the right eye?'; answer type: decimal, units: diopters (D). These should be represented as separate CDEs; no single ideal CDE can unify them.

conceptGroups.concept: Doctor-confirmed asthma diagnosis — subject, binary Yes/No
conceptGroups.idealCde: Chronic pulmonary/lung disease history and current management status: A composite domain capturing (1) lifetime diagnosis of chronic pulmonary/lung conditions (e.g., emphysema, asthma, tuberculosis, asbestosis) — binary Yes/No; (2) asthma-specific sub-elements: (a) whether the participant is currently seeing a healthcare provider for asthma — binary Yes/No, (b) age at first asthma diagnosis — ordinal categorical [Child (0–11) | Adolescent (12–17) | Adult (18–64) | Older adult (65–74) | Elderly (75+)], (c) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for asthma — binary Yes/No; and (3) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for chronic lung disease (non-asthma) — binary Yes/No. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified. The domain answers: 'Has the participant ever been diagnosed with a chronic pulmonary condition, and what is their current care and treatment status for asthma and/or chronic lung disease?' Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal radio for age-of-onset item.

conceptGroups.concept: Area-level multiple deprivation index score or domain sub-score (composite or domain-specific: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, community safety) for small geographic areas (LSOA/WIMD)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Area-level multiple deprivation index score or domain sub-score capturing the degree of socioeconomic deprivation experienced by residents of a small geographic area (e.g., Lower Super Output Area/LSOA in England or Wales). The CDE answers: 'What is the composite or domain-specific deprivation level for this geographic area, encompassing dimensions such as income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety?' Answer type: continuous numeric score or rank (dimensionless index value or percentile rank), assigned at the small-area geographic unit level, derived from a weighted combination of domain indicators (e.g., proportion of income-deprived individuals, geographical access distances to key services including food shops, GP surgeries, primary schools, post offices, and public libraries). May be reported as an overall multiple deprivation score/rank or as individual domain scores/ranks (income deprivation, access to services deprivation, etc.) for the specified area.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of diabetes by relative type (Type 1, Type 2, other/unknown) — which relatives have been diagnosed
conceptGroups.idealCde: Diabetes family history and personal diagnosis history: captures (1) whether first-degree relatives (parents, siblings, children) have been diagnosed with Type 1, Type 2, or other/unknown diabetes — answered per relative type via yes/no or multi-select checkbox; and (2) the approximate age at which the respondent was first told they had Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes — answered via age-group categories (Child 0–11, Adolescent 12–17, Adult 18–64, Older Adult 65–74, Older Adult 75+). Answer types: binary yes/no per relative category for family history items; ordinal age-group category for self-reported age-at-diagnosis items. Qualifiers vary by field: family history fields specify the relative (parent, sibling, daughter, son); age-at-diagnosis fields specify diabetes type (Type 1 vs. Type 2) and refer to the respondent (self).

conceptGroups.concept: Electronic nicotine product / e-cigarette use — current and ever
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and nicotine product use status (self-reported, participant): A set of current and lifetime use indicators covering multiple tobacco/nicotine delivery modalities — (1) current cigarette smoking (yes/no), (2) current e-cigarette/vaping use (yes/no), (3) ever e-cigarette/vaping use (yes/no), (4) ever traditional cigar/cigarillo/filtered cigar use (yes/no), and (5) current traditional cigar/cigarillo/filtered cigar use frequency (every day / some days / not at all). Each item answers 'Does/Did the participant currently or ever use [specific product]?' Answer types are binary yes/no for ever-use and current-use items, and an ordinal frequency category (every day, some days, not at all) for current cigar use frequency; all responses are self-reported by the study participant.

conceptGroups.concept: Race/ethnicity numeric category or aggregate group variable
conceptGroups.idealCde: Hispanic/Latino Ethnicity and Ancestry Identity: Captures a person's self-reported ethnic origin and ancestry, answering 'What is your ancestry or ethnic origin, and do you identify as Hispanic, Latina/x, or of Spanish origin?' The CDE accommodates two complementary response modes: (1) a free-text field for open-ended ancestry or ethnic origin description (e.g., Italian, Jamaican, Cherokee, Korean, Nigerian), and (2) a structured multi-select checkbox for Hispanic/Latino subgroup identity with options including: No; Yes – Mexican; Yes – Puerto Rican; Yes – Cuban; Yes – Dominican Republic; Yes – Central American; Yes – South American; Yes – Chicano; Yes – Other. Answer type: composite — free-text string for ancestry narrative plus categorical multi-select enumeration for Hispanic/Latino affiliation. No qualifier for subject other than self-report (respondent is the subject). No laterality or body-site qualifier applies.

conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported clinician-diagnosed stroke (Yes/No)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Self-reported history of cerebrovascular events (stroke and/or transient ischemic attack [TIA/mini-stroke]) in the participant themselves, capturing: (1) presence/absence of a clinician-diagnosed stroke (Yes/No); (2) age at first diagnosis of stroke, categorized as Child (0–11), Adolescent (12–17), Adult (18–64), Older Adult (65–74), or Elderly (75+); (3) age at first diagnosis of TIA/mini-stroke, using the same ordinal age-band categories; (4) whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for stroke (Yes/No); and (5) whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for TIA/mini-stroke (Yes/No). Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal categorical age-band radio for age-at-diagnosis items. All items are self-report, first-person (subject = self).

conceptGroups.concept: Population-level percentage of adults aged 25+ with at least a high school education (area-level education statistic)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'

conceptGroups.concept: General overall health self-rating (excellent–poor scale)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Positive affect / well-being item from the CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) positive subscale: a single self-report item asking the respondent how often during the past week they experienced a specific positive emotional state (e.g., felt hopeful about the future; felt happy). The question is framed as 'During the past week, how often did you feel [positive state]?' Answer type: ordinal 4-point frequency scale anchored to days in the past 7 days — 0 = All of the time (5–7 days), 1 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 2 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 3 = Rarely or none of the time (< 1 day). Note: the source concept cluster contains heterogeneous fields spanning positive affect (CES-D items), sexual/gender identity (closer self-description including queer, polysexual/omnisexual/sapiosexual/pansexual, asexual, two-spirit), a general overall health descriptor, and a 0–10 numeric pain intensity rating (past 7 days average); these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than a single unified element.

conceptGroups.concept: Interviewer identifier code (instrument-specific: CES, diet, ICF, VIAO)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Interviewer identifier code: a text field capturing the unique alphanumeric code assigned to the interviewer or data collector administering a specific study instrument or visit (e.g., CES, diet, ICF). Answer type: free-text string (alphanumeric code). Note: member fields carry instrument-specific qualifiers (CES, diet, ICF), indicating this CDE is instantiated per instrument context rather than as a single generic field. Separate but related fields capture participant primary language (free-text) and whether English is the participant's first language (boolean: Yes/No).

conceptGroups.concept: Languages in which participant can conduct a conversation (per language: Arabic, Chinese, English, French)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Interviewer identifier code: a text field capturing the unique alphanumeric code assigned to the interviewer or data collector administering a specific study instrument or visit (e.g., CES, diet, ICF). Separate but related fields capture participant primary language (free-text) and whether English is the participant's first language (boolean: Yes/No).

conceptGroups.concept: Frequency/servings of fruit consumption
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

conceptGroups.concept: Frequency/amount of butter, margarine, or fat used on vegetables, bread, or potatoes
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). conceptGroups.concept: Reasons contributing to decision to retire (multi-select Yes/No checklist)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Retirement circumstances and decision-making: A set of CDEs capturing the context and motivations surrounding an individual's retirement and, if applicable, return to work. Covers: (1) reasons contributing to the decision to retire (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (2) reasons contributing to the decision to return to work after first retirement (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (3) whether health-related retirement was due to physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both (single-select categorical: Physical health | Emotional/mental health including stress | Both); (4) whether the respondent contributed to an employer pension plan other than CPP/QPP prior to retirement (single-select categorical: Yes | No). All items are self-reported by the respondent about their own retirement experience. Answer types are binary Yes/No per factor for reason checklists, and single-select nominal categories for health-type and pension-plan items.

conceptGroups.concept: Number of alcoholic drinks consumed (quantity, numeric)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol consumption frequency (heavy episodic/binge drinking): Captures how often an individual consumed six or more standard alcoholic drinks on a single occasion during the past month. The question asked is: 'In the past month, how often did you have six or more drinks containing alcohol on one occasion?' Answer type is ordinal categorical with options: Never | Less than monthly | Monthly | Weekly | Daily or almost daily.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of mental health and substance use conditions (blood relatives) — screening and family-member follow-up
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of mental health and substance use conditions (blood relatives): A multi-part CDE capturing whether any blood relative has ever been diagnosed with specific mental health or substance use disorders, and if so, which family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, or other blood relative) are affected for each condition. The screening question asks whether any blood relative has ever received a diagnosis from a defined list of conditions (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety reaction/panic disorder, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and others); for each condition endorsed, a follow-up question identifies which specific biological family relationship(s) carry that diagnosis. Answer type: two-tier checkbox structure — Tier 1: multi-select categorical list of mental health/substance use condition categories (select all that apply); Tier 2: for each selected condition, a multi-select categorical list of biological family member relationship types (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, other blood relative). No laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified. Note: the source concept also includes a separate, distinct field capturing self-reported sleeping pill use in the past 2 weeks (ordinal frequency: No / A few days [<1 day/week] / Some days [1–2 days/week] / Most days [3–4 days/week] / Every day; with a 'Decline to answer' option), which carries a different qualifier (self, past-2-week window) and measures a different construct (own medication behavior) from the family history fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for asthma or chronic lung condition — subject, binary Yes/No
conceptGroups.idealCde: Chronic pulmonary/lung disease history and current management status: A composite domain capturing (1) lifetime diagnosis of chronic pulmonary/lung conditions (e.g., emphysema, asthma, tuberculosis, asbestosis) — binary Yes/No; (2) asthma-specific sub-elements: (a) whether the participant is currently seeing a healthcare provider for asthma — binary Yes/No, (b) age at first asthma diagnosis — ordinal categorical [Child (0–11) | Adolescent (12–17) | Adult (18–64) | Older adult (65–74) | Elderly (75+)], (c) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for asthma — binary Yes/No; and (3) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for chronic lung disease (non-asthma) — binary Yes/No. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified. The domain answers: 'Has the participant ever been diagnosed with a chronic pulmonary condition, and what is their current care and treatment status for asthma and/or chronic lung disease?' Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal radio for age-of-onset item.

conceptGroups.concept: Height measurement in cm
conceptGroups.idealCde: Waist circumference measurement: the circumference of the abdomen at the natural waist, answering 'What is the participant's waist circumference?' Expected answer type: numeric decimal value in centimeters (cm), captured via direct physical measurement. Note: this source concept clusters multiple related anthropometric fields including waist circumference in cm, waist-to-hip ratio (dimensionless decimal), measurement condition (skin contact vs. over clothing layers: 1=on skin, 2=over one layer, 3=over two layers), and height in cm — indicating the ideal CDE set covers waist circumference (cm, decimal), measurement clothing layer condition (ordinal categorical), waist-to-hip ratio (dimensionless decimal), and height (cm, text/numeric); no specific laterality, body-side, or subject-type qualifier is specified beyond the participant themselves.

conceptGroups.concept: Arterial blood pressure at rest (systolic and diastolic, two sequential readings)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Blood pressure measurement (systolic and diastolic) obtained via Omron device, captured as two sequential readings (reading 1 and reading 2). Concept: arterial blood pressure at rest. Questions: (1) What is the systolic blood pressure for reading 1/2? (2) What is the diastolic blood pressure for reading 1/2? Answer type: numeric continuous values in millimeters of mercury (mmHg), stored as paired systolic/diastolic values per reading occasion, with an associated device identifier (Omron gadget ID, text string) to link readings to the specific instrument used.

conceptGroups.concept: Type(s) of health insurance or health coverage plan currently held (select all that apply: employer/union, directly purchased, other)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current health insurance coverage status and type: A composite CDE capturing (1) whether the respondent currently has any health insurance or health coverage plan (excluding single-service plans such as dental, accident, or nursing home only), answered as a binary yes/no indicator, and (2) if covered, the type(s) of health insurance held, answered as one or more categories selected from: employer or union coverage (including COBRA, own or family member's), directly purchased coverage (including exchange/marketplace plans such as HealthCare.gov, own or family member's), government programs (e.g., Medicare, Medicaid, CHIP, VA, TRICARE), and any other health coverage plan. Answer type: binary indicator for overall coverage status (covered/not covered); multi-select categorical for coverage type(s). No units. Self- or family-reported; applies to the respondent's household coverage context.

conceptGroups.concept: Frequency of ADHD/mental health symptom interference with work or education
conceptGroups.idealCde: Contact attempt log entry capturing the date and time of a study participant contact attempt or outreach event, along with the purpose of that contact. The CDE answers: 'When was the contact attempt made, and what was the reason for contacting the participant?' Answer type: a structured record with (1) Date/time field in ISO 8601 datetime format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), and (2) Purpose of contact as a categorical coded value from a defined enumeration (e.g., questions regarding consent, report change in contact, device issue, device return, randomization completion request, in-person visit scheduling, study payment, adverse event report, or other).

conceptGroups.concept: Fasting plasma glucose concentration (numeric, mg/dL)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Fasting plasma glucose concentration measured after an overnight fast; answers 'What is the participant's fasting blood glucose level?' Expected answer type: numeric continuous value in units of mg/dL. Companion categorical classification field applies the 2003 ADA fasting criteria to categorize the result as: 0=Normal, 1=Impaired Fasting Glucose (IFG), 2=Untreated Diabetes, 3=Treated Diabetes. Dataset may include both an original (raw) numeric value and a calibrated/harmonized numeric value in mg/dL, plus a free-text comment field for laboratory notes or quality flags associated with the fasting glucose measurement.

Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal categorical age-band radio for age-at-diagnosis items. All items are self-report, first-person (subject = self).

No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified in the source fields; the concept is lifetime/ever diagnosis with no restricted time window.

conceptGroups.concept: Gender identity of subject/participant
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sex and Gender Identity — A composite concept capturing two related but distinct self-reported attributes: (1) Sex assigned at birth: the biological sex recorded at birth, answering 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' with a categorical response (Male | Female | Intersex | Other/None of these); and (2) Gender identity: the gender the participant currently identifies with, answering 'What is your current gender identity?' with a categorical response (Man/Male [including transgender men] | Woman/Female [including transgender women] | Non-binary | Genderqueer | Genderfluid | Trans man/FTM | Trans woman/MTF | Other) — ideally collected as two separate fields: one radio/select for sex assigned at birth and one multi-select checkbox for gender identity (allowing selection of a closer descriptor), both self-reported by the participant with an 'Other' or 'None of these describe me' write-in option. Answer type: categorical (enumerated codes); no units.

conceptGroups.concept: Sex of household member (numbered slots)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sex and Gender Identity — A composite concept capturing two related but distinct self-reported attributes: (1) Sex assigned at birth: the biological sex recorded at birth, answering 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' with a categorical response (Male | Female | Intersex | Other/None of these); and (2) Gender identity: the gender the participant currently identifies with, answering 'What is your current gender identity?' with a categorical response (Man/Male [including transgender men] | Woman/Female [including transgender women] | Non-binary | Genderqueer | Genderfluid | Trans man/FTM | Trans woman/MTF | Other) — ideally collected as two separate fields: one radio/select for sex assigned at birth and one multi-select checkbox for gender identity (allowing selection of a closer descriptor), both self-reported by the participant with an 'Other' or 'None of these describe me' write-in option. Answer type: categorical (enumerated codes); no units.

Diagnosis fields: binary yes/no per diabetes subtype. Distress fields: ordinal integer 0–4 per item, self-reported by the subject.

conceptGroups.concept: No participant response indicator (checkbox)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Contact attempt outcome and annotation: captures whether a participant contact attempt was successful for getting or relaying information (Yes/No radio), whether no participant response was received (checkbox), free-text comments about the contact, and the form or workflow context to which the comment is linked (dropdown: EHR Information, Mailing Information, Recruitment & Survey Management, Recruitment Survey, FAQ Survey, Screening Survey, Screening Stop Message, Pre-Consent Survey, Consent Survey, Staff Consent Attestation). Answers the question: 'Was this contact attempt successful, and what notes or contextual linkage apply?' Answer type: composite — boolean success indicator, boolean no-response flag, categorical form-link selection, and free-text notes fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Perceived availability and quality of fresh fruits and vegetables in neighborhood
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

conceptGroups.concept: Lifetime ≥100 cigarettes smoked indicator (Yes/No)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and marijuana use history — a composite set of substance use history fields capturing: (1) lifetime cigarette use threshold (whether the respondent has smoked ≥100 cigarettes in their lifetime; binary Yes/No); (2) age at smoking initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started smoking cigarettes; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (3) total duration of cigarette smoking (number of years the respondent has smoked; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (4) average daily cigarette consumption (typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, expressed as an ordinal banded count in increments up to >50 cigarettes/day, with pack equivalents noted); and (5) age at marijuana use initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started using marijuana; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years). All fields are self-reported, refer to the respondent themselves, and carry no specific time-window qualifier beyond lifetime/habitual use. Answer types: binary radio for lifetime threshold; ordinal dropdown bands (integer-anchored, self-referent) for age-at-initiation and duration fields; ordinal dropdown bands with pack-equivalent annotations for daily cigarette quantity.

conceptGroups.concept: Topics related to driving discussed with a medical professional (multi-select)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Healthcare Utilization and Access Pattern — captures the respondent's self-reported engagement with physician care and medications, access to and affordability of a regular primary care provider, frequency of allied health therapy visits (physical, speech, respiratory, audiology, occupational therapy) in the past 12 months, frequency of delaying or forgoing care due to perceived demographic dissimilarity (race/religion) between patient and provider, and frequency of successfully seeing providers perceived as demographically similar. The concept answers: 'How does this person access, use, and experience barriers to healthcare services?' Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.

conceptGroups.concept: Lifetime ever alcohol consumption (binary Yes/No)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol use history — lifetime consumption status: Whether the respondent (self) has ever consumed alcohol in their lifetime (at least one full drink, excluding small tastes or sips). The question asks: 'In your entire life, have you had at least 1 drink of any kind of alcohol (e.g., beer, wine, wine cooler, shot of liquor, or mixed drink), not counting small tastes or sips?' Answer type: binary categorical (Yes / No). Note: The source concept clusters fields spanning multiple distinct alcohol-related constructs — lifetime ever-use (binary), total years of alcohol consumption (numeric, years), drinking-and-driving behavior frequency (ordinal: Never/Rarely/Sometimes/Often/Always), and perceived neighborhood alcohol use (5-point Likert: Strongly disagree to Strongly agree) — which represent different measurement targets and should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than a single harmonized element.

conceptGroups.concept: Currently taking medication for a specific condition (hypertension, gout) — binary flag

Answer types: binary Yes/No radio responses for each current-care question (one per named condition); binary Yes/No radio for additional medication presence; free-text string for medication name(s). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; subject is the self-reporting participant.

conceptGroups.concept: Time from waking to first cigarette (numeric duration in hours and/or minutes)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Time from waking to first cigarette of the day: captures the latency between waking up and smoking the first morning cigarette as a measure of nicotine dependence urgency. Question: 'How soon after waking up do you smoke your first cigarette?' Expected answer type: numeric duration, recorded in minutes (or decomposed into hours and minutes components), representing elapsed time from waking to first cigarette. Note: the source cluster also includes a related but distinct sub-concept — depth of cigarette smoke inhalation — captured as an ordinal rating (0=Not at all, 1=Slightly, 2=Moderately, 3=Deeply); this is a separate behavioral/exposure dimension within the same smoking behavior domain and should ideally be represented as its own ordinal CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Currently using specific asthma medications (inhaled steroids or oral anti-inflammatory drugs) — subject, binary Yes/No
conceptGroups.idealCde: Chronic pulmonary/lung disease history and current management status: A composite domain capturing (1) lifetime diagnosis of chronic pulmonary/lung conditions (e.g., emphysema, asthma, tuberculosis, asbestosis) — binary Yes/No; (2) asthma-specific sub-elements: (a) whether the participant is currently seeing a healthcare provider for asthma — binary Yes/No, (b) age at first asthma diagnosis — ordinal categorical [Child (0–11) | Adolescent (12–17) | Adult (18–64) | Older adult (65–74) | Elderly (75+)], (c) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for asthma — binary Yes/No; and (3) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for chronic lung disease (non-asthma) — binary Yes/No. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified. The domain answers: 'Has the participant ever been diagnosed with a chronic pulmonary condition, and what is their current care and treatment status for asthma and/or chronic lung disease?' Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal radio for age-of-onset item.

conceptGroups.concept: Body Mass Index (BMI) category/classification
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Restless sleep frequency (past week or recent period)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sleep disturbance / insomnia symptom burden: A composite domain capturing the frequency, severity, and quality of sleep problems including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much, assessed over a defined recent time window (past 1–4 weeks). The CDE answers: 'How often have you experienced trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much, and how does it affect your sleep quality?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale (e.g., never / rarely / sometimes / often / always, or equivalent Likert-type ratings ranging from 0–3 or 1–5), with sub-components optionally capturing: (1) frequency of sleep-onset latency >30 minutes (ordinal: never to 5–7 times/week), (2) duration of sleep difficulty (decimal, in weeks/months/years), and (3) overall sleep satisfaction (ordinal: very satisfied to very dissatisfied). No single laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; fields reflect self-reported sleep experience of the respondent across multiple instruments (CES-D restless sleep item, PHQ-9 sleep item, PSQI-style items).

conceptGroups.concept: Ophthalmic condition or procedure occurrence flag (Yes/No)

The CDE answers the question: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you have, or have you ever been diagnosed with or undergone treatment for, a cardiac condition (e.g., heart attack/MI, angina, heart valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant)?' Answer type: categorical/radio; values: 1=Yes, 0=No. Note: member fields span multiple distinct cardiac conditions (MI, angina, valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant) that ideally should each be captured as separate CDEs; if a single umbrella CDE is required, it represents presence of any cardiac condition history. An optional supplementary free-text or checklist field may specify the condition type, and a date field (text/date format: YYYY-MM-DD) may capture the date of the relevant cardiac event or procedure (e.g., heart transplant date).

Each category is self-reported by the subject (self) regarding their own current diabetes management. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier applies. The question is framed as 'During the past week, how often did you feel [positive state]?' Answer type: ordinal 4-point frequency scale anchored to days in the past 7 days — 0 = All of the time (5–7 days), 1 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 2 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 3 = Rarely or none of the time (< 1 day). Time window varies across member fields (past 12 months or past month). Answer type: ordinal categorical (radio/select) for each sub-item. No laterality or body-site qualifier; subject is self-report.
