Answer type is an ordinal categorical variable with values: Child (0–11), Adolescent (12–17), Adult (18–64), Older Adult (65–74), and implicitly an oldest adult category (75+). Each condition constitutes a distinct CDE instance sharing this structure. Subject is self (the survey respondent). Note: the source concept also includes heterogeneous fields (diabetes survey date as free-text date, and waist-to-hip ratio as a calculated numeric value) that do not share this measurement construct and represent separate CDEs.

conceptGroups.concept: Neighborhood traffic volume makes walking difficult or unpleasant (agreement rating)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability barrier perception — individual item assessing the degree to which a specific environmental or safety factor (crime rate during the day, crime rate at night, or traffic volume/unpleasantness) makes walking in the respondent's neighborhood difficult or unsafe; question asks the respondent to rate their level of agreement with a stated barrier to neighborhood walking (e.g., 'The crime rate in my neighborhood makes it unsafe to go on walks [during the day / at night]' or 'There is so much traffic on the streets that it makes it difficult or unpleasant to walk in my neighborhood'); answer type is an ordinal Likert scale with 4 response options (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with an optional non-applicable response for the traffic item (e.g., 'There are no streets or roads in my neighborhood'); qualifier varies by item: daytime crime barrier, nighttime crime barrier, or traffic/street barrier to walking — these are distinct sub-items and should not be collapsed into a single field.

conceptGroups.concept: Ever stopped smoking for more than 6 months (among former daily smokers)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco smoking behavior assessment: a set of related categorical items capturing multiple dimensions of an individual's smoking history and family smoking exposure. The concept encompasses: (1) Current tobacco smoking status — question 'Do you smoke tobacco now?' with response options: Yes on most or all days / Only occasionally / No; (2) Ever stopped smoking for more than 6 months (among former regular daily smokers) — question 'In the time that you smoked, did you ever stop for more than 6 months?' with response options: Yes / No; (3) Lifetime light smoking threshold (among occasional or minimal smokers) — question 'In your lifetime, have you smoked a total of at least 100 times?' with response options: Yes / No; (4) Likelihood of resuming smoking (among former regular daily smokers who previously stopped for 6+ months) — question 'Do you think you may start smoking again?' with categorical response options indicating probability of resumption; (5) Maternal smoking exposure around time of participant's birth — question 'Did your mother smoke regularly around the time when you were born?' with response options: Yes / No. Each item is a single-select categorical variable. Items 2, 3, and 4 are conditionally collected based on responses to prior items. Item 5 pertains to the participant's mother (not the participant themselves) and reflects perinatal secondhand smoke exposure. Answer type: categorical (single-select) for each sub-item; no continuous units.

conceptGroups.concept: Weekly frequency of eating fast food meals or snacks
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

conceptGroups.concept: Vigorous exercise frequency in a typical week (self-reported)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical Activity Assessment: A multi-dimensional CDE capturing self-reported frequency and intensity of physical activity across multiple domains (light/home-based exercise such as stretching, calisthenics, or yoga; moderate activity such as carrying light loads, bicycling at regular pace, or doubles tennis; and vigorous activity such as hiking, jogging, heavy lifting, aerobics, or fast bicycling), as well as objective physical activity monitor data availability. The CDE answers: 'How frequently does the participant engage in physical activity at each intensity level, and was objective activity monitor data collected?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale for self-reported items (e.g., daily/almost daily, irregular/1–2 times per week, rarely/none; or days per week with duration thresholds such as ≥30 min on ≥3 days/week), binary yes/no for vigorous and moderate activity participation in the past 7 days, and binary yes/no for physical activity monitor data download status; units: categorical frequency categories or days per week, with intensity stratified into light/home-based, moderate, and vigorous tiers.

conceptGroups.concept: Number of activities prevented by pain or discomfort (ordinal: none/a few/some/most)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Pain/Discomfort Activity Limitation: Captures the extent to which pain or discomfort prevents participation in activities, including both a summary frequency/severity rating and identification of specific activity types affected. Primary question: 'How many activities does your pain or discomfort prevent?' with ordinal response options (none, a few, some, most); supplemented by a multi-select checklist or free-text enumeration of specific prevented activities (e.g., sitting, bending/crouching, handling objects, and other activities), allowing multiple responses. Answer type: composite — (1) ordinal categorical scale [none / a few / some / most] for overall activity limitation count, and (2) multi-select categorical list of specific activity types prevented, coded as binary indicators per activity domain.

conceptGroups.concept: Reasons contributing to decision to return to work after first retirement (multi-select Yes/No checklist)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Retirement circumstances and decision-making: A set of CDEs capturing the context and motivations surrounding an individual's retirement and, if applicable, return to work. Covers: (1) reasons contributing to the decision to retire (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (2) reasons contributing to the decision to return to work after first retirement (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (3) whether health-related retirement was due to physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both (single-select categorical: Physical health | Emotional/mental health including stress | Both); (4) whether the respondent contributed to an employer pension plan other than CPP/QPP prior to retirement (single-select categorical: Yes | No). All items are self-reported by the respondent about their own retirement experience. Answer types are binary Yes/No per factor for reason checklists, and single-select nominal categories for health-type and pension-plan items.

conceptGroups.concept: Automated (Omron device) diastolic blood pressure reading (mmHg)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Blood pressure measurement (seated position) — captures both systolic and diastolic components at a specified reading number (1st, 2nd, etc.) during a seated blood pressure assessment. Question: 'What was the [systolic/diastolic] blood pressure value recorded at the [1st/2nd] reading while the subject was seated?' Answer type: integer or numeric; units: mmHg. The CDE should be structured as a paired systolic/diastolic measurement with reading-sequence qualifier (1st reading, 2nd reading) and posture qualifier (seated), yielding four discrete values: seated systolic 1st reading, seated diastolic 1st reading, seated systolic 2nd reading, seated diastolic 2nd reading — each expressed in mmHg.

conceptGroups.concept: Difficulty noticing objects to the side while walking due to eyesight
conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical functional mobility — walking ability: A CDE capturing the degree to which an individual can perform walking and related ambulatory activities (e.g., walking, climbing stairs, carrying objects) without assistance. The question asks about the presence, severity, or independence of walking/ambulation capacity. Expected answer type: ordinal categorical scale reflecting difficulty or independence level (e.g., No difficulty / A little difficulty / Moderate difficulty / Extreme difficulty / Unable; or Yes/No for unaided walking; or a graded frequency/extent scale). Note: member fields carry heterogeneous qualifiers — some assess general walking ability (unaided ambulation, yes/no), some assess difficulty with stairs and everyday physical activities, one specifically qualifies walking difficulty as attributable to eyesight (vision-related peripheral awareness while walking), and one captures fatigue-related inability to initiate movement ('get going'); these represent distinct sub-constructs (functional mobility, vision-related mobility limitation, fatigue-related initiation) that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than collapsed into one.

conceptGroups.concept: Age at marijuana use initiation
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and marijuana use history — a composite set of substance use history fields capturing: (1) lifetime cigarette use threshold (whether the respondent has smoked ≥100 cigarettes in their lifetime; binary Yes/No); (2) age at smoking initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started smoking cigarettes; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (3) total duration of cigarette smoking (number of years the respondent has smoked; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (4) average daily cigarette consumption (typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, expressed as an ordinal banded count in increments up to >50 cigarettes/day, with pack equivalents noted); and (5) age at marijuana use initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started using marijuana; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years). All fields are self-reported, refer to the respondent themselves, and carry no specific time-window qualifier beyond lifetime/habitual use. Answer types: binary radio for lifetime threshold; ordinal dropdown bands (integer-anchored, self-referent) for age-at-initiation and duration fields; ordinal dropdown bands with pack-equivalent annotations for daily cigarette quantity.

conceptGroups.concept: Physician care engagement and medication adherence composite score
conceptGroups.idealCde: Healthcare Utilization and Access Pattern — captures the respondent's self-reported engagement with physician care and medications, access to and affordability of a regular primary care provider, frequency of allied health therapy visits (physical, speech, respiratory, audiology, occupational therapy) in the past 12 months, frequency of delaying or forgoing care due to perceived demographic dissimilarity (race/religion) between patient and provider, and frequency of successfully seeing providers perceived as demographically similar. The concept answers: 'How does this person access, use, and experience barriers to healthcare services?' Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.

Answers the questions: (1) Does the subject experience pain in the leg or buttock while walking? (Yes/No); (2) Does the pain include the calf/calves? Answer type: categorical/binary responses per sub-item, collectively forming a standardized claudication symptom questionnaire (consistent with Rose/Edinburgh Claudication Questionnaire methodology). No units; responses are nominal/ordinal coded values.

conceptGroups.idealCde: Self-reported height and weight perception — a cluster of two related self-report measures collected from the respondent about themselves: (1) Self-perceived weight status: the question 'Do you consider yourself overweight, underweight, or just about right?' answered as an ordinal categorical variable with values: Overweight | Underweight | Just about right; (2) Self-reported standing height without shoes: the question 'How tall are you without shoes on?' answered as a categorical/ordinal variable encoded in foot-and-inch bands with corresponding centimeter ranges (e.g., 1'0"–1'11", 2'0"–2'11", 3'0"–3'11", 4'0" and above), spanning the full plausible human height range, with each response band representing approximately 2.5 cm increments. Answer type: (1) nominal categorical (3-level); (2) ordinal categorical height band (feet/inches with cm equivalents).

conceptGroups.concept: Percent of total body mass that is fat (DXA)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much in past 2 weeks (PHQ-9 item)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sleep disturbance / insomnia symptom burden: A composite domain capturing the frequency, severity, and quality of sleep problems including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much, assessed over a defined recent time window (past 1–4 weeks). The CDE answers: 'How often have you experienced trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much, and how does it affect your sleep quality?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale (e.g., never / rarely / sometimes / often / always, or equivalent Likert-type ratings ranging from 0–3 or 1–5), with sub-components optionally capturing: (1) frequency of sleep-onset latency >30 minutes (ordinal: never to 5–7 times/week), (2) duration of sleep difficulty (decimal, in weeks/months/years), and (3) overall sleep satisfaction (ordinal: very satisfied to very dissatisfied). No single laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; fields reflect self-reported sleep experience of the respondent across multiple instruments (CES-D restless sleep item, PHQ-9 sleep item, PSQI-style items).

conceptGroups.concept: Frequency of consuming six or more drinks on one occasion (past year)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol Use Frequency and Quantity (AUDIT-C-style): A set of items capturing the pattern of alcohol consumption, specifically (1) how often the respondent drinks alcohol (frequency of any drinking occasion), (2) how many standard drinks they consume on a typical drinking day (typical quantity), and (3) how often they consume six or more drinks on a single occasion (heavy episodic/binge drinking frequency). Each item is answered on an ordinal frequency or quantity scale: frequency options range from 'never' through daily or almost daily (e.g., never, less than monthly/once a month or less, monthly/2–4 times a month, weekly/2–3 times a week, daily or almost daily/4+ times a week); typical quantity options are 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–9, or 10 or more standard drinks; heavy-occasion frequency options are never (in the past year/month), less than monthly, monthly, weekly, or daily or almost daily. Time window varies across member fields (past 12 months or past month). Answer type: ordinal categorical (radio/select) for each sub-item. No laterality or body-site qualifier; subject is self-report.

Questions addressed: (1) Whether sleep has changed (Yes/No); (2) If changed, the specific type of change — sleeping too much (hypersomnia) or trouble falling asleep (insomnia onset) (each Yes/No); (3) Whether difficulty sleeping is currently present (Yes/No); (4) The extent to which difficulty sleeping limits usual activities (not limiting / causing avoidance, reduction, or spreading out of usual activities); (5) Duration of difficulty sleeping (less than 2 weeks / 2–4 weeks / 4–12 weeks / more than 12 weeks). Answer types: categorical single-select for each sub-component; conditionally administered (items 2–5 contingent on affirmative responses to prior items). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier specified; context is self-reported health and wellbeing.

notComputed.reason: No stage stamps WHICH rule changed a given variable. The preparation report is per-rule counts plus a per-variable before/after diff; the join between them is inferred, not recorded. Per-field rule provenance is deferred by SPEC, so this is a product-level gap rather than a switch someone can turn on.

The M7 concept-match gate is an opt-in LLM stage and this run did not enable it, so no run paid for it. It IS wired: set the run's concept_gate option and the signal arrives as a real value. Absent here means not asked, not 'no mismatch found'.

Re-adjudication is caller-invoked with an explicit list of group ids and nothing on this run invoked it, so no record is a re-split child. The pipeline never re-splits an over-merged group on its own — the coherence flag is a suggestion for a human.

cde.id: Family health problems psychological history type

records.idealCde: Family history of mental health and substance use conditions (blood relatives): A multi-part CDE capturing whether any blood relative has ever been diagnosed with specific mental health or substance use disorders, and if so, which family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, or other blood relative) are affected for each condition. The screening question asks whether any blood relative has ever received a diagnosis from a defined list of conditions (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety reaction/panic disorder, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and others); for each condition endorsed, a follow-up question identifies which specific biological family relationship(s) carry that diagnosis. Answer type: two-tier checkbox structure — Tier 1: multi-select categorical list of mental health/substance use condition categories (select all that apply); Tier 2: for each selected condition, a multi-select categorical list of biological family member relationship types (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, other blood relative). No laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified. Note: the source concept also includes a separate, distinct field capturing self-reported sleeping pill use in the past 2 weeks (ordinal frequency: No / A few days [<1 day/week] / Some days [1–2 days/week] / Most days [3–4 days/week] / Every day; with a 'Decline to answer' option), which carries a different qualifier (self, past-2-week window) and measures a different construct (own medication behavior) from the family history fields.

records.concept: Physician care engagement and medication adherence composite score
records.idealCde: Healthcare Utilization and Access Pattern — captures the respondent's self-reported engagement with physician care and medications, access to and affordability of a regular primary care provider, frequency of allied health therapy visits (physical, speech, respiratory, audiology, occupational therapy) in the past 12 months, frequency of delaying or forgoing care due to perceived demographic dissimilarity (race/religion) between patient and provider, and frequency of successfully seeing providers perceived as demographically similar. The concept answers: 'How does this person access, use, and experience barriers to healthcare services?' Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.

gencde.title: Physician Care Engagement and Medication Adherence Composite Score
gencde.definition: A self-reported composite measure categorizing a respondent's level of engagement with physician care (visit frequency with a regular doctor) and medication adherence (regularity of taking prescribed medicines) into a single ordinal score.

gencde.rationale: Source field AI-READI:dmlmd uses a numeric scoring scheme (0, 5, 10) that encodes both visit frequency and medication adherence as a single ordinal composite; codes are preserved as-is from the source to maintain scoring fidelity. Code 777 ('Prefer not to say') is a response-quality sentinel retained in the permissible-value set per source observation but should be treated as missing/non-informative in analytic contexts. Near-miss CDEs (primary care and other physician follow-up indicators) address only visit frequency without the medication adherence dimension, confirming this is a distinct composite construct. No additional answer concepts were introduced beyond those observed in the source field.

records.concept: Topics related to driving discussed with a medical professional (multi-select)
records.idealCde: Healthcare Utilization and Access Pattern — captures the respondent's self-reported engagement with physician care and medications, access to and affordability of a regular primary care provider, frequency of allied health therapy visits (physical, speech, respiratory, audiology, occupational therapy) in the past 12 months, frequency of delaying or forgoing care due to perceived demographic dissimilarity (race/religion) between patient and provider, and frequency of successfully seeing providers perceived as demographically similar. The concept answers: 'How does this person access, use, and experience barriers to healthcare services?' Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.

gencde.rationale: The three CLSA source fields (TRA_MEDTPC_HRB_MCQ, TRA_MEDTPC_MED_MCQ, TRA_MEDTPC_THR_MCQ) are parallel multi-select items sharing the same stem question but each capturing a distinct driving-related topic category: health/medical conditions (HRB), medications (MED), and driving therapy/restriction recommendations (THR). These are reconciled into three canonical permissible values. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a broader healthcare utilization construct that does not align well with this narrower driving-counseling concept; the near-miss CDEs (current driving status, drowsy driving, night driving difficulty) are related but distinct. Confidence is moderate because the source fields are text-type multi-select checkboxes and the exact permissible value labels are inferred from the variable name suffixes (HRB, MED, THR) rather than from an explicit codebook; label wording should be verified against the CLSA data dictionary.

Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.

gencde.title: Ever Seen General Practitioner for Nerves, Anxiety, Tension, or Depression
gencde.definition: A binary self-report of whether the respondent has ever consulted a general practitioner (GP) specifically for nerves, anxiety, tension, or depression at any point in their lifetime.
gencde.questionText: Have you ever seen a general practitioner (GP) for nerves, anxiety, tension, or depression?
aliases: Primary care visit for anxiety or depression

Mental health help-seeking from primary care provider
GP contact for common mental disorder

relatedCdes: Have you ever seen a doctor about this pain [PhenX]
Have you been bothered by nervousness or your nerves during the past month [NHANES]
Doctor or health care professional ever told you that you have diabetes
gencde.rationale: Sourced from UK Biobank (UKBB) ACE touchscreen item. Original response set included 'Do not know' and 'Prefer not to answer' sentinels, which are excluded per harmonization instructions retaining only substantive answer concepts (Yes/No). The concept is lifetime (ever) and restricted to GP/primary care contact, distinguishing it from specialist mental health service use. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX pain doctor visit; NHANES nervousness symptom frequency; diabetes diagnosis) share structural similarity but differ in clinical domain or time window. Aliases drawn from MeSH, SNOMED CT, and ICD-10 primary care mental health terminology.

gencde.rationale: Source field (AoU smoking_numberofyearsnumber) is typed as text but captures a numeric year count; the GenCDE standardizes this as numeric (integer or decimal) in UCUM years ('a'). Maximum of 120 reflects a biologically plausible upper bound aligned with maximum human lifespan. Near-miss CDEs (Cough phlegm lasting time, Patient Age Year Count, Sport high school primary played count) share a 'count in years' structure but measure distinct concepts and were used only to inform alias terminology. No permissible-value enumeration is appropriate for a continuous numeric measure.

gencde.title: Vaping / E-Cigarette Use History (Age Started, Total Years Used, Weekly Frequency)
gencde.definition: A composite set of fields capturing the history of vaping or e-cigarette use, including the age at which the respondent first started vaping or using e-cigarettes (in whole years, with a capped category for >60 years), the total number of years the respondent has vaped or used e-cigarettes (in whole years, with a capped category for >20 years), and the typical number of days per week the respondent uses a vaping device or e-cigarette.
gencde.questionText: At what age did you start vaping or using e-cigarettes? How many total years have you vaped or used e-cigarettes? When you vaped or used e-cigarettes, approximately how many days in a typical week would you use it?
aliases: electronic nicotine delivery system use history
How many years have you vaped?
relatedCdes: How many years have you vaped?
How old were you when you started smoking cigars regularly [PhenX]
For how many years did you (have you) smoke(d) up to now?
gencde.rationale: This GenCDE is a composite covering three sub-fields from AI-READI (suvpstage, suvptoage, suvpdosfr). The permissible-value set is intentionally minimal because the source fields are dropdown numerics whose full integer ranges were not enumerated in the harmonized export; only the sentinel/capped values (>60 years old, >20 years, Prefer not to say) were explicitly observed. For a production CDE, each sub-field should ideally be split into three separate CDEs (age started [integer 0–98], total years [integer 0–98], days/week [integer 1–7]) with the capped and prefer-not-to-say codes as additional permissible values. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX cigar-smoking age, years smoked) were used only to inform aliases. Confidence is moderate because the composite structure and incomplete value enumeration reduce precision.

gencde.title: Total Years Lived With a Cigarette Smoker (Secondhand Smoke Exposure Duration)
gencde.definition: The total cumulative number of years a person has lived in the same household or dwelling with an active cigarette smoker, serving as a measure of chronic secondhand tobacco smoke exposure.
gencde.questionText: In total, how many years have you lived with a cigarette smoker?
relatedCdes: Tobacco cigarette use stopped age value
Tobacco smoke pack-year value
Tobacco cigarette use started age value
gencde.rationale: Sourced from MESA variable cgr25 (TOTAL YEARS LIVED WITH CIGARETTE SMOKER), a single numeric field capturing cumulative household secondhand smoke exposure in whole years. The ideal CDE anchor describes a broader composite tobacco/marijuana use history instrument; this GenCDE isolates only the secondhand smoke exposure duration sub-element. Near-miss CDEs (pack-years, smoking start/stop age) are first-person active-smoking measures and are retained only as contextual relations. Maximum value set to 99 years as a practical biological ceiling; no explicit cap was documented in the source field. Units expressed in UCUM 'a' (annum/years).

records.idealCde: Tobacco and marijuana use history — a composite set of substance use history fields capturing: (1) lifetime cigarette use threshold (whether the respondent has smoked ≥100 cigarettes in their lifetime; binary Yes/No); (2) age at smoking initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started smoking cigarettes; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (3) total duration of cigarette smoking (number of years the respondent has smoked; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (4) average daily cigarette consumption (typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, expressed as an ordinal banded count in increments up to >50 cigarettes/day, with pack equivalents noted); and (5) age at marijuana use initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started using marijuana; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years). All fields are self-reported, refer to the respondent themselves, and carry no specific time-window qualifier beyond lifetime/habitual use. Answer types: binary radio for lifetime threshold; ordinal dropdown bands (integer-anchored, self-referent) for age-at-initiation and duration fields; ordinal dropdown bands with pack-equivalent annotations for daily cigarette quantity.

gencde.rationale: Two source fields from AoU were harmonized into a single CDE covering both the ever-use binary item and the current-frequency ordinal item, as they jointly define the concept. Permissible values 1–2 apply to the ever-use question; values 3–5 apply to the current-frequency follow-up question (asked only of ever-users). Missing-data sentinels (Don't know, Prefer not to answer) were excluded per instructions. Near-miss PhenX CDEs on cigar inhalation and regular cigar use were retained as aliases only, as they differ in scope or phrasing. Confidence is slightly reduced because combining two logically sequential items into one CDE is a structural compromise; implementers may prefer to split into two separate CDEs.

gencde.rationale: Harmonized from CLSA (SMK_OTREG_TRM, binary yes/no with codes 1/2) and MESA (othtob1, binary yes/no with codes 1/0). Canonical coding adopts 1=Yes, 0=No to align with the MESA convention and standard binary CDE practice; CLSA code 2=No is remapped to 0. The CLSA sub-items (SMK_TYPEOT_CG_TRM=cigars, SMK_TYPEOT_CH_TRM=chewing tobacco, SMK_TYPEOT_PI_TRM=pipe, SMK_TYPEOT_PT_TRM=smokeless/snuff, SMK_TYPEOT_SM_TRM=smokeless other) are product-specific indicators sharing the same binary value domain and the same ≥6-month regular-use qualifier; they are captured here as a single umbrella CDE with the understanding that product-type sub-elements may be represented as companion CDEs. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX pipe use, tobacco exposure duration) were consulted for alias terminology only and do not match the lifetime any-other-tobacco framing.

gencde.rationale: Two source fields were harmonized: chew1c (never/former/current) and chwcur1 (used in last 30 days, yes/no). Because chwcur1 sub-classifies 'current' users by 30-day recency, the canonical value set merges both dimensions into four mutually exclusive categories: Never (chew1c=0), Former (chew1c=1), Current–Used in Last 30 Days (chew1c=2 AND chwcur1=1), and Current–Not Used in Last 30 Days (chew1c=2 AND chwcur1=0). No answer concepts beyond those observed in the source fields were introduced. The near-miss CDEs (Tobacco product used type; Tobacco current use indicator; Tobacco use duration) informed alias selection only. Confidence is modestly reduced because the two-field merge requires a derivation rule not directly encoded in either source field alone.

records.concept: Weekly frequency of eating fast food meals or snacks
records.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

gencde.rationale: The two source fields measure overlapping but not identical constructs: AI-READI captures a composite lean protein category (beans, chicken, fish) on a 3-level weekly frequency scale, while UKBB captures beans/pulses/lentils only with a serving-count scale (quarter, half, 1, 2, 3+). Reconciliation maps UKBB 'quarter' and 'half' to a sub-1-serving sub-weekly code (code 1), UKBB '1'–'2' to code 2, and UKBB '3+' to code 3, preserving the AI-READI 'Less than 1 time' as code 0 for zero-frequency reporters and 'Prefer not to say' as code 777. The UKBB field is narrower (pulses/lentils only, conditioned on vegetable consumption) and uses serving counts rather than weekly episodes, so harmonization introduces some conceptual imprecision. The near-miss CDEs (cooked dried beans, margarine/butter, fried eggs) were used only to confirm non-overlap and inform aliases. Confidence is moderate due to the partial construct mismatch between the two source instruments.

gencde.title: Frequency or Amount of Butter, Margarine, or Meat Fat Used on Vegetables, Bread, or Potatoes
gencde.definition: An ordinal or categorical assessment of how often or how much butter, margarine, or meat fat is used to season or top vegetables, potatoes, bread, or corn, capturing both frequency-based and quantity-based response formats observed across dietary survey instruments.
gencde.questionText: How much or how often do you use butter, margarine, or meat fat on vegetables, bread, potatoes, or corn?
aliases: Margarine or butter on vegetables including potatoes frequency
Margarine or butter on bread rolls pancakes frequency
Margarine butter or oil on rice or pasta frequency
Butter margarine use on cooked vegetables
Cooking fat seasoning on vegetables and bread
relatedCdes: About how often did you eat Margarine or butter on vegetables, including potatoes?
About how often did you eat Margarine or butter on bread, rolls, pancakes?
About how often did you eat Margarine, butter, or oil on rice or pasta?
gencde.rationale: Source fields use heterogeneous response formats: AI-READI uses an amount scale (Very little / Some / A lot), CLSA uses a frequency scale (Rarely-Never / Per Day / Per Week / Per Month / Per Year) with a companion numeric field (NUT_BTTR_NB_COM) for the count, and MESA uses a binary yes/no indicator for butter as a cooking fat. Because these formats are not directly reconcilable into a single ordinal scale without loss of information, the canonical permissible-value set preserves the distinct conceptual anchors from each source (amount, frequency, binary) as labeled codes. Implementers should note that the CLSA numeric companion field (NUT_BTTR_NB_COM) carries the quantity associated with the frequency unit and should be stored as a paired numeric variable. The 'Per Year' CLSA option is collapsed into 'Never/Rarely/Very little' (code 0) as it is functionally equivalent to rare use. The ideal CDE anchor provided was a multi-item diet composite and was used only for contextual orientation, not for value derivation. Confidence is moderate due to the heterogeneity of response formats across source instruments.

relatedCdes: About how often did you drink Orange juice or grapefruit juice?
How often is the orange juice you drink calcium fortified?
About how often did you eat Fruit (not juices)?
gencde.rationale: Two source fields were harmonized: AI-READI diet9 uses a daily-servings frame (<1, 1–2, 3+) while MESA addqcalciumfort5 uses a general frequency frame (never/seldom, sometimes, often/always) specific to calcium-fortified juice. The canonical permissible values map these two scales ordinally (code 0 = none/rare, code 1 = moderate, code 2 = high/frequent) since the underlying construct—low vs. moderate vs. high fruit juice consumption—is equivalent across both instruments. The 'Prefer not to say' sentinel from AI-READI is retained as code 999. Confidence is moderate because the two source fields differ in beverage specificity (all fruit juice vs. calcium-fortified juice only) and temporal framing (daily servings vs. general frequency), introducing conceptual heterogeneity. Near-miss CDEs for orange/grapefruit juice frequency and calcium-fortified juice frequency were used only to inform aliases.

records.concept: Servings of specific foods consumed (24-hour dietary recall: baked beans, potatoes, coleslaw, crumble, dried fruit cereal, fried potatoes)
records.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE consolidates six distinct 24-hour dietary recall items from the UK Biobank (Oxford WebQ) that share a common ordinal serving-count response framework. The permissible-value set is reconciled from all observed answer concepts across the six source fields: quarter, half, 1, 2, 3, 3+, 4+, Yes, and Varied. Fractional servings (quarter, half) appear only in vegetable-type items; 4+ appears only for crumble; Yes/Varied appear only for the dried fruit cereal binary item. Because the source fields are item-specific (not a single composite), this CDE is best implemented as a repeating or item-keyed structure. The ideal CDE anchor describes a different construct (weekly frequency composite diet quality score) and was used only to confirm non-match. Near-miss CDEs informed aliases for cooked dried beans and potato-related items. Confidence is moderate (0.62) because the concept spans heterogeneous response scales across items that would ideally be represented as separate CDEs per food, but are grouped here per the harmonization instruction.

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE aggregates heterogeneous source fields spanning three intensity domains (light/home-based: AI-READI:dmlhex; moderate: AoU:ipaq_3; vigorous: AoU:ipaq_1; walking: AoU:ipaq_5) plus objective monitor availability (AI-READI:dvamwendwnd). Frequency response options were reconciled from the AI-READI ordinal scale and AoU Yes/No IPAQ items into a single canonical set; 'Unsure' was retained from the observed answer concepts list. MESA numeric MET-min/wk fields (exercm1c, exercm5c) and ECG/cardiac fields (ecgnum5, major7a5) were excluded from the permissible-value set as they represent continuous or unrelated constructs not expressible in this categorical schema — implementers should treat those as companion numeric elements. CLSA free-text fields (PA2_EXER_MCQ, PA2_SIT_MCQ) map to frequency categories 1–3. The 7-day recall window from IPAQ is the dominant reference period. Confidence is moderate because the source fields span genuinely distinct sub-concepts (intensity levels, monitor availability) that ideally would be separate CDEs, but the harmonization brief treats them as one concept.

gencde.title: Calculated Hispanic Ethnicity Score for Demographics Screening Logic
gencde.definition: A calculated numeric score derived from self-reported demographic data to quantify the degree or likelihood of Hispanic/Latino ethnic identity, used as a screening logic variable in demographic classification algorithms.
gencde.questionText: What is the calculated Hispanic ethnicity score derived from demographic screening responses?
relatedCdes: Hispanic origin

gencde.rationale: This CDE represents a calculated/derived variable (type: calc) from the AI-READI cohort used in demographics screening logic, not a directly self-reported item. The exact scoring algorithm and scale maximum are not specified in the source field metadata; minimum is assumed 0 (no Hispanic indicators). Near-miss CDEs (Hispanic origin, Other Hispanic/Latino specification, child Hispanic/Latino origin) were used only to inform aliases. Because the source field is a computed intermediate variable rather than a primary self-report item, confidence is moderate; the ideal CDE anchor describes a richer self-report construct, but the source field is strictly a derived numeric score. Units use UCUM placeholder '{score}' for dimensionless calculated scores. Maximum value should be updated once the scoring algorithm range is confirmed.

gencde.rationale: Both source fields (AI-READI racetrib and AoU aian_tribe) are free-text prompts capturing self-reported tribal name, enrollment, affiliation, or descent for American Indian, Alaska Native, and broader Indigenous populations. No permissible values are defined because the domain is open-ended by design; controlled vocabulary (e.g., BIA-recognized tribe list, NCAI tribal directory) may be applied post-collection for harmonization. The near-miss CDEs address race/ethnicity categorically and do not capture this granular tribal-identity narrative. The ideal anchor CDE addresses Hispanic/Latino ancestry in a related but distinct domain; tribal affiliation is retained as a separate, standalone element per standard NIH race/ethnicity data collection guidance (2024 OMB standards).

gencde.title: Age-, Gender-, and Race-Adjusted Coronary Artery Calcium Score Quantile and Non-Zero Calcium Probability (McClelland 2006)
gencde.definition: Clinically computed statistics derived from a participant's raw coronary artery calcium (CAC) score: (1) the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted quantile of the CAC score among individuals with CAC > 0 (expressed as a probability between 0 and 1, per McClelland et al., Circulation 2006), and (2) the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted probability that a participant's calcium score is non-zero, based on the same reference population and methodology.
gencde.questionText: What is the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted quantile of the participant's CAC score among those with CAC > 0, and what is the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted probability that the participant has a non-zero CAC score, as derived from McClelland et al. (Circulation 2006)?
relatedCdes: NIH Toolbox Cognitive ? Cognition crystallized composite age adjusted scale score
NIH Toolbox Cognitive ? Cognition total composition age adjusted scale score
NIH Toolbox Cognitive ? Cognition fluid composite age adjusted scale score
gencde.rationale: Two closely related numeric statistics from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) are captured here: CACQ1C (the age/gender/race-adjusted quantile of the CAC score, restricted to participants with CAC > 0, range 0–1) and PRCACGT01C (the age/gender/race-adjusted probability of having a non-zero CAC score, range 0–1). Both are continuous probabilities on [0,1] per the McClelland et al. 2006 Circulation reference equations. They are paired clinical computed statistics rather than raw measurements, and no existing NIH CDE covers this cardiovascular imaging-derived computed statistic. The near-miss CDEs relate to age-adjusted cognitive composite scores (NIH Toolbox), which share the 'age-adjusted scale score' structural pattern but are entirely different in domain. Confidence is slightly reduced because these two sub-measures (quantile vs. probability) are conceptually distinct and could alternatively be split into two separate CDEs; they are combined here because they share the same reference methodology, population, and value domain.

records.concept: Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
records.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

records.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

gencde.title: DXA Assumed Percent of Lean Body Mass That Is Water
gencde.definition: The assumed percentage of lean body mass composed of water, as derived from dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) body composition analysis, used as a fixed physiological constant or region-specific estimate in hydration and body composition calculations.
gencde.questionText: What is the assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water, as estimated from DXA body composition analysis?
relatedCdes: Dual X-ray absorptiometry whole body total lean value
Body mass index value
Body mass index category
gencde.rationale: All three source fields (DXA_AGC_WATER_LBM_COM, DXA_OI_WATER_LBM_COM, DXA_WBC_WATER_LBM_COM) from the CLSA cohort are decimal-typed and share an identical definition, differing only by anatomical region (whole body composition, osteoporosis index region, and age-gender-corrected region). The GenCDE abstracts across these regional variants into a single numeric element with percent units. The value is typically a physiological constant near 73% in standard DXA software but is retained as a continuous numeric field to accommodate software- or region-specific variation. Near-miss CDEs (DXA whole body lean value, BMI value, BMI category) were used only to inform alias vocabulary and confirm non-overlap. No categorical permissible values are warranted given the continuous decimal source type.

gencde.rationale: Sourced exclusively from MESA variable wtmodp5. The concept is a quality-control/data-integrity flag indicating whether the standard operating procedure for weight measurement was altered (e.g., participant unable to remove shoes, used wheelchair scale). Near-miss CDEs (Body weight Measured; Body weight; Body weight Stated) capture the weight value itself, not the protocol modification status. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes body composition metrics, which is a related but distinct concept; this CDE specifically flags procedural deviation during weight collection. Binary coding follows the source field convention (0=No, 1=Yes).

records.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

gencde.title: Lifetime History of Depressed Mood Lasting at Least One Week
gencde.definition: Self-reported indicator of whether an individual has ever experienced a period of feeling depressed or down lasting at least one continuous week at any point in their lifetime, serving as the gateway criterion for further characterization of depressive episode frequency, duration, and derived major depression diagnoses.
gencde.questionText: Looking back over your life, have you ever had a time when you were feeling depressed or down for at least a whole week?
aliases: Ever depressed for a whole week
sourceVariables: UKBB:Ever depressed for a whole week
UKBB:Single episode of probable major depression
relatedCdes: Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless in last 2 weeks [Reported.PHQ]
Patient Health Questionnaire Depression (PHQ) - Depressed score
Center for Epidemiologic Studies-Depression Scale (CES-D) - depressed indicator
gencde.rationale: The concept spans five UKBB fields: a binary gateway question (F4598), two numeric follow-up fields (longest episode duration in weeks, F4609; number of episodes, F4620), and two derived categorical flags (single-episode probable major depression; recurrent moderate probable major depression). Because the IDEAL CDE anchor is a CES-D past-week symptom item and the near-miss CDEs are PHQ/CES-D current-symptom measures, this GenCDE is intentionally scoped to the lifetime binary gateway construct — the only answer concepts observed across all harmonized source fields are Yes and No. The numeric sub-fields (duration, episode count) and derived diagnosis flags are treated as companion elements rather than merged here, to preserve semantic precision. Missing-data sentinels (-1 Do not know, -3 Prefer not to answer) are excluded from the permissible-value set per instructions. Confidence is moderate (0.72) because the concept conflates a self-report screen with algorithmically derived clinical diagnoses, and no single authoritative NIH CDE or ontology term fully captures this composite lifetime construct.

records.concept: Seated systolic blood pressure reading (mmHg), by reading sequence (1st/2nd/3rd)
records.idealCde: Blood pressure measurement (seated position) — captures both systolic and diastolic components at a specified reading number (1st, 2nd, etc.) during a seated blood pressure assessment. Question: 'What was the [systolic/diastolic] blood pressure value recorded at the [1st/2nd] reading while the subject was seated?' Answer type: integer or numeric; units: mmHg. The CDE should be structured as a paired systolic/diastolic measurement with reading-sequence qualifier (1st reading, 2nd reading) and posture qualifier (seated), yielding four discrete values: seated systolic 1st reading, seated diastolic 1st reading, seated systolic 2nd reading, seated diastolic 2nd reading — each expressed in mmHg.

aliases: Mean arterial pressure measurement method type

uncoveredLabels: Question not asked due to previous answers
gencde.rationale: Source field is UKBB 'Method of measuring blood pressure' (categorical single). Two sentinel/administrative codes from the source (-1=Question not asked due to previous answers) were collapsed into a single 'Not performed' category (code 4) as both represent absence of a valid measurement rather than a substantive answer concept; the -1 sentinel was dropped per schema instructions to exclude missing-data sentinels. 'Manual sphygmometer' label was standardised to 'Manual sphygmomanometer' (correct clinical spelling) while preserving the original concept. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a paired systolic/diastolic seated BP measurement, which is a related but distinct concept; this CDE captures only the collection-method qualifier. Near-miss CDEs (mean arterial pressure measurement method type; blood pressure measurement; systolic BP augmentation measurement) were used only to inform aliases.

gencde.title: Care Recipient Sex
gencde.definition: The biological sex of the primary care recipient — the person to whom the caregiver subject provided the most assistance.
gencde.questionText: Is the person to whom you provided the most assistance male or female?
aliases: gender of person receiving most assistance
relatedCdes: Has this person done any of the following for you or helped you out [PhenX]
When considering all of the support resources you have been exposed to, is there one that stands out as being the most helpful to you so far?
Section generator PhenX
gencde.rationale: Both CLSA source fields (CAG_GNDR_COM and CAG_GNDR_TRM) use identical wording and identical two-value response sets (1=Male, 2=Female), indicating a straightforward binary sex variable as reported by the caregiver about their primary care recipient. The question wording uses 'male or female,' reflecting biological sex rather than gender identity; only two answer concepts were observed across all source fields, so no additional permissible values (e.g., Intersex, Non-binary) are introduced. The near-miss CDEs relate to caregiver support resources and social support inventories, not to care recipient demographics, and were used only to confirm non-overlap. Confidence is slightly reduced from maximum because the source instrument conflates 'sex' and 'gender' in its question wording, and the binary framing may not capture all biological sex categories.

gencde.rationale: Source field (AoU employment_employmentworkaddress) presents this as a radio-type input with two options: free-text address entry and 'Prefer not to answer'. The canonical permissible-value set collapses to a free-text entry field (data_type: text) because the only substantive answer concept observed is an open address entry; 'Prefer not to answer' is a missing-data sentinel excluded per instructions. The near-miss CDEs (Participant Street Address, Full Residential Address) are residential rather than occupational, confirming this is a distinct work-site concept. Confidence is moderate (0.72) because only one source cohort contributed data and the concept is a free-text address rather than a structured categorical element, limiting harmonization validation.

gencde.rationale: Source field MESA:empstat5 encodes employment status as a binary yes/no indicator at Exam 5, collapsing the richer multi-select categorical structure described in the ideal CDE (which includes employed, self-employed, out of work, homemaker, student, retired, unable to work) into a single employed/not-employed dichotomy. The canonical permissible-value set is therefore restricted to the two answer concepts actually observed (YES=1, NO=0). Near-miss CDEs ('Employment Status - Specify', 'Employment Specify Other Status', 'Parent's Employment Specify Other Status') were used only to inform aliases and confirm non-match. Confidence is moderate because the binary collapse loses granularity relative to standard employment-status CDEs, and the exam-visit qualifier (Exam 5) is cohort-specific to MESA.

gencde.rationale: Source field AI-READI:icf_consent is a radio-button item capturing affirmative agreement after full form review. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a date/time of consent completion, but the sole source field measures the agreement decision itself (binary yes/no), not a timestamp; the GenCDE therefore reflects the actual observed data type. Near-miss CDEs (future contact consent, smoking history, Rosenberg self-esteem) were used only to confirm distinctness and contributed no permissible values. If a consent-date companion field exists, it should be captured in a separate date-type CDE. Qualifier: instrument = Informed Consent Form (ICF); context = baseline enrollment.

aliases: number of food frequency questionnaires completed
relatedCdes: Overall diet health scale
Food Frequency Questionnaire - (FFQ)-special diet indicator
Mitochondrial disease past restrict diet indicator
gencde.rationale: Sourced from UK Biobank field 'Number of diet questionnaires completed' (integer type). The concept counts completed dietary assessment instruments per participant; no upper bound is imposed as it is study-design-dependent. The ideal CDE anchor describes a date/time of completion, which is a related but distinct concept (instrument completion timestamp vs. instrument completion count); the count concept is retained here as the true harmonized target. Near-miss CDEs (diet health scale, FFQ special diet indicator, mitochondrial diet restriction) are categorically distinct and were used only to inform alias terminology. UCUM unit '{questionnaires}' denotes a dimensionless count of discrete instruments.

gencde.rationale: This is a hybrid numeric/categorical element: the primary response is an integer age in years (minimum 3, maximum = participant's current age at assessment), with a single categorical override for participants who report never having had sexual intercourse. Sentinel codes for 'Do not know' and 'Prefer not to answer' observed in the UKBB source field are treated as missing-data sentinels and excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. A confirmation prompt is recommended when the reported value is less than 12. The upper bound is left null because it is participant-age-dependent. Near-miss CDEs (hearing difficulty onset age, menarche age, kidney failure diagnosis age) share the 'age at first event' structure and inform the question phrasing pattern but represent distinct concepts.

gencde.title: Ever Had Same-Sex Sexual Intercourse (Lifetime)
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether the participant has ever engaged in sexual intercourse (defined as vaginal, oral, or anal intercourse) with a person of the same sex at any point in their lifetime, as self-reported by the participant.
gencde.questionText: Have you ever had sexual intercourse with someone of the same sex?
aliases: ever had sex with same-sex partner
relatedCdes: How many times in the last year have you been paid for having sexual relations with someone [Denver Youth Survey]
How many times in the last year have you had or tried to have sexual relations with someone against their will (other than events you just mentioned)?
Over the past 4 weeks when you attempted sexual intercourse, how often were you able to penetrate - enter your partner [PhenX]
gencde.rationale: The source fields span two distinct but related sexual history constructs from UK Biobank (UKBB F2159 and F2149). The IDEAL CDE anchor describes age at first intercourse (numeric), but the observed answer concepts across all source fields are strictly binary (Yes/No), corresponding to the same-sex intercourse item (F2159). The lifetime number of sexual partners field (F2149) is integer-valued but its only observed answer concepts submitted for reconciliation are Yes and No; no numeric partner-count values were included in the ANSWER CONCEPTS list, so no numeric permissible values are authored here. Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer) are excluded per instructions. This element should only be administered to participants who have previously confirmed ever having had sexual intercourse. Near-miss CDEs relate to paid sex frequency, non-consensual sex, and erectile penetration ability — all distinct constructs retained only for relational context.

gencde.rationale: This element functions as a gating/consent prompt preceding sexual history items (e.g., age at first intercourse). It is not a clinical measure of sexual behavior itself but a participant-autonomy control item. The two permissible values (Continue, Skip this section) are drawn exclusively from the UKBB ACE touchscreen source field. Near-miss CDEs were confirmed non-matches: they address interpersonal care, childhood abuse disclosure, and social participation — distinct constructs. Confidence is slightly reduced because this is a survey-administration artifact rather than a substantive clinical variable, and its generalizability across cohorts beyond UKBB is uncertain.

gencde.rationale: Source is the UK Biobank (UKBB) touchscreen questionnaire hierarchical branching item on ethnic background. Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer) were excluded from the permissible-value set per instructions. If you have lived there for less than one year select Less than a year.
If you are unsure, please provide an estimate or select Do not know.
If you have lived at your current address at different times, add up
the total number of years you lived there. For instance if you lived
at your current address for 3 years, moved overseas for one year and
returned to your current address for another 5 years, then you would
enter 8 years.

relatedCdes: In your day-to-day life, how often have any of the following things happened to you? You have received poorer service than other people at restaurants or stores

gencde.rationale: This is a multi-select categorical element derived from two UKBB touchscreen fields (main assessment and pilot). Codes 1–8 represent distinct supplement types observed across both source fields; synonymous entries (e.g., Iron appearing in both fields with different codes) were merged into a single canonical code. The 'Prefer not to answer' sentinel (-3) was excluded from the permissible-value set per CDE best practice for missing-data handling. The 'None of the above' option (-7) is retained as a substantive response. The ideal CDE anchor provided (age at first sexual intercourse) is unrelated to this concept and was disregarded; the GenCDE is authored solely from the source fields and observed answer concepts.

gencde.rationale: Source is the UK Biobank pilot touchscreen questionnaire (field on progestogen-only oral contraceptive type). Permissible values correspond to the six named UK-marketed mini-pill brands observed in the source field plus 'None of the above'; missing-data sentinels (-1 mapped to 'None of the above' as a substantive response, -3 'Prefer not to answer' omitted per schema instructions to drop missing-data sentinels). Brands map to active ingredients: Microval/Norgeston = levonorgestrel; Micronor/Noriday = norethisterone; Femulen = ethynodiol diacetate; Cerazette = desogestrel. The IDEAL CDE anchor provided (age at first sexual intercourse) is unrelated to this concept and was disregarded; it appears to be an erroneous anchor. Confidence slightly reduced due to single-cohort sourcing and pilot-study provenance.

gencde.definition: This is a null/degenerate CDE record indicating that the source fields submitted for harmonization do not share a common measurable concept and cannot be meaningfully unified into a single data element; the fields span study visit stage, diabetes type classification, non-cancer illness timing, and operation timing.

gencde.rationale: The source fields are semantically unrelated: AI-READI eos_dsvst captures study visit stage; CLSA DIA_TYPE_COM captures diabetes type; UKBB fields capture non-cancer illness timing and operation timing. The ideal CDE anchor (cancer diagnosis history) is also unrelated to all five source fields. No coherent single CDE can be authored. The permissible values listed are the raw observed answer concepts pooled verbatim from the source fields as required by the schema, but they belong to entirely different constructs. Confidence is near zero. Recommend returning these fields to the harmonization team for re-clustering before CDE authoring.

records.concept: Exertional leg/buttock pain claudication screening (Rose/Edinburgh Questionnaire items)

cde.id: Do your legs hurt when you walk [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication screening): a structured assessment capturing the presence, characteristics, and behavior of leg or buttock pain during walking. Answers the questions: (1) Does the subject experience pain in the leg or buttock while walking? (Yes/No); (2) Does the pain include the calf/calves? (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves); (3) Does the leg pain ever disappear while continuing to walk? (Yes/No); (4) On which side is the leg pain predominant? (Right | Left | Both); (5) Does leg pain occur when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground? (Yes/No). Answer type: categorical/binary responses per sub-item, collectively forming a standardized claudication symptom questionnaire (consistent with Rose/Edinburgh Claudication Questionnaire methodology). No units; responses are nominal/ordinal coded values.

records.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication screening): a structured assessment capturing the presence, characteristics, and behavior of leg or buttock pain during walking. (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves); (3) Does the leg pain ever disappear while continuing to walk? (Yes/No); (4) On which side is the leg pain predominant? (Right | Left | Both); (5) Does leg pain occur when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground? (Yes/No). cde.id: Are you now taking diabetic pills to lower your blood sugar [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Diabetes management modality assessment: a set of CDEs capturing the specific methods a person uses to manage blood glucose and A1C levels, covering five distinct treatment/management categories — (1) oral glucose-lowering medications (e.g., biguanides, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT-2 inhibitors, alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, meglitinides, bile acid sequestrants): Yes/No; (2) non-insulin injectable glucose-lowering agents (e.g., GLP-1 receptor agonists, amylin analogs): Yes/No; (3) insulin injections: Yes/No; (4) lifestyle modifications (regular exercise, dietary changes, consistent meal scheduling): Yes/No; (5) diabetes health education engagement frequency (consulting dietician, support groups, books, websites, apps): ordinal categorical — Regularly/at least monthly, Occasionally/every 2–3 months, Rarely/less than every 3 months, or Never. Each category is self-reported by the subject (self) regarding their own current diabetes management. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier applies. Categories (1)–(4) are binary Yes/No response type; category (5) is an ordered frequency scale.

gencde.definition: Indicates whether an individual uses lifestyle modifications, such as regular physical exercise, dietary changes (e.g., avoiding sugary foods, eating a balanced diet rich in vegetables), and consistent meal scheduling, as a method to control blood glucose levels and glycated hemoglobin (A1C).

gencde.rationale: Derived from a single source field (AI-READI:cmtrt_lfst) with a clear yes/no response domain. The binary coding (1=Yes, 0=No) is canonical; source used a yesno type. Near-miss CDEs (blood glucose test frequency, HbA1c lab value, glucose threshold) are related measurement concepts but capture outcomes or monitoring behaviors rather than the management modality itself. gencde.title: Frequency of Engagement in Diabetes Health Education Activities
gencde.definition: A categorical measure of how often a person with diabetes engages in health education activities related to their condition, including but not limited to consulting a dietician, attending support groups, reading diabetes-related books, using diabetes-focused websites or apps, or watching health-focused media.
gencde.questionText: How often would you say that you engage in diabetes health education? (Examples: consulting with a dietician, attending support groups, reading books on diabetes, using diabetes-focused websites, watching TV shows on health, or using health-focused apps on your phone or tablet)

relatedCdes: Doctor or health care professional ever told you that you have diabetes
Dietician consult past year count
Medical office visit diabetes past year count
gencde.rationale: Derived from a single source field (AI-READI:dmledu). Original numeric codes (0, 5, 10, 777) are preserved as they carry ordinal meaning and are used in the source instrument; 777 is a non-response sentinel retained as a permissible value per source convention rather than treated as missing, because the concept explicitly includes patient preference to not disclose. Near-miss CDEs (dietician consult count, medical office visit count) are related but capture specific visit counts rather than self-reported engagement frequency across multiple education modalities. The concept aligns with DSME/S (Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support) constructs in the ADA Standards of Care.

Categories (1)–(4) are binary Yes/No response type; category (5) is an ordered frequency scale.

gencde.questionText: Are you still seeing a doctor or health care provider for diabetes (prediabetes, type 1 diabetes, or type 2 diabetes)?
relatedCdes: Doctor or health care professional ever told you that you have diabetes
Medical office visit diabetes past year count
Are you taking medicine for diabetes [PhenX]
gencde.rationale: Three AoU source fields (prediabetes, type 1, type 2) each ask the same binary question about current provider engagement; they are harmonized into a single binary CDE covering all diabetes subtypes. The near-miss CDEs address ever-diagnosis, visit counts, and medication use — distinct constructs. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes management modality detail (medications, lifestyle), which is a related but separate concept; this CDE captures only the binary provider-contact status. Permissible values are restricted to Yes/No as observed across all source fields; missing-data sentinels were excluded per instructions.

records.concept: Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)

cde.id: What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed or the highest degree you have received [NHANES]

records.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'

records.concept: CES-D positive affect item: past-week frequency of positive emotional state (hopeful/happy), 4-point ordinal scale
records.idealCde: Positive affect / well-being item from the CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) positive subscale: a single self-report item asking the respondent how often during the past week they experienced a specific positive emotional state (e.g., felt hopeful about the future; felt happy). The question is framed as 'During the past week, how often did you feel [positive state]?' Answer type: ordinal 4-point frequency scale anchored to days in the past 7 days — 0 = All of the time (5–7 days), 1 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 2 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 3 = Rarely or none of the time (< 1 day). Note: the source concept cluster contains heterogeneous fields spanning positive affect (CES-D items), sexual/gender identity (closer self-description including queer, polysexual/omnisexual/sapiosexual/pansexual, asexual, two-spirit), a general overall health descriptor, and a 0–10 numeric pain intensity rating (past 7 days average); these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than a single unified element.

gencde.title: CES-D Positive Affect Item: Past-Week Frequency of Positive Emotional State (Hopeful/Happy)
gencde.definition: A single self-report ordinal item from the CES-D positive affect subscale asking how often during the past week the respondent experienced a specific positive emotional state (e.g., felt hopeful about the future or felt happy), rated on a 4-point frequency scale anchored to number of days in the prior 7 days.
