records.concept: Area-level multiple deprivation index score or domain sub-score (composite or domain-specific: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, community safety) for small geographic areas (LSOA/WIMD)
records.idealCde: Area-level multiple deprivation index score or domain sub-score capturing the degree of socioeconomic deprivation experienced by residents of a small geographic area (e.g., Lower Super Output Area/LSOA in England or Wales). The CDE answers: 'What is the composite or domain-specific deprivation level for this geographic area, encompassing dimensions such as income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety?' Answer type: continuous numeric score or rank (dimensionless index value or percentile rank), assigned at the small-area geographic unit level, derived from a weighted combination of domain indicators (e.g., proportion of income-deprived individuals, geographical access distances to key services including food shops, GP surgeries, primary schools, post offices, and public libraries). May be reported as an overall multiple deprivation score/rank or as individual domain scores/ranks (income deprivation, access to services deprivation, etc.) for the specified area.

gencde.title: Area-Level Multiple Deprivation Index Score or Domain Sub-Score (Small Geographic Area)
gencde.definition: A continuous numeric score or rank quantifying the degree of socioeconomic deprivation experienced by residents of a small geographic area (e.g., Lower Super Output Area/LSOA in England, or equivalent Welsh small area), derived from a composite index or a domain-specific sub-index encompassing dimensions such as income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety.
gencde.questionText: What is the composite or domain-specific deprivation index score or rank assigned to the small geographic area (e.g., LSOA or WIMD area) in which this individual resides, as measured by the Index of Multiple Deprivation (England) or Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wales)?
aliases: Barriers to housing and services score
relatedCdes: Household Member Size
Family income supported persons count
Health problem interfere household task good day scale
gencde.rationale: All five source fields (IMD England composite, WIMD Wales composite, Income domain England, Income domain Wales, Access to Services domain Wales) measure continuous dimensionless deprivation scores or ranks assigned at the LSOA/small-area level. No permissible value enumeration applies; the value domain is a non-negative real number (score) or positive integer (rank). Maximum is unbounded in the schema because rank upper bounds vary by release year and nation (e.g., 32,844 LSOAs in England 2010; 1,896 LSOAs in Wales 2008). Units coded as '1' (dimensionless per UCUM convention). A single CDE accommodates both composite and domain sub-scores; implementers should use a companion 'domain_type' qualifier variable (e.g., composite, income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access_to_services, community_safety) and a 'nation' qualifier (England, Wales) to distinguish instances. Near-miss CDEs (household size, family income count, health interference scale) are conceptually distinct individual-level measures and were not used as aliases.

memberDetails.name: Access to services score (Wales)
memberDetails.text:
The purpose of this domain is to illustrate the deprivation as a result of a household's inability to access a range of services, considered necessary for day-to-day living. The access is by walking or using public bus services or both. The indicators used for the geographical access to services domain were:
  • Food shop
  • GP surgery
  • Primary school
  • Post office
  • Public library
  • Leisure centre
  • NHS dentist
  • Secondary school
  • Transport nodes

memberDetails.name: Income score (England)
memberDetails.text:
This domain measures the proportion of the population in an area experiencing deprivation related to low income. A combined count of income deprived individuals per LSOA is calculated by summing the following five indicators:
  • Adults and children in Income Support families
  • Adults and children in Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance families
  • Adults and children in Pension Credit (Guarantee) families
  • Adults and children in Child Tax Credit families (who are not in receipt of Income Support, Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance or Pension Credit) whose equivalised income (excluding housing benefits) is below 60 per cent of the median before housing costs
  • Asylum seekers in England in receipt of subsistence support, accommodation support, or both.

memberDetails.name: Income score (Wales)
memberDetails.text:
The purpose of this domain is to capture the extent of deprivation relating to income at a small area level across Wales. It focuses on the proportion of people living in households with income below a defined threshold or claiming benefits relating to low incomes. The indicators used for the income domain were:
  • Adults & children in income support households
  • Adults & children in pension credit households
  • Adults & children in income-based job seekers allowance households
  • Adults & children in tax credit (child tax credit and working tax credit) households below a low income threshold
  • National Asylum Support Service (NASS) supported asylum seekers in Wales in receipt of subsistence only and accommodation support

memberDetails.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (England)
memberDetails.text:
The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at the small area level. The model of multiple deprivation which underpins the Indices of Deprivation 2010 is based on the idea of distinct domains of deprivation which can be recognised and measured separately. These domains are experienced by individuals living in an area. People may be counted in one or more of the domains, depending on the number of types of deprivation that they experience.

Each domain represents a specific form of deprivation experienced by people and each can be measured individually using a number of indicators. Seven distinct domains have been identified in the English Indices of Deprivation; Income Deprivation, Employment Deprivation, Health Deprivation and Disability, Education Skills and Training Deprivation, Barriers to Housing and Services, Living Environment Deprivation, and Crime. Individual domains can be used in isolation as measures of each specific form of deprivation. They can also be combined, using appropriate weights, into a single overall Index of Multiple Deprivation which can be used to rank every small area in England according to the deprivation experienced by the people living there. Along with two supplementary indices, Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index and Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index, they form the English Indices of Deprivation. These statistics allow the most, and least, deprived areas of the country to be identified as well as providing information about the issues faced by people living in different parts of the country.

memberDetails.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wales)
memberDetails.text:
The Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation 2008 is the official measure of deprivation for small areas in Wales. It was developed for the Welsh Assembly Government by the Assembly's Statistical Directorate and the Local Government Data Unit (Wales).

The WIMD 2008 is made up of eight separate domains (or kinds) of deprivation: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety.

Each of them was based on a range of different indicators which meant that they were measured in different ways using different units. So before they could be combined the measurements had to be transformed to make them compatible. For example, if the height of something had been measured in metres and the weight in kilograms it would not make sense simply to add them together.

Income and employment were classed as the most important factors, and they were given the biggest weighting in the overall index. Although there is more to deprivation than poverty, not having enough money or a job is a big part of it.

gencde.rationale: Derived from two source fields: CLSA:MEDI_NO_COM (text-encoded integer) and UKBB 'Number of treatments/medications taken' (integer). Both fields capture the same concept — a non-negative integer count of all current medications/treatments at time of assessment. The CLSA field uses a text type but encodes a numeric value; the canonical type is numeric (non-negative integer). No upper bound is enforced in source data, so maximum_value is left null. The IDEAL CDE also references an assessment date element, but that is a separate CDE; this element covers only the count. Near-miss CDEs (concomitant medications text, pain treatment text/dose) are qualitative or condition-specific and were excluded from the value domain.

gencde.rationale: Source field is UKBB F2956, a categorical-single item administered as a follow-up to participants endorsing widespread body pain interfering with usual activities (F6159). Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer) are excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per harmonization instructions. Body site qualifier 'all over the body' distinguishes this element from site-specific chronic pain CDEs (back, hip, neck/shoulder, abdomen). The 3-month duration threshold aligns with the IASP definition of chronic pain and the ACR 1990 widespread pain criterion used in fibromyalgia classification. Near-miss CDEs reference pain presence or episode timing but do not capture the chronic (>3 months) widespread pain construct.

records.concept: Neighborhood crime rate makes it unsafe to walk during the day (agreement rating)
records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability barrier perception — individual item assessing the degree to which a specific environmental or safety factor (crime rate during the day, crime rate at night, or traffic volume/unpleasantness) makes walking in the respondent's neighborhood difficult or unsafe; question asks the respondent to rate their level of agreement with a stated barrier to neighborhood walking (e.g., 'The crime rate in my neighborhood makes it unsafe to go on walks [during the day / at night]' or 'There is so much traffic on the streets that it makes it difficult or unpleasant to walk in my neighborhood'); answer type is an ordinal Likert scale with 4 response options (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with an optional non-applicable response for the traffic item (e.g., 'There are no streets or roads in my neighborhood'); qualifier varies by item: daytime crime barrier, nighttime crime barrier, or traffic/street barrier to walking — these are distinct sub-items and should not be collapsed into a single field.

records.concept: Neighborhood traffic volume makes walking difficult or unpleasant (agreement rating)
records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability barrier perception — individual item assessing the degree to which a specific environmental or safety factor (crime rate during the day, crime rate at night, or traffic volume/unpleasantness) makes walking in the respondent's neighborhood difficult or unsafe; question asks the respondent to rate their level of agreement with a stated barrier to neighborhood walking (e.g., 'The crime rate in my neighborhood makes it unsafe to go on walks [during the day / at night]' or 'There is so much traffic on the streets that it makes it difficult or unpleasant to walk in my neighborhood'); answer type is an ordinal Likert scale with 4 response options (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with an optional non-applicable response for the traffic item (e.g., 'There are no streets or roads in my neighborhood'); qualifier varies by item: daytime crime barrier, nighttime crime barrier, or traffic/street barrier to walking — these are distinct sub-items and should not be collapsed into a single field.

The 4-point Likert agreement scale (codes 1–4) constitutes the substantive response set; codes 88, 555, and 777 are retained as non-substantive but clinically meaningful response options observed in the source data. No missing-data sentinels (e.g., 999, -9) were present and none were added. The item is conceptually aligned with the Neighborhood Environment Walkability Scale (NEWS) traffic subscale and the IPAQ neighborhood environment module, supporting the listed aliases. Near-miss CDEs address physical mobility limitations rather than perceived environmental barriers and were used only to confirm non-overlap.

cde.id: How often do you have 6 or more drinks on 1 occasion [SAMHSA]

records.idealCde: Alcohol Use Frequency and Quantity (AUDIT-C-style): A set of items capturing the pattern of alcohol consumption, specifically (1) how often the respondent drinks alcohol (frequency of any drinking occasion), (2) how many standard drinks they consume on a typical drinking day (typical quantity), and (3) how often they consume six or more drinks on a single occasion (heavy episodic/binge drinking frequency). Each item is answered on an ordinal frequency or quantity scale: frequency options range from 'never' through daily or almost daily (e.g., never, less than monthly/once a month or less, monthly/2–4 times a month, weekly/2–3 times a week, daily or almost daily/4+ times a week); typical quantity options are 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–9, or 10 or more standard drinks; heavy-occasion frequency options are never (in the past year/month), less than monthly, monthly, weekly, or daily or almost daily. Time window varies across member fields (past 12 months or past month). Answer type: ordinal categorical (radio/select) for each sub-item. No laterality or body-site qualifier; subject is self-report.

records.idealCde: Alcohol Use Frequency and Quantity (AUDIT-C-style): A set of items capturing the pattern of alcohol consumption, specifically (1) how often the respondent drinks alcohol (frequency of any drinking occasion), (2) how many standard drinks they consume on a typical drinking day (typical quantity), and (3) how often they consume six or more drinks on a single occasion (heavy episodic/binge drinking frequency). Each item is answered on an ordinal frequency or quantity scale: frequency options range from 'never' through daily or almost daily (e.g., never, less than monthly/once a month or less, monthly/2–4 times a month, weekly/2–3 times a week, daily or almost daily/4+ times a week); typical quantity options are 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–9, or 10 or more standard drinks; heavy-occasion frequency options are never (in the past year/month), less than monthly, monthly, weekly, or daily or almost daily. Time window varies across member fields (past 12 months or past month). Answer type: ordinal categorical (radio/select) for each sub-item. No laterality or body-site qualifier; subject is self-report.

gencde.title: Hip-Waist Ratio Measurement Test Exclusion Flag
gencde.definition: A binary indicator denoting whether a participant was excluded from undergoing the hip-to-waist ratio measurement procedure at the time of assessment.
gencde.questionText: Was the participant excluded from the hip-waist ratio test?
relatedCdes: Waist-hip ratio value
Hip scanned Hip PhenX
Dual X-ray absorptiometry hip T score
gencde.rationale: Derived from a single CLSA source field (WHC_EXCL_COM) coded as a boolean true/false flag. The ideal CDE anchor provided (standing height) appears to be a mismatch with the concept; the GenCDE is authored strictly on the observed concept (hip-waist ratio exclusion) and the single binary answer set observed. Near-miss CDEs (waist-hip ratio value, hip PhenX scan, DXA hip T-score) confirm the anthropometric domain but are distinct constructs. Confidence is moderate because only one source cohort contributed data and the clinical reason for exclusion is not captured.

gencde.rationale: Source fields are sex-stratified (CLSA females: 4+ drinks; CLSA males: 5+ drinks), consistent with NIAAA sex-specific binge drinking thresholds. The eight permissible values are reconciled directly from the pooled observed answer options across both source fields — no options were added or removed. Code 96 (Never) in source was remapped to code 8 for clean sequential ordering. The ideal CDE anchor uses a 6+ drink threshold and a past-month window (AUDIT-C style), making it a near-miss; this GenCDE preserves the 12-month reference period and sex-specific thresholds actually observed. Confidence is slightly reduced from 1.0 due to the dual-threshold sex-specific design, which is uncommon in standard CDE repositories and may require split representation in some systems.

gencde.rationale: Source field AI-READI:diet4 used an ambiguous label '2-Jan' which is a date-parsing artifact for the range '1-2'; this has been reconciled to '1 to 2 per day' (code 1). The missing-data sentinel 777 ('Prefer not to say') is retained as a canonical permissible value (recoded to 999) rather than dropped, because it represents a meaningful response category distinct from a true missing value. Near-miss CDEs (FFQ-style frequency-of-consumption questions for caffeinated and non-diet colas) were used to inform aliases but differ in time window (usual frequency vs. daily count) and beverage scope. The concept is specific to non-diet, sugar-sweetened sodas and sweet tea, excluding diet beverages, energy drinks, and other caffeinated beverages.

Answer types: binary Yes/No radio responses for each current-care question (one per named condition); binary Yes/No radio for additional medication presence; free-text string for medication name(s). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; subject is the self-reporting participant.

gencde.rationale: All five source fields (AoU circulatory and infectious disease modules) share an identical binary Yes/No response structure and a common stem question about ongoing provider contact for a named condition. The concept is condition-qualified (CHF, coronary artery disease, high cholesterol, hypertension, STIs); implementations should record the specific condition as a companion variable or repeat this element per condition. Near-miss CDEs address past treatment or ever-diagnosed status, which are temporally distinct from the current-care focus captured here. Permissible values collapsed from verbose source codes (e.g., CongestiveHeartFailureCurrently_Yes) to canonical Yes/No with binary codes 1/0.

records.idealCde: Current Medical Management Status: A composite concept capturing whether an individual is currently under active medical care or treatment for cardiovascular and metabolic conditions, and what medications they are currently taking. Specifically addresses: (1) whether the person is currently seeing a doctor or health care provider for each of the following conditions — congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, and high cholesterol; and (2) whether the person is currently taking any medications (prescription, over-the-counter, vitamins, or herbal supplements) not otherwise captured, along with free-text entry of medication names. Answer types: binary Yes/No radio responses for each current-care question (one per named condition); binary Yes/No radio for additional medication presence; free-text string for medication name(s). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; subject is the self-reporting participant.

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE represents a condition-agnostic template for the AoU 'currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment' question pattern applied across multiple disease domains (circulatory, digestive, infectious diseases). The condition qualifier (e.g., Afib, CHF, PE/DVT, acid reflux, bowel obstruction, celiac disease, colon polyps, STIs) must be specified as a context variable or instantiated as a condition-specific CDE. The permissible value set is binary (Yes/No) as consistently observed across all eight source fields; internal coded values (e.g., RxMedsforAtrialFibrillation_Yes) were treated as synonymous with Yes/No and collapsed. Near-miss CDEs were used only to inform aliases and confirm non-overlap with existing catalog entries.

gencde.rationale: CLSA source field provides an ordinal categorical encoding (1=One, 2=Two, 3=Three or more) while MESA totmed5 is a continuous numeric field; because the only observed answer concepts across both sources are 'One', 'Two', and 'Three or more', the canonical permissible-value set is constrained to these three ordinal categories. A fully numeric representation would be preferable if raw MESA values were pooled directly, but the harmonized answer concepts observed do not support that. Near-miss CDEs (prescription medication indicator, headache treatment) were used only to inform aliases and confirm non-overlap.

gencde.rationale: Source is UK Biobank Data-Field 20003 (Treatment/medication code), a multi-select categorical field where positive codes map to a controlled drug/treatment vocabulary and negative codes capture free-text entries. The ideal CDE anchor describes a broader composite concept (current medical management for CVD/metabolic conditions plus any medications); this GenCDE is scoped narrowly to the coded treatment/medication identifier as actually observed in the source field. Permissible values are representative archetypes (coded entry, free-text entry, prefer-not-to-answer, none) because the full UKBB coding list (Coding 4) contains thousands of drug codes and cannot be enumerated here. Near-miss CDEs were laboratory-test negative-specify-text fields sharing the free-text-entry pattern but are conceptually unrelated. Confidence is moderate because only one source cohort field was available and the ideal anchor concept is broader than the single observed field.

records.concept: Age (life-stage category) when first told had congestive heart failure
records.idealCde: Age at first diagnosis of a specified condition (self-reported): captures the life-stage age category at which the respondent was first told by a healthcare provider that they had a given medical condition. The question asked is 'About how old were you when you were first told you had [condition]?' with [condition] being a condition-specific qualifier (e.g., congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, high cholesterol). Answer type is an ordinal categorical variable with values: Child (0–11), Adolescent (12–17), Adult (18–64), Older Adult (65–74), and implicitly an oldest adult category (75+). Each condition constitutes a distinct CDE instance sharing this structure. Subject is self (the survey respondent). Note: the source concept also includes heterogeneous fields (diabetes survey date as free-text date, and waist-to-hip ratio as a calculated numeric value) that do not share this measurement construct and represent separate CDEs.

Near-miss CDEs (PhenX kidney failure age item; heart attack age items) informed alias construction but were not used to add answer concepts. LOINC and SNOMED CT do not currently carry an exact pre-coordinated term for age-at-CHF-diagnosis life-stage category, so no authoritative code is assigned.

gencde.rationale: The source fields are entirely unrelated: they include a diabetes survey date (text), waist-to-hip ratio (continuous), diabetes incidence flag (binary), height protocol modification flags (binary), birth weight (continuous, kg), birth weight unit (categorical), gestational diabetes indicator (categorical), heel bone mineral density T-scores (continuous, SD units), height device ID (text), and weight-skip reason (multi-category). No single clinical concept, data type, unit, or question text unifies them. The pooled answer-concept list is itself a mixture of yes/no responses, measurement-unit choices, and skip-reason codes from entirely different instruments. A GenCDE cannot be meaningfully authored for this grouping; the permissible-value set above is provided only to satisfy schema requirements and reflects the observed categorical codes verbatim. Confidence is near zero (0.05) because the concept boundary is undefined.

records.concept: Contact attempt log entry: date/time of attempt and purpose of contact
records.idealCde: Contact attempt log entry capturing the date and time of a study participant contact attempt or outreach event, along with the purpose of that contact. The CDE answers: 'When was the contact attempt made, and what was the reason for contacting the participant?' Answer type: a structured record with (1) Date/time field in ISO 8601 datetime format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), and (2) Purpose of contact as a categorical coded value from a defined enumeration (e.g., questions regarding consent, report change in contact, device issue, device return, randomization completion request, in-person visit scheduling, study payment, adverse event report, or other).

gencde.title: Study Participant Contact Attempt Date/Time and Purpose of Contact
gencde.definition: A structured log entry recording the date and time of a study participant contact attempt or outreach event, together with the coded reason for initiating that contact.
gencde.questionText: When was the contact attempt made, and what was the purpose of contacting the participant?
relatedCdes: Illness or injury onset date and time
Event discovery date and time
Attempt sex intercourse satisfac PhenX
gencde.rationale: This CDE is a compound concept combining two tightly coupled sub-fields observed in AI-READI: (1) a free-text ISO 8601 datetime stamp for the contact attempt (cnct_dattim) and (2) a categorical purpose-of-contact code (cnct_prp). Because the schema requires a single data_type, 'categorical' is assigned to represent the purpose dimension, which carries the primary analytical value; the datetime component should be captured as a companion ISO 8601 text/date field (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS) in any implementation. Permissible values are drawn exclusively from the nine answer concepts observed in the source fields; missing-data sentinel 888 ('Other') is retained as a canonical code per source. Near-miss CDEs (illness/injury onset datetime; event discovery datetime) share a datetime-logging pattern but differ in clinical domain and do not contribute permissible values here.

gencde.title: Participant Employment/Work Address Location (City, State, Country)
gencde.definition: The geographic location of a study participant's employment or work address, captured as city (free text), state (coded enumeration of U.S. states and D.C.), and country (free text).
gencde.questionText: What is the city, state, and country of your employment or work address?
relatedCdes: City PhenX
City__2
Job hx company address Addr NHANES
gencde.rationale: This GenCDE consolidates three source sub-fields (city as free text, state as coded dropdown, country as free text) from the AoU employment/work address module into a single composite location CDE. The canonical permissible-value set covers only the state sub-component, using standard USPS two-letter codes as canonical codes mapped to the 50 U.S. states plus D.C. observed in the source. City and country remain free-text components of the composite. The IDEAL CDE anchor described a contact-attempt log, which is a different concept; the source fields clearly represent participant work address geography. Near-miss CDEs (City PhenX, City__2, Job hx company address NHANES) were used only to inform aliases. Confidence is moderate because the concept spans three distinct sub-fields that ideally would be separate CDEs, and the state enumeration is U.S.-centric.

Answer type: a structured record with (1) Date/time field in ISO 8601 datetime format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), and (2) Purpose of contact as a categorical coded value from a defined enumeration (e.g., questions regarding consent, report change in contact, device issue, device return, randomization completion request, in-person visit scheduling, study payment, adverse event report, or other).

gencde.title: Mobility Within Home: Access to Other Rooms (Frequency and Assistance)
gencde.definition: A composite assessment of whether an individual was able to access rooms in their home other than their sleeping room during the past four weeks, how frequently they did so, and whether they required personal assistance or adaptive equipment to do so.
gencde.questionText: During the past four weeks, have you been to other rooms of your home besides the room where you sleep? If yes, how often did you get to other rooms, and did you use aids or equipment or need help from another person to do so?

permissibleValues.label: Yes – no assistance or equipment needed
Yes – personal assistance (with or without equipment)
No – did not access other rooms

relatedCdes: In the past 7 days How often did pain restrict your social life to your home?
Are you able to move a chair from one room to another?__2
How much DIFFICULTY do you currently have walking around one floor of your home?
gencde.rationale: Three source fields from CLSA (LSI_ROOM_COM, LSI_RMFQ_COM, LSI_RMAID_COM) collectively capture a single functional mobility concept: ability to access other rooms in the home, frequency of doing so, and level of assistance required. Because these are logically related sub-questions of one concept, the permissible values from all three are pooled into a single canonical set. Codes 1–4 reflect the access/assistance dimension (merging the binary 'Yes/No' from LSI_ROOM_COM with the assistance categories from LSI_RMAID_COM; 'Yes' without qualification maps to code 1 as the unassisted case). Codes 5–8 reflect the frequency dimension from LSI_RMFQ_COM. Implementers may choose to represent this as a structured multi-part item or split into sub-elements. The ideal CDE anchor provided (contact attempt log) appears to be a metadata mismatch and was disregarded in favor of the source fields and concept description. Near-miss CDEs were used only to confirm distinctness and inform aliases.

gencde.rationale: Concept is drawn from a single CLSA source field (RET_STDLIV_TRM) with a 3-level ordinal response scale. The ideal CDE anchor provided describes a contact-attempt log, which is unrelated to this concept and was disregarded; the GenCDE is authored solely from the source field and observed answer concepts. Near-miss CDEs (household size, quality of life, household income amount) are related but distinct constructs. The permissible-value set is minimal (3 codes) and fully grounded in observed source values; no additional categories were introduced. Confidence is slightly reduced due to single-cohort sourcing and the mismatch between the provided ideal CDE anchor and the actual concept.

gencde.definition: A binary self-reported indicator of whether an individual has ever been addicted to or dependent on a prescription or over-the-counter medication, or has ever been prescribed medication by a health professional for unusual or psychotic experiences (e.g., visions, voices, paranoid beliefs).
gencde.questionText: Have you ever been addicted to or dependent on a prescription or over-the-counter medication, or been prescribed a medication by a health professional for unusual or psychotic experiences such as seeing visions, hearing voices, or believing something strange was communicating with you or that there was a plot against you?

gencde.rationale: Two distinct UKBB fields (F20401-derived addiction/dependence item and F20471/F20463/F20474/F20468-derived psychosis medication item) were harmonized under this concept because both capture a binary yes/no history of clinically significant medication involvement related to mental health or substance use. The ideal CDE anchor provided (contact attempt log) appears to be a metadata mismatch and was disregarded in favor of the actual source field content. Missing-data sentinels (-818=Prefer not to answer, -121=Do not know) were excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. Confidence is moderate (0.55) because the two source fields represent conceptually adjacent but not identical constructs; downstream users should consider splitting into separate CDEs if analytic precision is required.

gencde.title: Employment Gap History and Impact on Normal Roles
gencde.definition: A composite assessment capturing the nature of periods when a participant was not engaged in paid employment for at least 20 hours per week (gap coding), and the degree to which problems during a worst depressive episode interfered with normal life roles including employment, childcare, housework, and leisure.
gencde.questionText: During periods when you were not working in paid employment for at least 20 hours per week, what were you doing? And during your worst period of depression, how much did these problems interfere with your normal roles and activities (e.g., study/employment, childcare, housework, leisure pursuits)?

permissibleValues.label: Paid work for less than 15 hours per week on average or lasting less than 6 months
Looking after the home and/or family
Unable to work due to sickness or disability

aliases: functional role impact during depressive episode
sourceVariables: UKBB:Impact on normal roles during worst period of depression
relatedCdes: Participation Assessment with Recombined Tools-Objective (PART-O) - Job money time score
Mayo-Portland Adaptability Inventory (MPAI-4) - paid employment scale
Physical activity 20 minute day during week count
gencde.rationale: This GenCDE consolidates two conceptually distinct but related UKBB fields: (1) gap coding — the reason(s) for periods of non-employment — and (2) role impact during worst depression, which captures functional interference with employment and other life roles. The permissible values are drawn exclusively from the observed answer concepts across both source fields; missing-data sentinels (Prefer not to answer, -121 Unknown) are collapsed into 'Unknown, cannot remember' per schema guidance. The integer field (number of gap periods) is a count companion variable and is noted here but not separately enumerated as it is numeric. Confidence is moderate-low because the concept as stated conflates two distinct measurement constructs (gap reason vs. functional impact severity), which ideally would be separated into two CDEs; however, the source harmonization groups them together. Near-miss CDEs (PART-O, MPAI-4) inform aliases only.

gencde.rationale: Sourced exclusively from UK Biobank (UKBB) ACE touchscreen item. Original response options included 'Do not know' (-1) and 'Prefer not to answer' (-3), which are treated as missing-data sentinels and excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per harmonization rules. The concept aligns with the UK Office for National Statistics definition of limiting long-term illness (LLTI) and is conceptually related to, but narrower than, the PhenX disability CDE near-misses, which focus specifically on interference with daily activities or functional disability domains. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a broader multi-domain disability/coverage construct; this GenCDE is scoped strictly to the generic long-standing illness/disability/infirmity yes/no flag as observed in the source field.

records.idealCde: Ophthalmic/cardiovascular procedure or condition occurrence flag and associated date: a pair of data elements capturing (1) whether a specific ocular condition (e.g., age-related macular degeneration in one or both eyes, retinal vascular occlusion in one or both eyes) or diagnostic procedure (e.g., best-corrected visual acuity assessment, Eidon confocal fundus photography mosaic image creation, EKG/electrocardiogram) was present or performed — answered as a binary Yes/No (1=Yes, 0=No) — and (2) the date and time the condition was recorded or the procedure was performed, expressed as a free-text or structured datetime value (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM). Note: member fields carry heterogeneous qualifiers spanning distinct conditions and procedures (AMD bilateral, retinal vascular occlusion bilateral, CFP mosaic imaging, BCVA, EKG); no single unified qualifier applies — each member represents a separate condition- or procedure-specific occurrence indicator with its own associated datetime.

gencde.title: Snellen Fraction Visual Acuity Measurement (Mesopic/Photopic, OD/OS)
gencde.definition: A text-encoded Snellen fraction (e.g., '20/20') representing the measured visual acuity of a specified eye (oculus dexter or oculus sinister) under a specified luminance condition (mesopic or photopic), obtained during a standardized visual acuity assessment.
gencde.questionText: What is the Snellen fraction visual acuity recorded for the specified eye (OD or OS) under the specified lighting condition (mesopic or photopic)?
relatedCdes: Optical coherence tomography (OCT) retinal thickness laterality type
Optical coherence tomography (OCT) oculus dexter (OD) macula volume measurement
Optical coherence tomography retinal nerve fiber layer thickness laterality type
gencde.rationale: All three source fields (viaodmsf, viaodpsf, viaosmsf) are typed as free text and encode Snellen fractions (numerator/denominator format, e.g., '20/40'). Because the value space is an open-ended ratio string rather than a fixed enumeration, data_type is set to 'text' rather than 'numeric'; downstream pipelines should parse and convert to logMAR or decimal equivalents as needed. The concept covers two laterality qualifiers (OD, OS) and two luminance conditions (mesopic, photopic); implementations should pair this CDE with laterality and luminance-condition qualifier elements. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a binary flag/date pair for ophthalmic conditions, which is a distinct concept; near-miss CDEs relate to OCT measurements and are used only to inform aliases. Confidence is modestly reduced because the source field for OS photopic (viaospsf) was not present in the harmonized set, leaving the OS-photopic cell unconfirmed.

AoU:sdoh_intro.name: sdoh_intro
AoU:sdoh_intro.text:
Thank you (again) for being a part of the All of Us Research Program. Many things can make us sick or keep us healthy. Where you were born or where you live, go to school, or work can affect your health. These are sometimes referred to as social factors, or the "social determinants", of health. Help us learn more by completing this survey about your neighborhood, social life, stress, and feelings about your everyday life. This survey will take less than 10 minutes to complete.

Please answer each question as honestly as possible. It is important that you answer as many questions as you can. We are looking for your own answers, and not what you think your doctors, family, or friends want you to say.

Don't feel like you have to spend a long time on each question. The first answer that comes to you is usually the best one. If you aren't sure how to answer a question, choose the best answer from the options given. Some of the questions may be sensitive. You can choose not to answer.

UKBB:Access to services score (Wales).text:
The purpose of this domain is to illustrate the deprivation as a result of a household's inability to access a range of services, considered necessary for day-to-day living. The access is by walking or using public bus services or both. The indicators used for the geographical access to services domain were:
  • Food shop
  • GP surgery
  • Primary school
  • Post office
  • Public library
  • Leisure centre
  • NHS dentist
  • Secondary school
  • Transport nodes

UKBB:Degree to which abdominal pain/disc.name: Degree to which abdominal pain/discomfort/altered bowel habits affect/interfere with life in general
UKBB:Degree to which abdominal pain/disc.text:
Question asked: "Please indicate how much abdominal pain or discomfort or altered bowel habits are affecting or interfering with your life in general."

Participants were asked to move a slider to choose a number between 0 to 10, with 0 meaning "not at all" and 10 meaning "completely". Participants using an older browser were asked to select a button from 0 to 10.

The question in this field was taken from the IBS Severity Scoring System used with the authors' permission.

Francis CY, Morris J, Whorwell PJ. The irritable bowel severity scoring system: a simple method of monitoring irritable bowel syndrome and its progress. Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics 1997;11(2):395-402

UKBB:Income score (England).name: Income score (England)
UKBB:Income score (England).text:
This domain measures the proportion of the population in an area experiencing deprivation related to low income. A combined count of income deprived individuals per LSOA is calculated by summing the following five indicators:
  • Adults and children in Income Support families
  • Adults and children in Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance families
  • Adults and children in Pension Credit (Guarantee) families
  • Adults and children in Child Tax Credit families (who are not in receipt of Income Support, Income-Based Jobseeker's Allowance or Pension Credit) whose equivalised income (excluding housing benefits) is below 60 per cent of the median before housing costs
  • Asylum seekers in England in receipt of subsistence support, accommodation support, or both.

UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Engl.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (England)
UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Engl.text:
The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at the small area level. The model of multiple deprivation which underpins the Indices of Deprivation 2010 is based on the idea of distinct domains of deprivation which can be recognised and measured separately. These domains are experienced by individuals living in an area. People may be counted in one or more of the domains, depending on the number of types of deprivation that they experience.

Each domain represents a specific form of deprivation experienced by people and each can be measured individually using a number of indicators. Seven distinct domains have been identified in the English Indices of Deprivation; Income Deprivation, Employment Deprivation, Health Deprivation and Disability, Education Skills and Training Deprivation, Barriers to Housing and Services, Living Environment Deprivation, and Crime. Individual domains can be used in isolation as measures of each specific form of deprivation. They can also be combined, using appropriate weights, into a single overall Index of Multiple Deprivation which can be used to rank every small area in England according to the deprivation experienced by the people living there. Along with two supplementary indices, Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index and Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index, they form the English Indices of Deprivation. These statistics allow the most, and least, deprived areas of the country to be identified as well as providing information about the issues faced by people living in different parts of the country.

UKBB:Income score (Wales).name: Income score (Wales)
UKBB:Income score (Wales).text:
The purpose of this domain is to capture the extent of deprivation relating to income at a small area level across Wales. It focuses on the proportion of people living in households with income below a defined threshold or claiming benefits relating to low incomes. The indicators used for the income domain were:
  • Adults & children in income support households
  • Adults & children in pension credit households
  • Adults & children in income-based job seekers allowance households
  • Adults & children in tax credit (child tax credit and working tax credit) households below a low income threshold
  • National Asylum Support Service (NASS) supported asylum seekers in Wales in receipt of subsistence only and accommodation support

UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time.name: Pulse wave peak to peak time
UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time.text:
peak to peak time in milliseconds

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. peak to peak time is the difference between the peak values of direct and reflected components.

UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wale.name: Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wales)
UKBB:Index of Multiple Deprivation (Wale.text:
The Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation 2008 is the official measure of deprivation for small areas in Wales. It was developed for the Welsh Assembly Government by the Assembly's Statistical Directorate and the Local Government Data Unit (Wales).

The WIMD 2008 is made up of eight separate domains (or kinds) of deprivation: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety.

Each of them was based on a range of different indicators which meant that they were measured in different ways using different units. So before they could be combined the measurements had to be transformed to make them compatible. For example, if the height of something had been measured in metres and the weight in kilograms it would not make sense simply to add them together.

Income and employment were classed as the most important factors, and they were given the biggest weighting in the overall index. Although there is more to deprivation than poverty, not having enough money or a job is a big part of it.

UKBB:Position of the pulse wave peak.name: Position of the pulse wave peak
UKBB:Position of the pulse wave peak.text:
position of the peak

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. This field is the time when the peak occurs in the waveform.

UKBB:Position of pulse wave notch.name: Position of pulse wave notch
UKBB:Position of pulse wave notch.text:
position of the notch

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. This is the time when when notch occurs in the waveform.

UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time res.name: Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time res.text:
Wave data containing 3 waveforms, each consisting of one direct and one reflected component.

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. Each waveform is actually a single pulse with 100 points. Since the heart rate is in beats per minute, a single beat takes 60seconds / Heart Rate and time between two beats is (60/Heart Rate)/100.

The data is formatted as follows:

  • The first number (i.e. digits before the first '|' character)indicate the number of points X,Y for the curve.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated by a '|' character from the preceding/succeeding pair.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated internally by a ',' character.
The X-axis is the time in milliseconds and the Y-axis is the Pulse signal strength in arbitrary units.

Thank you (again) for being a part of the All of Us Research Program. Many things can make us sick or keep us healthy. Where you were born or where you live, go to school, or work can affect your health. These are sometimes referred to as social factors, or the "social determinants", of health. Help us learn more by completing this survey about your neighborhood, social life, stress, and feelings about your everyday life. This survey will take less than 10 minutes to complete.

Please answer each question as honestly as possible. It is important that you answer as many questions as you can. We are looking for your own answers, and not what you think your doctors, family, or friends want you to say.

Don't feel like you have to spend a long time on each question. The first answer that comes to you is usually the best one. If you aren't sure how to answer a question, choose the best answer from the options given. Some of the questions may be sensitive. You can choose not to answer.

conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of mental health and substance use conditions (blood relatives): A multi-part CDE capturing whether any blood relative has ever been diagnosed with specific mental health or substance use disorders, and if so, which family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, or other blood relative) are affected for each condition. The screening question asks whether any blood relative has ever received a diagnosis from a defined list of conditions (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety reaction/panic disorder, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and others); for each condition endorsed, a follow-up question identifies which specific biological family relationship(s) carry that diagnosis. Answer type: two-tier checkbox structure — Tier 1: multi-select categorical list of mental health/substance use condition categories (select all that apply); Tier 2: for each selected condition, a multi-select categorical list of biological family member relationship types (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, other blood relative). No laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified. Note: the source concept also includes a separate, distinct field capturing self-reported sleeping pill use in the past 2 weeks (ordinal frequency: No / A few days [<1 day/week] / Some days [1–2 days/week] / Most days [3–4 days/week] / Every day; with a 'Decline to answer' option), which carries a different qualifier (self, past-2-week window) and measures a different construct (own medication behavior) from the family history fields.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Current treatment/medication status, diagnosis details, and free-text specification for mental health and substance use conditions
conceptGroups.coherenceAxis: mental health or substance use condition

conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical Activity Assessment: A multi-dimensional CDE capturing self-reported frequency and intensity of physical activity across multiple domains (light/home-based exercise such as stretching, calisthenics, or yoga; moderate activity such as carrying light loads, bicycling at regular pace, or doubles tennis; and vigorous activity such as hiking, jogging, heavy lifting, aerobics, or fast bicycling), as well as objective physical activity monitor data availability. The CDE answers: 'How frequently does the participant engage in physical activity at each intensity level, and was objective activity monitor data collected?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale for self-reported items (e.g., daily/almost daily, irregular/1–2 times per week, rarely/none; or days per week with duration thresholds such as ≥30 min on ≥3 days/week), binary yes/no for vigorous and moderate activity participation in the past 7 days, and binary yes/no for physical activity monitor data download status; units: categorical frequency categories or days per week, with intensity stratified into light/home-based, moderate, and vigorous tiers.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Able to walk or cycle unaided for 10 minutes
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Total physical activity energy expenditure expressed in MET-minutes per week, covering moderate and/or vigorous activity across the full week.

conceptGroups.concept: Survey/form completion or start date and time (instrument-qualified)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Survey/form completion date and time: the date (and, where applicable, time) on which a specific survey or consent form was completed or submitted by the participant. Answers the question: 'When was this instrument completed?' Expected answer type: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) or datetime (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss) string, with the specific instrument (e.g., paper consent, CES-D-10, dietary survey) identified as a qualifier. Note: member fields carry different instrument qualifiers (paper consent form, CES-D-10 questionnaire, dietary survey) and some distinguish start vs. completion timestamps; each instrument-specific date/datetime should be captured as a separate CDE instance qualified by instrument name and event type (started vs. completed).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Timestamps or dates recording when a survey or consent form was started or completed within a study data collection system.

conceptGroups.concept: CES-D individual item — self-reported frequency of specific depressive symptom in past week
conceptGroups.idealCde: CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) individual item response — Concept: Self-reported frequency of a specific depressive or psychological symptom experienced by the respondent during the past week, as measured by a single CES-D scale item (e.g., feeling bothered by things, trouble concentrating, feeling depressed, effortfulness of activities, feeling fearful). Question: 'How often during the past week did you experience [specific symptom]?' Answer type: Ordinal radio-button selection scored 0–3, where 0 = Rarely or none of the time (<1 day), 1 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 2 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 3 = All of the time (5–7 days); self-report, past-7-day reference window.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported depressive symptom experiences (e.g., feeling depressed, lonely, effortful, bothered, hopeless, or inattentive) as measured by CES-D-style items

conceptGroups.concept: Miscellaneous unrelated fields (anthropometric measures, diabetes survey metadata, birth weight, bone density, etc.)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Age at first diagnosis of a specified condition (self-reported): captures the life-stage age category at which the respondent was first told by a healthcare provider that they had a given medical condition. The question asked is 'About how old were you when you were first told you had [condition]?' with [condition] being a condition-specific qualifier (e.g., congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, high cholesterol). Answer type is an ordinal categorical variable with values: Child (0–11), Adolescent (12–17), Adult (18–64), Older Adult (65–74), and implicitly an oldest adult category (75+). Each condition constitutes a distinct CDE instance sharing this structure. Subject is self (the survey respondent). Note: the source concept also includes heterogeneous fields (diabetes survey date as free-text date, and waist-to-hip ratio as a calculated numeric value) that do not share this measurement construct and represent separate CDEs.

conceptGroups.concept: Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (beer, wine, liquor, other) per typical week, in standard servings
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (beer, wine, or liquor) during a typical/average week; asks how many standard-serving units of a specific alcoholic beverage type (beer: 12 oz. bottles/cans; wine: 5 oz. glasses; liquor: 1.5 oz. shots/mixed drinks) the respondent usually consumes per week during a defined reference period; answer type is numeric quantity (count of standard servings per week), captured either as an ordinal-banded integer (e.g., 0=less than 1, up to 36 or more) or as a continuous decimal value; separate fields are expected for each beverage type (beer, wine, liquor), and may be further stratified by day type (weekday vs. weekend) within the reference period (e.g., past 12 months or general average week); self-reported by the study participant.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Number of drinks of a specific alcoholic beverage type consumed in a typical week (weekday or weekend) over the past 12 months

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of specific cancer type: which biological relatives have been diagnosed (multi-select relative per cancer type)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of cancer by cancer type and affected biological relative: For each specific cancer type (e.g., bladder cancer, blood/soft tissue cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, and other cancer types), identifies which first- and second-degree biological relatives have been diagnosed with that cancer. The question asked is 'Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.' The answer is a multi-select checkbox response where each selectable option represents a specific biological relative relationship (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent, and potentially other relatives). Answer type: categorical multi-select (select all that apply); one such CDE per cancer type, with response options representing distinct biological relative categories (e.g., Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Family history of a specific type of cancer (select all that apply), where each field captures which family members have had a particular cancer type

conceptGroups.concept: Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Highest level of educational attainment (degree, diploma, or grade) completed by the respondent

conceptGroups.concept: Seated diastolic blood pressure reading (mmHg), by reading sequence (1st/2nd/3rd)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Blood pressure measurement (seated position) — captures both systolic and diastolic components at a specified reading number (1st, 2nd, etc.) during a seated blood pressure assessment. Question: 'What was the [systolic/diastolic] blood pressure value recorded at the [1st/2nd] reading while the subject was seated?' Answer type: integer or numeric; units: mmHg. The CDE should be structured as a paired systolic/diastolic measurement with reading-sequence qualifier (1st reading, 2nd reading) and posture qualifier (seated), yielding four discrete values: seated systolic 1st reading, seated diastolic 1st reading, seated systolic 2nd reading, seated diastolic 2nd reading — each expressed in mmHg.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Seated diastolic blood pressure readings (individual measurements) in mmHg

conceptGroups.concept: Exertional leg/buttock pain claudication screening (Rose/Edinburgh Questionnaire items)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication screening): a structured assessment capturing the presence, characteristics, and behavior of leg or buttock pain during walking. Answers the questions: (1) Does the subject experience pain in the leg or buttock while walking? (Yes/No); (2) Does the pain include the calf/calves? (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves); (3) Does the leg pain ever disappear while continuing to walk? (Yes/No); (4) On which side is the leg pain predominant? (Right | Left | Both); (5) Does leg pain occur when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground? (Yes/No). Answer type: categorical/binary responses per sub-item, collectively forming a standardized claudication symptom questionnaire (consistent with Rose/Edinburgh Claudication Questionnaire methodology). No units; responses are nominal/ordinal coded values.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Leg pain when standing still or sitting
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Assessment of leg pain characteristics during walking, including location, onset, and relief — consistent with claudication/peripheral artery disease screening

conceptGroups.concept: Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Body Mass Index (BMI) measurement across cohort visits and sub-studies

conceptGroups.concept: Number of cigarettes smoked per day (average or current)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and marijuana use history — a composite set of substance use history fields capturing: (1) lifetime cigarette use threshold (whether the respondent has smoked ≥100 cigarettes in their lifetime; binary Yes/No); (2) age at smoking initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started smoking cigarettes; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (3) total duration of cigarette smoking (number of years the respondent has smoked; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (4) average daily cigarette consumption (typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, expressed as an ordinal banded count in increments up to >50 cigarettes/day, with pack equivalents noted); and (5) age at marijuana use initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started using marijuana; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years). All fields are self-reported, refer to the respondent themselves, and carry no specific time-window qualifier beyond lifetime/habitual use. Answer types: binary radio for lifetime threshold; ordinal dropdown bands (integer-anchored, self-referent) for age-at-initiation and duration fields; ordinal dropdown bands with pack-equivalent annotations for daily cigarette quantity.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported number of cigarettes smoked per day (current or average)

conceptGroups.concept: Specific cancer type(s) diagnosed (multi-select checklist per cancer type)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Cancer diagnosis history (any type): A CDE capturing whether the participant has ever been diagnosed with cancer of any type, as reported by a physician. The primary question is: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you had cancer (any type)?' Answer type: categorical/boolean (Yes / No). Supplementary component: multi-select checklist of specific cancer types diagnosed (e.g., bladder cancer [cct_cantp_bl], breast cancer [cct_cantp_br], and additional types), each as a binary Yes/No indicator. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified in the source fields; the concept is lifetime/ever diagnosis with no restricted time window.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported type(s) of cancer diagnosed, captured as coded or categorized responses

conceptGroups.concept: Anxiety symptom profile and functional impact during worst period of anxiety (DSM-aligned Yes/No and ordinal items: concentration difficulty, sleep disturbance, keyed up, irritability, restlessness, muscle tension, role impairment, professional help-seeking)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Generalized anxiety symptom profile during worst period of anxiety: a set of categorical (Yes/No or ordinal severity) items assessing the co-occurrence of specific DSM-aligned anxiety symptoms — including difficulty concentrating, sleep-onset/maintenance disturbance, feeling keyed up or on edge, and increased irritability — as well as functional impairment in normal roles (study/employment, childcare, housework, leisure) during the worst period of anxiety. Each symptom item is answered as a binary categorical (0=No, 1=Yes); the functional impairment item is answered on an ordinal scale (0=Not at all, 1=A little, 2=Somewhat, with additional severity levels implied). All items are conditioned on the respondent having endorsed persistent worry/anxiety (either confirmed anxiety episode or worry duration ≥6 months). Qualifier: worst period of anxiety (peak severity epoch, not current or lifetime general status).

conceptGroups.concept: Hedonic liking for specific food/beverage items rated on a 9-point bipolar scale (1=extremely dislike to 9=extremely like)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary pattern and food preference assessment: captures both overall dietary quality (via a composite diet score) and individual food/beverage liking preferences. Specifically measures (1) adherence to a dietary pattern on a scored index (e.g., DASH Diet score including sodium, 0–9 integer points, where higher scores indicate greater adherence) and (2) hedonic liking for specific foods and beverages (diet fizzy drinks, dried fruit, fruit, grapefruit) each rated on a 9-point bipolar hedonic scale (1 = extremely dislike to 9 = extremely like, with special codes for 'never tried' and 'do not wish to answer'). Answer types: Numeric integer (diet score, range 0–9); Categorical ordinal single-select (food liking items, 9-point hedonic scale plus 'never tried' and 'do not wish to answer' response options). No specific laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; context is self-reported dietary quality and food preference.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Liking for sweet coffee house drinks
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported liking for a specific food or beverage item measured on a 9-point scale

conceptGroups.concept: Currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for a specific condition (Afib, CHF, PE/DVT, acid reflux, bowel obstruction, celiac disease, colon polyps, STIs)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current Medical Management Status: A composite concept capturing whether an individual is currently under active medical care or treatment for cardiovascular and metabolic conditions, and what medications they are currently taking. Specifically addresses: (1) whether the person is currently seeing a doctor or health care provider for each of the following conditions — congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, and high cholesterol; and (2) whether the person is currently taking any medications (prescription, over-the-counter, vitamins, or herbal supplements) not otherwise captured, along with free-text entry of medication names. Answer types: binary Yes/No radio responses for each current-care question (one per named condition); binary Yes/No radio for additional medication presence; free-text string for medication name(s). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; subject is the self-reporting participant.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Whether the respondent is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for a specific medical condition
coherenceDistinctValues: pulmonary embolism or deep vein thrombosis

conceptGroups.concept: Current marital/partner status of participant (categorical)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current marital/partner status of the participant (self-report). Question: 'What is your current marital or partner status?' Answer type: categorical (single-select); recommended response options include: Married, Living with a partner/common-law relationship, Domestic partner, Single/Never married, Separated, Divorced, Widowed, Other. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier; subject is the participant themselves at time of data collection.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Current marital (or marital/partner) status of the participant

conceptGroups.concept: Sex of subject/participant (general, binary)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sex and Gender Identity — A composite concept capturing two related but distinct self-reported attributes: (1) Sex assigned at birth: the biological sex recorded at birth, answering 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' with a categorical response (Male | Female | Intersex | Other/None of these); and (2) Gender identity: the gender the participant currently identifies with, answering 'What is your current gender identity?' with a categorical response (Man/Male [including transgender men] | Woman/Female [including transgender women] | Non-binary | Genderqueer | Genderfluid | Trans man/FTM | Trans woman/MTF | Other) — ideally collected as two separate fields: one radio/select for sex assigned at birth and one multi-select checkbox for gender identity (allowing selection of a closer descriptor), both self-reported by the participant with an 'Other' or 'None of these describe me' write-in option. Answer type: categorical (enumerated codes); no units.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Biological sex or gender of the participant, recorded or self-reported.

conceptGroups.concept: Frequency/servings of vegetable consumption
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Frequency or amount of vegetable consumption, covering various vegetable subgroups (other vegetables, cruciferous, green leafy, dark yellow) or total vegetables.

conceptGroups.concept: PHQ-12 SS: past 3 months bother by specific somatic symptom (ordinal 0–2 Likert per symptom item)
conceptGroups.idealCde: PHQ-12 Somatic Symptom Scale (PHQ-12 SS) — individual somatic symptom bother items assessed over the past 3 months. Each item asks: 'During the past 3 months, how much have you been bothered by [specific somatic symptom]?' covering distinct symptoms including back pain, chest pain, dizziness, palpitations (feeling heart pound or race), and headaches. Answer type: ordinal Likert scale per item (e.g., 0 = Not bothered at all, 1 = Bothered a little, 2 = Bothered a lot), with one response per symptom; time window qualifier: past 3 months; instrument qualifier: PHQ-12 SS. Note: member fields represent separate item-level CDEs within the same scale, each scoped to a distinct somatic symptom domain rather than a single unified measure.

conceptGroups.concept: Seated systolic blood pressure reading (mmHg), by reading sequence (1st/2nd/3rd)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Blood pressure measurement (seated position) — captures both systolic and diastolic components at a specified reading number (1st, 2nd, etc.) during a seated blood pressure assessment. Question: 'What was the [systolic/diastolic] blood pressure value recorded at the [1st/2nd] reading while the subject was seated?' Answer type: integer or numeric; units: mmHg. The CDE should be structured as a paired systolic/diastolic measurement with reading-sequence qualifier (1st reading, 2nd reading) and posture qualifier (seated), yielding four discrete values: seated systolic 1st reading, seated diastolic 1st reading, seated systolic 2nd reading, seated diastolic 2nd reading — each expressed in mmHg.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Seated systolic blood pressure readings (individual measurements in mmHg)

conceptGroups.concept: Physical functional mobility — walking and ambulatory activity ability
conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical functional mobility — walking ability: A CDE capturing the degree to which an individual can perform walking and related ambulatory activities (e.g., walking, climbing stairs, carrying objects) without assistance. The question asks about the presence, severity, or independence of walking/ambulation capacity. Expected answer type: ordinal categorical scale reflecting difficulty or independence level (e.g., No difficulty / A little difficulty / Moderate difficulty / Extreme difficulty / Unable; or Yes/No for unaided walking; or a graded frequency/extent scale). Note: member fields carry heterogeneous qualifiers — some assess general walking ability (unaided ambulation, yes/no), some assess difficulty with stairs and everyday physical activities, one specifically qualifies walking difficulty as attributable to eyesight (vision-related peripheral awareness while walking), and one captures fatigue-related inability to initiate movement ('get going'); these represent distinct sub-constructs (functional mobility, vision-related mobility limitation, fatigue-related initiation) that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than collapsed into one.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported ability or difficulty with walking and related ambulatory physical activities

conceptGroups.concept: Alcohol drinking behavior and context (change vs 10 years ago, with meals, former drinker status, reason for reducing/stopping)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol drinking behavior and context: a set of related categorical measures capturing self-reported current and historical alcohol consumption patterns, including (1) change in alcohol intake compared to 10 years previously (more/same/less), (2) whether alcohol is typically consumed with meals (yes/no/varies), (3) former alcohol drinker status among current non-drinkers (yes/no), (4) preferred hot drink temperature (very hot/hot/warm/does not drink hot drinks), and (5) reason for reducing alcohol consumption among those who drink less than 10 years ago (illness/doctor's advice/health precaution/other). Each sub-element is a single-select categorical response collected conditionally based on current drinking status. No single unified question; each answers a specific aspect of drinking behavior and context for an individual participant.
