conceptGroups.concept: Body weight numeric value
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Participant body weight measured or reported in pounds or kilograms

conceptGroups.concept: Waist circumference measurement in cm
conceptGroups.idealCde: Waist circumference measurement: the circumference of the abdomen at the natural waist, answering 'What is the participant's waist circumference?' Expected answer type: numeric decimal value in centimeters (cm), captured via direct physical measurement. Note: this source concept clusters multiple related anthropometric fields including waist circumference in cm, waist-to-hip ratio (dimensionless decimal), measurement condition (skin contact vs. over clothing layers: 1=on skin, 2=over one layer, 3=over two layers), and height in cm — indicating the ideal CDE set covers waist circumference (cm, decimal), measurement clothing layer condition (ordinal categorical), waist-to-hip ratio (dimensionless decimal), and height (cm, text/numeric); no specific laterality, body-side, or subject-type qualifier is specified beyond the participant themselves.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Waist circumference measurement (in cm or inches) taken at various study visits

conceptGroups.concept: Ever used other tobacco products regularly for ≥6 months (and specific types)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and nicotine product use status (self-reported, participant): A set of current and lifetime use indicators covering multiple tobacco/nicotine delivery modalities — (1) current cigarette smoking (yes/no), (2) current e-cigarette/vaping use (yes/no), (3) ever e-cigarette/vaping use (yes/no), (4) ever traditional cigar/cigarillo/filtered cigar use (yes/no), and (5) current traditional cigar/cigarillo/filtered cigar use frequency (every day / some days / not at all). Each item answers 'Does/Did the participant currently or ever use [specific product]?' Answer types are binary yes/no for ever-use and current-use items, and an ordinal frequency category (every day, some days, not at all) for current cigar use frequency; all responses are self-reported by the study participant.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Ever used other (non-cigarette) tobacco products regularly for at least six months, with each core member representing a distinct product-type response option within the same survey question
conceptGroups.coherenceAxis: specific other tobacco product type or response option
coherenceDistinctValues: any other tobacco regular use screener (CLSA:SMK_OTREG_TRM)

conceptGroups.concept: Neighborhood built environment and recreation facilities
conceptGroups.idealCde: Contact attempt log entry capturing the date and time of a study participant contact attempt or outreach event, along with the purpose of that contact. The CDE answers: 'When was the contact attempt made, and what was the reason for contacting the participant?' Answer type: a structured record with (1) Date/time field in ISO 8601 datetime format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS), and (2) Purpose of contact as a categorical coded value from a defined enumeration (e.g., questions regarding consent, report change in contact, device issue, device return, randomization completion request, in-person visit scheduling, study payment, adverse event report, or other).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Perceived availability and quality of neighborhood features that support physical activity and walkability
coherenceDistinctValues: interesting things to look at while walking

conceptGroups.concept: Servings of specific foods consumed (24-hour dietary recall: baked beans, potatoes, coleslaw, crumble, dried fruit cereal, fried potatoes)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported serving counts of specific food items consumed (from a dietary recall questionnaire, primarily vegetable-related foods), asked conditionally to UKBB participants

conceptGroups.concept: Past 12-month assistive device use — binary indicator per device type (hand-held communication, hand-held tremor-control, leg communication, leg tremor-control, notebook/tablet communication, notebook/tablet tremor-control)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Assistive device use in the past 12 months — captures whether an individual has used specific assistive devices (including hand-held communication devices, hand-held tremor-control devices, leg/lower-extremity communication devices, leg/lower-extremity tremor-control devices, and notebook/tablet computers) during the preceding 12-month period. Question: 'During the past 12 months, have you used [specific assistive device]?' Answer type: Binary indicator per device type (Yes=1 / No=0); one response per device category within the past-12-months time window.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported use of assistive devices in the past 12 months, capturing various device types across community and tracking sub-cohorts in the CLSA.

conceptGroups.concept: Chest pain or discomfort screening (presence, exertional triggers, relief)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication screening): a structured assessment capturing the presence, characteristics, and behavior of leg or buttock pain during walking. Answers the questions: (1) Does the subject experience pain in the leg or buttock while walking? (Yes/No); (2) Does the pain include the calf/calves? (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves); (3) Does the leg pain ever disappear while continuing to walk? (Yes/No); (4) On which side is the leg pain predominant? (Right | Left | Both); (5) Does leg pain occur when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground? (Yes/No). Answer type: categorical/binary responses per sub-item, collectively forming a standardized claudication symptom questionnaire (consistent with Rose/Edinburgh Claudication Questionnaire methodology). No units; responses are nominal/ordinal coded values.

conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported standing height without shoes (categorical/banded)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Self-reported height and weight perception — a cluster of two related self-report measures collected from the respondent about themselves: (1) Self-perceived weight status: the question 'Do you consider yourself overweight, underweight, or just about right?' answered as an ordinal categorical variable with values: Overweight | Underweight | Just about right; (2) Self-reported standing height without shoes: the question 'How tall are you without shoes on?' answered as a categorical/ordinal variable encoded in foot-and-inch bands with corresponding centimeter ranges (e.g., 1'0"–1'11", 2'0"–2'11", 3'0"–3'11", 4'0" and above), spanning the full plausible human height range, with each response band representing approximately 2.5 cm increments. Both measures are self-reported by the respondent (not proxy or measured), with no shoes, and pertain to the respondent's own body. Answer type: (1) nominal categorical (3-level); (2) ordinal categorical height band (feet/inches with cm equivalents).
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported height without shoes, asked as part of a height and weight questionnaire in the CLSA cohort, with multiple repeated measurement fields (trials/attempts).

conceptGroups.concept: Current occupation/employment status (single-select categorical: homemaker, employed full/part-time, on leave, unemployed, retired variants)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current employment status of the participant (self-reported): captures the individual's present work situation by asking 'What is your current employment status?' Allows selection of one or more categories from a standardized set including: Employed for wages (part-time or full-time), Self-employed, Out of work for 1 year or more, Out of work for less than 1 year, Homemaker, Student, Retired, and Unable to work. Answer type: multi-select categorical (checkbox); values are mutually exclusive categories but multiple selections permitted. Qualifier: current status, self-report, participant (not proxy). Note: source concept also includes related but distinct fields — a binary current employment indicator (yes/no paid work including part-time/seasonal/contract), a work street address (work-site qualifier), and a longest-held job pay type (paid employee/self-employed/unpaid family worker, career retrospective) — which represent separate CDEs and should not be collapsed into this current-status element.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Current occupation title or description for a respondent's present job

conceptGroups.concept: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire event date (invitation sent, module started, or module completed)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire administration date: captures the date associated with a participant's online mental health or well-being questionnaire event (invitation sent, module started, or module completed). Question answered: 'What is the date of the specified online mental health/well-being questionnaire event (invitation dispatch, start, or completion) for this participant?' Answer type: Date (ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD). Note: member fields carry distinct event-type qualifiers (invitation sent, questionnaire completed, module started, module completed) and module-level qualifiers (general health module, mental health module); the ideal CDE should be instantiated separately for each combination of event type and module scope rather than collapsed into a single undifferentiated date field.

conceptGroups.concept: Degree of difficulty rating (a little/somewhat/very difficult) for specific physical tasks (handling/gripping, lifting 10 lbs, pushing, reaching at shoulder, standing 15 minutes, stooping/bending) at a specified assessment term
conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical function difficulty degree rating across multiple specific physical tasks (handling/gripping, lifting 10 lbs, pushing, stooping/bending at shoulder, standing 15 minutes) at a specified assessment term. Question: 'Would you say the degree of difficulty is…?' for each named physical activity. Answer type: ordinal categorical; values: 1=A little difficult, 2=Somewhat difficult, 3=Very difficult. Note: member fields carry different task-specific qualifiers (handling, lifting 10 lbs, pushing, shoulder-level activity, standing 15 minutes) and a shared time-point qualifier ('trm'); each task constitutes a distinct item within this shared response-scale concept.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Rated degree of difficulty (a little / somewhat / very difficult) for a specific physical activity or functional task, asked as a follow-up qualifier in the CLSA survey

conceptGroups.concept: Digital volume pulse waveform parameters (notch/peak/shoulder position, peak-to-peak time, wave data, reflection index)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Right ventricular stroke volume: the volume of blood ejected by the right ventricle per cardiac cycle. Question answered: 'What is the right ventricular stroke volume?' Expected answer type: numeric value in milliliters (mL).

conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported race (checkbox and/or radio, including EHR-sourced raw values)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Hispanic/Latino Ethnicity and Ancestry Identity: Captures a person's self-reported ethnic origin and ancestry, answering 'What is your ancestry or ethnic origin, and do you identify as Hispanic, Latina/x, or of Spanish origin?' The CDE accommodates two complementary response modes: (1) a free-text field for open-ended ancestry or ethnic origin description (e.g., Italian, Jamaican, Cherokee, Korean, Nigerian), and (2) a structured multi-select checkbox for Hispanic/Latino subgroup identity with options including: No; Yes – Mexican; Yes – Puerto Rican; Yes – Cuban; Yes – Dominican Republic; Yes – Central American; Yes – South American; Yes – Chicano; Yes – Other. Answer type: composite — free-text string for ancestry narrative plus categorical multi-select enumeration for Hispanic/Latino affiliation. No qualifier for subject other than self-report (respondent is the subject). No laterality or body-site qualifier applies.
conceptGroups.coherenceSummary: Self-reported or EHR-recorded race (and ethnicity) of a participant, captured via various response formats (checkbox, radio, free text, or EHR extraction).

conceptGroups.concept: Ancestral ethnic or cultural group membership (repeated language/origin slots)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Hispanic/Latino Ethnicity and Ancestry Identity: Captures a person's self-reported ethnic origin and ancestry, answering 'What is your ancestry or ethnic origin, and do you identify as Hispanic, Latina/x, or of Spanish origin?' The CDE accommodates two complementary response modes: (1) a free-text field for open-ended ancestry or ethnic origin description (e.g., Italian, Jamaican, Cherokee, Korean, Nigerian), and (2) a structured multi-select checkbox for Hispanic/Latino subgroup identity with options including: No; Yes – Mexican; Yes – Puerto Rican; Yes – Cuban; Yes – Dominican Republic; Yes – Central American; Yes – South American; Yes – Chicano; Yes – Other. Answer type: composite — free-text string for ancestry narrative plus categorical multi-select enumeration for Hispanic/Latino affiliation. No qualifier for subject other than self-report (respondent is the subject). No laterality or body-site qualifier applies.

conceptGroups.concept: ACS-style functional disability indicators: serious difficulty seeing, hearing, concentrating/remembering/deciding, dressing/bathing, and doing errands alone (each Yes/No)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Disability and Government Health Coverage Status: A set of binary (Yes/No) self-reported indicators capturing whether an individual (1) is currently covered by Medicaid, Medical Assistance (MA), CHIP, or any income- or disability-based state/government-sponsored health insurance program, and (2) experiences any of the following functional disabilities: serious difficulty seeing even with glasses (blindness/visual impairment), serious difficulty hearing (deafness/hearing impairment), serious difficulty concentrating, remembering, or making decisions due to a physical, mental, or emotional condition, and serious difficulty dressing or bathing (self-care limitation). Each domain is answered independently as a dichotomous radio response (Yes / No). No laterality, body-site, or time-window qualifier is specified in the source fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Unrelated fields (study visit stage, diabetes type, non-cancer illness timing, operation timing)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Cancer diagnosis history (any type): A CDE capturing whether the participant has ever been diagnosed with cancer of any type, as reported by a physician. The primary question is: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you had cancer (any type)?' Answer type: categorical/boolean (Yes / No). Supplementary component: multi-select checklist of specific cancer types diagnosed (e.g., bladder cancer [cct_cantp_bl], breast cancer [cct_cantp_br], and additional types), each as a binary Yes/No indicator. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified in the source fields; the concept is lifetime/ever diagnosis with no restricted time window.

conceptGroups.concept: Lifetime depression history — ever felt depressed for a whole week, number of periods, duration, and derived major depression diagnoses
conceptGroups.idealCde: CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) individual item response — Concept: Self-reported frequency of a specific depressive or psychological symptom experienced by the respondent during the past week, as measured by a single CES-D scale item (e.g., feeling bothered by things, trouble concentrating, feeling depressed, effortfulness of activities, feeling fearful). Question: 'How often during the past week did you experience [specific symptom]?' Answer type: Ordinal radio-button selection scored 0–3, where 0 = Rarely or none of the time (<1 day), 1 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 2 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 3 = All of the time (5–7 days); self-report, past-7-day reference window.
memberVariableNames: UKBB:Ever depressed for a whole week

conceptGroups.concept: Method used to complete form (EVA/ETDRS, with free-text other)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Form completion method: captures how the data collection form was completed, answering 'What method was used to complete this form?' Expected answer type is categorical (radio/enumerated), with defined values such as EVA or ETDRS, plus a free-text 'Other (please specify)' option to capture methods not listed among the predefined choices. No specific laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is implied by the source fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of circulatory/cardiovascular conditions (which blood relatives have had specific heart/blood conditions)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of circulatory/cardiovascular conditions: captures which first-degree biological relatives (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, and potentially other blood relatives) have been diagnosed with specific heart and blood conditions. The question asked is: 'Who in your family (related by blood) has had [specific circulatory condition]?' or equivalently 'Has anyone in your family ever been diagnosed with the following heart and blood conditions?' Conditions covered include congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease (including angina), heart attack (myocardial infarction), heart valve disease, aortic aneurysm, atrial fibrillation, anemia, and other circulatory conditions. Answer type: multi-select checkbox matrix — for each condition, one or more affected relative types are selected from: Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, and other blood relatives; responses are categorical (select all that apply), yielding a set of [condition × relative-type] Boolean indicators per respondent. Subject qualifier: biological family members (not self); no laterality or body-site qualifier applies.

conceptGroups.concept: Specific activity types prevented by pain or discomfort (multi-select checklist)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Pain/Discomfort Activity Limitation: Captures the extent to which pain or discomfort prevents participation in activities, including both a summary frequency/severity rating and identification of specific activity types affected. Primary question: 'How many activities does your pain or discomfort prevent?' with ordinal response options (none, a few, some, most); supplemented by a multi-select checklist or free-text enumeration of specific prevented activities (e.g., sitting, bending/crouching, handling objects, and other activities), allowing multiple responses. Answer type: composite — (1) ordinal categorical scale [none / a few / some / most] for overall activity limitation count, and (2) multi-select categorical list of specific activity types prevented, coded as binary indicators per activity domain.

conceptGroups.concept: Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary Yes/No
conceptGroups.idealCde: This source concept clusters several distinct circulatory/medical-history elements that should ideally be represented as separate CDEs: (1) Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had high blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had high blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (2) Low blood pressure lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had low blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had low blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (3) Age at first hypertension diagnosis — self-reported age category at which the participant was first told they had hypertension; question: 'About how old were you when you were first told you had hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Ordinal categorical (Child [0–11], Adolescent [12–17], Adult [18–64], Older adult [65–74], Older adult [75+]). (4) Current hypertension treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (5) Current peripheral vascular disease treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No).

conceptGroups.concept: Participant's age in completed years (numeric value)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Age at time of assessment — numeric value representing the participant's age in completed years. Question: 'What is your age?' Expected answer: integer, units = years. Note: one member field (Q3 HOW OLD ARE YOU) captures interviewer-rated accuracy of age recall rather than age itself (ordinal accuracy scale: correct / missed by 1–3 years / missed by >3 years / not attempted); this accuracy-rating variant should be treated as a distinct CDE from the direct age-value CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Currently still seeing a doctor/health care provider for a specific condition (CHF, coronary artery disease, high cholesterol, hypertension, STIs)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current Medical Management Status: A composite concept capturing whether an individual is currently under active medical care or treatment for cardiovascular and metabolic conditions, and what medications they are currently taking. Specifically addresses: (1) whether the person is currently seeing a doctor or health care provider for each of the following conditions — congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease, and high cholesterol; and (2) whether the person is currently taking any medications (prescription, over-the-counter, vitamins, or herbal supplements) not otherwise captured, along with free-text entry of medication names. Answer types: binary Yes/No radio responses for each current-care question (one per named condition); binary Yes/No radio for additional medication presence; free-text string for medication name(s). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified; subject is the self-reporting participant.

conceptGroups.concept: Heart rate in beats per minute
conceptGroups.idealCde: This source concept is heterogeneous and conflates multiple distinct measurements: (1) Heart Rate — the resting pulse rate in beats per minute (bpm), captured as a numeric value; question: 'What is the subject's heart rate?'; answer type: integer or decimal, units: beats per minute (bpm). (2) Eidon CFP Mosaic Image Creation — whether a color fundus photography mosaic image was created using the Eidon device; question: 'Was an Eidon mosaic CFP image created?'; answer type: boolean (Yes/No). (3) OD Autorefractor Axis — the axis of the refractive correction for the right eye (oculus dexter) as measured by autorefractor; question: 'What is the autorefractor-measured axis for the right eye?'; answer type: integer, units: degrees (0–180). (4) OD Autorefractor Cylinder — the cylindrical (astigmatic) refractive power for the right eye as measured by autorefractor; question: 'What is the autorefractor-measured cylinder power for the right eye?'; answer type: decimal, units: diopters (D). These should be represented as separate CDEs; no single ideal CDE can unify them.

conceptGroups.concept: Doctor-confirmed asthma diagnosis — subject, binary Yes/No
conceptGroups.idealCde: Chronic pulmonary/lung disease history and current management status: A composite domain capturing (1) lifetime diagnosis of chronic pulmonary/lung conditions (e.g., emphysema, asthma, tuberculosis, asbestosis) — binary Yes/No; (2) asthma-specific sub-elements: (a) whether the participant is currently seeing a healthcare provider for asthma — binary Yes/No, (b) age at first asthma diagnosis — ordinal categorical [Child (0–11) | Adolescent (12–17) | Adult (18–64) | Older adult (65–74) | Elderly (75+)], (c) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for asthma — binary Yes/No; and (3) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for chronic lung disease (non-asthma) — binary Yes/No. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified. The domain answers: 'Has the participant ever been diagnosed with a chronic pulmonary condition, and what is their current care and treatment status for asthma and/or chronic lung disease?' Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal radio for age-of-onset item.

conceptGroups.concept: Area-level multiple deprivation index score or domain sub-score (composite or domain-specific: income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, community safety) for small geographic areas (LSOA/WIMD)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Area-level multiple deprivation index score or domain sub-score capturing the degree of socioeconomic deprivation experienced by residents of a small geographic area (e.g., Lower Super Output Area/LSOA in England or Wales). The CDE answers: 'What is the composite or domain-specific deprivation level for this geographic area, encompassing dimensions such as income, employment, health, education, housing, environment, access to services, and community safety?' Answer type: continuous numeric score or rank (dimensionless index value or percentile rank), assigned at the small-area geographic unit level, derived from a weighted combination of domain indicators (e.g., proportion of income-deprived individuals, geographical access distances to key services including food shops, GP surgeries, primary schools, post offices, and public libraries). May be reported as an overall multiple deprivation score/rank or as individual domain scores/ranks (income deprivation, access to services deprivation, etc.) for the specified area.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of diabetes by relative type (Type 1, Type 2, other/unknown) — which relatives have been diagnosed
conceptGroups.idealCde: Diabetes family history and personal diagnosis history: captures (1) whether first-degree relatives (parents, siblings, children) have been diagnosed with Type 1, Type 2, or other/unknown diabetes — answered per relative type via yes/no or multi-select checkbox; and (2) the approximate age at which the respondent was first told they had Type 1 or Type 2 diabetes — answered via age-group categories (Child 0–11, Adolescent 12–17, Adult 18–64, Older Adult 65–74, Older Adult 75+). Answer types: binary yes/no per relative category for family history items; ordinal age-group category for self-reported age-at-diagnosis items. Qualifiers vary by field: family history fields specify the relative (parent, sibling, daughter, son); age-at-diagnosis fields specify diabetes type (Type 1 vs. Type 2) and refer to the respondent (self).

conceptGroups.concept: Electronic nicotine product / e-cigarette use — current and ever
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and nicotine product use status (self-reported, participant): A set of current and lifetime use indicators covering multiple tobacco/nicotine delivery modalities — (1) current cigarette smoking (yes/no), (2) current e-cigarette/vaping use (yes/no), (3) ever e-cigarette/vaping use (yes/no), (4) ever traditional cigar/cigarillo/filtered cigar use (yes/no), and (5) current traditional cigar/cigarillo/filtered cigar use frequency (every day / some days / not at all). Each item answers 'Does/Did the participant currently or ever use [specific product]?' Answer types are binary yes/no for ever-use and current-use items, and an ordinal frequency category (every day, some days, not at all) for current cigar use frequency; all responses are self-reported by the study participant.

conceptGroups.concept: Race/ethnicity numeric category or aggregate group variable
conceptGroups.idealCde: Hispanic/Latino Ethnicity and Ancestry Identity: Captures a person's self-reported ethnic origin and ancestry, answering 'What is your ancestry or ethnic origin, and do you identify as Hispanic, Latina/x, or of Spanish origin?' The CDE accommodates two complementary response modes: (1) a free-text field for open-ended ancestry or ethnic origin description (e.g., Italian, Jamaican, Cherokee, Korean, Nigerian), and (2) a structured multi-select checkbox for Hispanic/Latino subgroup identity with options including: No; Yes – Mexican; Yes – Puerto Rican; Yes – Cuban; Yes – Dominican Republic; Yes – Central American; Yes – South American; Yes – Chicano; Yes – Other. Answer type: composite — free-text string for ancestry narrative plus categorical multi-select enumeration for Hispanic/Latino affiliation. conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported clinician-diagnosed stroke (Yes/No)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Self-reported history of cerebrovascular events (stroke and/or transient ischemic attack [TIA/mini-stroke]) in the participant themselves, capturing: (1) presence/absence of a clinician-diagnosed stroke (Yes/No); (2) age at first diagnosis of stroke, categorized as Child (0–11), Adolescent (12–17), Adult (18–64), Older Adult (65–74), or Elderly (75+); (3) age at first diagnosis of TIA/mini-stroke, using the same ordinal age-band categories; (4) whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for stroke (Yes/No); and (5) whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for TIA/mini-stroke (Yes/No). Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal categorical age-band radio for age-at-diagnosis items. All items are self-report, first-person (subject = self).

conceptGroups.concept: Population-level percentage of adults aged 25+ with at least a high school education (area-level education statistic)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'

conceptGroups.concept: General overall health self-rating (excellent–poor scale)

Note: the source cluster also includes a related but distinct sub-concept — depth of cigarette smoke inhalation — captured as an ordinal rating (0=Not at all, 1=Slightly, 2=Moderately, 3=Deeply); this is a separate behavioral/exposure dimension within the same smoking behavior domain and should ideally be represented as its own ordinal CDE.

conceptGroups.idealCde: Chronic pulmonary/lung disease history and current management status: A composite domain capturing (1) lifetime diagnosis of chronic pulmonary/lung conditions (e.g., emphysema, asthma, tuberculosis, asbestosis) — binary Yes/No; (2) asthma-specific sub-elements: (a) whether the participant is currently seeing a healthcare provider for asthma — binary Yes/No, (b) age at first asthma diagnosis — ordinal categorical [Child (0–11) | Adolescent (12–17) | Adult (18–64) | Older adult (65–74) | Elderly (75+)], (c) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for asthma — binary Yes/No; and (3) whether currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for chronic lung disease (non-asthma) — binary Yes/No. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier is specified. The domain answers: 'Has the participant ever been diagnosed with a chronic pulmonary condition, and what is their current care and treatment status for asthma and/or chronic lung disease?' Answer types: binary radio (Yes/No) for occurrence and treatment items; ordinal radio for age-of-onset item.

conceptGroups.concept: Body Mass Index (BMI) category/classification
conceptGroups.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Restless sleep frequency (past week or recent period)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sleep disturbance / insomnia symptom burden: A composite domain capturing the frequency, severity, and quality of sleep problems including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much, assessed over a defined recent time window (past 1–4 weeks). The CDE answers: 'How often have you experienced trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much, and how does it affect your sleep quality?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale (e.g., never / rarely / sometimes / often / always, or equivalent Likert-type ratings ranging from 0–3 or 1–5), with sub-components optionally capturing: (1) frequency of sleep-onset latency >30 minutes (ordinal: never to 5–7 times/week), (2) duration of sleep difficulty (decimal, in weeks/months/years), and (3) overall sleep satisfaction (ordinal: very satisfied to very dissatisfied). No single laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; fields reflect self-reported sleep experience of the respondent across multiple instruments (CES-D restless sleep item, PHQ-9 sleep item, PSQI-style items).

conceptGroups.concept: Ophthalmic condition or procedure occurrence flag (Yes/No)

Note: member fields carry heterogeneous qualifiers spanning distinct conditions and procedures (AMD bilateral, retinal vascular occlusion bilateral, CFP mosaic imaging, BCVA, EKG); no single unified qualifier applies — each member represents a separate condition- or procedure-specific occurrence indicator with its own associated datetime.

conceptGroups.concept: Doctor-diagnosed diabetes (general, non-pregnancy)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Medical history of diagnosed health conditions: A multi-domain, provider-diagnosed condition inventory capturing whether a doctor or health care provider has ever told the respondent they have specific medical conditions across circulatory (e.g., anemia, atrial fibrillation/flutter, bleeding disorder, congestive heart failure), mental health (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety/panic disorder, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder), and metabolic/endocrine (e.g., diabetes, borderline diabetes, or high blood sugar including gestational diabetes) domains. The question asked is: 'Has a doctor or health care provider ever told you that you have [condition]?' with a pregnancy-specific variant for gestational diabetes: 'When you were pregnant, did the doctor tell you that you had diabetes, borderline diabetes, or high blood sugar?' Answer type: categorical yes/no per condition (binary: Yes/No), with multi-select checkbox format for condition-list domains; subject is the respondent (self-report); no laterality or body-site qualifier; lifetime ('ever') time window, with gestational context as a distinct qualifier for the diabetes item.

conceptGroups.concept: Doctor-diagnosed history of heart attack or myocardial infarction
conceptGroups.idealCde: Cardiovascular disease history (other/unspecified cardiac conditions): A binary indicator capturing whether an individual has a self-reported or clinician-diagnosed history of any cardiac condition not elsewhere classified, including but not limited to pacemaker implantation, heart valve disease, open heart surgery, heart attack/myocardial infarction, angina/chest pain due to heart disease, or heart transplant. The CDE answers the question: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you have, or have you ever been diagnosed with or undergone treatment for, a cardiac condition (e.g., heart attack/MI, angina, heart valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant)?' Answer type: categorical/radio; values: 1=Yes, 0=No. Note: member fields span multiple distinct cardiac conditions (MI, angina, valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant) that ideally should each be captured as separate CDEs; if a single umbrella CDE is required, it represents presence of any cardiac condition history. An optional supplementary free-text or checklist field may specify the condition type, and a date field (text/date format: YYYY-MM-DD) may capture the date of the relevant cardiac event or procedure (e.g., heart transplant date).

conceptGroups.concept: Currently seeing a doctor/health care provider for diabetes (prediabetes/type 1/type 2) (Yes/No)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Diabetes management modality assessment: a set of CDEs capturing the specific methods a person uses to manage blood glucose and A1C levels, covering five distinct treatment/management categories — (1) oral glucose-lowering medications (e.g., biguanides, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT-2 inhibitors, alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, meglitinides, bile acid sequestrants): Yes/No; (2) non-insulin injectable glucose-lowering agents (e.g., GLP-1 receptor agonists, amylin analogs): Yes/No; (3) insulin injections: Yes/No; (4) lifestyle modifications (regular exercise, dietary changes, consistent meal scheduling): Yes/No; (5) diabetes health education engagement frequency (consulting dietician, support groups, books, websites, apps): ordinal categorical — Regularly/at least monthly, Occasionally/every 2–3 months, Rarely/less than every 3 months, or Never. Each category is self-reported by the subject (self) regarding their own current diabetes management. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier applies. Categories (1)–(4) are binary Yes/No response type; category (5) is an ordered frequency scale.

conceptGroups.concept: Visual acuity under mesopic (low-light) conditions, right eye (OD): letter score and LogMAR
conceptGroups.idealCde: Visual acuity measured separately under two luminance conditions (mesopic [low-light] and photopic [standard/bright-light]) for each eye independently (right eye [OD] and left eye [OS]); answers the question 'What is the patient's visual acuity under mesopic or photopic conditions in the specified eye?'; recorded as both a raw letter score (integer count of letters read correctly, text entry) and a derived LogMAR score (continuous numeric, calculated from letter score); qualifier: laterality (OD vs OS) and luminance condition (mesopic vs photopic) are both required dimensions of each measurement instance.

conceptGroups.concept: CES-D positive affect item: past-week frequency of positive emotional state (hopeful/happy), 4-point ordinal scale
conceptGroups.idealCde: Positive affect / well-being item from the CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) positive subscale: a single self-report item asking the respondent how often during the past week they experienced a specific positive emotional state (e.g., felt hopeful about the future; felt happy). The question is framed as 'During the past week, how often did you feel [positive state]?' Answer type: ordinal 4-point frequency scale anchored to days in the past 7 days — 0 = All of the time (5–7 days), 1 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 2 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 3 = Rarely or none of the time (< 1 day). Note: the source concept cluster contains heterogeneous fields spanning positive affect (CES-D items), sexual/gender identity (closer self-description including queer, polysexual/omnisexual/sapiosexual/pansexual, asexual, two-spirit), a general overall health descriptor, and a 0–10 numeric pain intensity rating (past 7 days average); these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than a single unified element.

conceptGroups.concept: Sex/gender of the person the subject provided most assistance to (care recipient)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sex and Gender Identity — A composite concept capturing two related but distinct self-reported attributes: (1) Sex assigned at birth: the biological sex recorded at birth, answering 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' with a categorical response (Male | Female | Intersex | Other/None of these); and (2) Gender identity: the gender the participant currently identifies with, answering 'What is your current gender identity?' with a categorical response (Man/Male [including transgender men] | Woman/Female [including transgender women] | Non-binary | Genderqueer | Genderfluid | Trans man/FTM | Trans woman/MTF | Other) — ideally collected as two separate fields: one radio/select for sex assigned at birth and one multi-select checkbox for gender identity (allowing selection of a closer descriptor), both self-reported by the participant with an 'Other' or 'None of these describe me' write-in option. Answer type: categorical (enumerated codes); no units.

conceptGroups.concept: Neighborhood crime rate makes it unsafe to walk during the day (agreement rating)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability barrier perception — individual item assessing the degree to which a specific environmental or safety factor (crime rate during the day, crime rate at night, or traffic volume/unpleasantness) makes walking in the respondent's neighborhood difficult or unsafe; question asks the respondent to rate their level of agreement with a stated barrier to neighborhood walking (e.g., 'The crime rate in my neighborhood makes it unsafe to go on walks [during the day / at night]' or 'There is so much traffic on the streets that it makes it difficult or unpleasant to walk in my neighborhood'); answer type is an ordinal Likert scale with 4 response options (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with an optional non-applicable response for the traffic item (e.g., 'There are no streets or roads in my neighborhood'); qualifier varies by item: daytime crime barrier, nighttime crime barrier, or traffic/street barrier to walking — these are distinct sub-items and should not be collapsed into a single field.

conceptGroups.concept: Free-text comments/notes about contact attempt

Answers the question: 'Was this contact attempt successful, and what notes or contextual linkage apply?' Answer type: composite — boolean success indicator, boolean no-response flag, categorical form-link selection, and free-text notes fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Personal tobacco smoking status (current and past frequency)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco smoking behavior assessment: a set of related categorical items capturing multiple dimensions of an individual's smoking history and family smoking exposure. The concept encompasses: (1) Current tobacco smoking status — question 'Do you smoke tobacco now?' with response options: Yes on most or all days / Only occasionally / No; (2) Ever stopped smoking for more than 6 months (among former regular daily smokers) — question 'In the time that you smoked, did you ever stop for more than 6 months?' with response options: Yes / No; (3) Lifetime light smoking threshold (among occasional or minimal smokers) — question 'In your lifetime, have you smoked a total of at least 100 times?' with response options: Yes / No; (4) Likelihood of resuming smoking (among former regular daily smokers who previously stopped for 6+ months) — question 'Do you think you may start smoking again?' with categorical response options indicating probability of resumption; (5) Maternal smoking exposure around time of participant's birth — question 'Did your mother smoke regularly around the time when you were born?' with response options: Yes / No. Each item is a single-select categorical variable. Items 2, 3, and 4 are conditionally collected based on responses to prior items. Item 5 pertains to the participant's mother (not the participant themselves) and reflects perinatal secondhand smoke exposure. Answer type: categorical (single-select) for each sub-item; no continuous units.

conceptGroups.concept: Weekly frequency of eating beans, chicken, or fish (lean protein)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

conceptGroups.concept: Anticipated/likely reasons for future retirement (multi-select Yes/No checklist, pre-retirees)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Retirement circumstances and decision-making: A set of CDEs capturing the context and motivations surrounding an individual's retirement and, if applicable, return to work. Covers: (1) reasons contributing to the decision to retire (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (2) reasons contributing to the decision to return to work after first retirement (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (3) whether health-related retirement was due to physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both (single-select categorical: Physical health | Emotional/mental health including stress | Both); (4) whether the respondent contributed to an employer pension plan other than CPP/QPP prior to retirement (single-select categorical: Yes | No). All items are self-reported by the respondent about their own retirement experience. Answer types are binary Yes/No per factor for reason checklists, and single-select nominal categories for health-type and pension-plan items.

conceptGroups.concept: Total gross family income past 12 months (ordinal range brackets)

conceptGroups.concept: Number of standard drinks on a typical drinking day
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol Use Frequency and Quantity (AUDIT-C-style): A set of items capturing the pattern of alcohol consumption, specifically (1) how often the respondent drinks alcohol (frequency of any drinking occasion), (2) how many standard drinks they consume on a typical drinking day (typical quantity), and (3) how often they consume six or more drinks on a single occasion (heavy episodic/binge drinking frequency). Each item is answered on an ordinal frequency or quantity scale: frequency options range from 'never' through daily or almost daily (e.g., never, less than monthly/once a month or less, monthly/2–4 times a month, weekly/2–3 times a week, daily or almost daily/4+ times a week); typical quantity options are 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–9, or 10 or more standard drinks; heavy-occasion frequency options are never (in the past year/month), less than monthly, monthly, weekly, or daily or almost daily. Time window varies across member fields (past 12 months or past month). Answer type: ordinal categorical (radio/select) for each sub-item. No laterality or body-site qualifier; subject is self-report.

conceptGroups.concept: Doctor-diagnosed history of angina or chest pain due to heart disease
conceptGroups.idealCde: Cardiovascular disease history (other/unspecified cardiac conditions): A binary indicator capturing whether an individual has a self-reported or clinician-diagnosed history of any cardiac condition not elsewhere classified, including but not limited to pacemaker implantation, heart valve disease, open heart surgery, heart attack/myocardial infarction, angina/chest pain due to heart disease, or heart transplant. The CDE answers the question: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you have, or have you ever been diagnosed with or undergone treatment for, a cardiac condition (e.g., heart attack/MI, angina, heart valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant)?' Answer type: categorical/radio; values: 1=Yes, 0=No. Note: member fields span multiple distinct cardiac conditions (MI, angina, valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant) that ideally should each be captured as separate CDEs; if a single umbrella CDE is required, it represents presence of any cardiac condition history. An optional supplementary free-text or checklist field may specify the condition type, and a date field (text/date format: YYYY-MM-DD) may capture the date of the relevant cardiac event or procedure (e.g., heart transplant date).

conceptGroups.concept: Ever stopped smoking for more than 6 months (among former daily smokers)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco smoking behavior assessment: a set of related categorical items capturing multiple dimensions of an individual's smoking history and family smoking exposure. The concept encompasses: (1) Current tobacco smoking status — question 'Do you smoke tobacco now?' with response options: Yes on most or all days / Only occasionally / No; (2) Ever stopped smoking for more than 6 months (among former regular daily smokers) — question 'In the time that you smoked, did you ever stop for more than 6 months?' with response options: Yes / No; (3) Lifetime light smoking threshold (among occasional or minimal smokers) — question 'In your lifetime, have you smoked a total of at least 100 times?' with response options: Yes / No; (4) Likelihood of resuming smoking (among former regular daily smokers who previously stopped for 6+ months) — question 'Do you think you may start smoking again?' with categorical response options indicating probability of resumption; (5) Maternal smoking exposure around time of participant's birth — question 'Did your mother smoke regularly around the time when you were born?' with response options: Yes / No. Each item is a single-select categorical variable. Items 2, 3, and 4 are conditionally collected based on responses to prior items. Item 5 pertains to the participant's mother (not the participant themselves) and reflects perinatal secondhand smoke exposure. Answer type: categorical (single-select) for each sub-item; no continuous units.

conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

conceptGroups.concept: Vigorous exercise frequency in a typical week (self-reported)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical Activity Assessment: A multi-dimensional CDE capturing self-reported frequency and intensity of physical activity across multiple domains (light/home-based exercise such as stretching, calisthenics, or yoga; moderate activity such as carrying light loads, bicycling at regular pace, or doubles tennis; and vigorous activity such as hiking, jogging, heavy lifting, aerobics, or fast bicycling), as well as objective physical activity monitor data availability. The CDE answers: 'How frequently does the participant engage in physical activity at each intensity level, and was objective activity monitor data collected?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale for self-reported items (e.g., daily/almost daily, irregular/1–2 times per week, rarely/none; or days per week with duration thresholds such as ≥30 min on ≥3 days/week), binary yes/no for vigorous and moderate activity participation in the past 7 days, and binary yes/no for physical activity monitor data download status; units: categorical frequency categories or days per week, with intensity stratified into light/home-based, moderate, and vigorous tiers.

conceptGroups.concept: Number of activities prevented by pain or discomfort (ordinal: none/a few/some/most)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Pain/Discomfort Activity Limitation: Captures the extent to which pain or discomfort prevents participation in activities, including both a summary frequency/severity rating and identification of specific activity types affected. Primary question: 'How many activities does your pain or discomfort prevent?' with ordinal response options (none, a few, some, most); supplemented by a multi-select checklist or free-text enumeration of specific prevented activities (e.g., sitting, bending/crouching, handling objects, and other activities), allowing multiple responses. Answer type: composite — (1) ordinal categorical scale [none / a few / some / most] for overall activity limitation count, and (2) multi-select categorical list of specific activity types prevented, coded as binary indicators per activity domain.

conceptGroups.concept: Reasons contributing to decision to return to work after first retirement (multi-select Yes/No checklist)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Retirement circumstances and decision-making: A set of CDEs capturing the context and motivations surrounding an individual's retirement and, if applicable, return to work. Covers: (1) reasons contributing to the decision to retire (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (2) reasons contributing to the decision to return to work after first retirement (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (3) whether health-related retirement was due to physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both (single-select categorical: Physical health | Emotional/mental health including stress | Both); (4) whether the respondent contributed to an employer pension plan other than CPP/QPP prior to retirement (single-select categorical: Yes | No). All items are self-reported by the respondent about their own retirement experience. Answer types are binary Yes/No per factor for reason checklists, and single-select nominal categories for health-type and pension-plan items.

conceptGroups.concept: DASH Diet score including sodium (0-9 points)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary pattern and food preference assessment: captures both overall dietary quality (via a composite diet score) and individual food/beverage liking preferences. Specifically measures (1) adherence to a dietary pattern on a scored index (e.g., DASH Diet score including sodium, 0–9 integer points, where higher scores indicate greater adherence) and (2) hedonic liking for specific foods and beverages (diet fizzy drinks, dried fruit, fruit, grapefruit) each rated on a 9-point bipolar hedonic scale (1 = extremely dislike to 9 = extremely like, with special codes for 'never tried' and 'do not wish to answer'). Answer types: Numeric integer (diet score, range 0–9); Categorical ordinal single-select (food liking items, 9-point hedonic scale plus 'never tried' and 'do not wish to answer' response options). No specific laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; context is self-reported dietary quality and food preference.

conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported weight change compared to one year ago (gained/lost/same)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Dietary pattern stability and recent weight change: A composite concept capturing (1) self-reported directional change in body weight over the past 6 months (gained / lost / stayed the same), (2) magnitude of that weight change in pounds or kilograms over the past 6 months, (3) whether major changes to diet have occurred in the past 5 years and the reason for any such change (illness vs. other), (4) whether the participant's diet on a reference day was atypical and, if so, the reason (illness, fasting, travel/away, or other), and (5) week-to-week variability of the habitual diet (never/rarely, sometimes, often). The ideal CDE set answers the question: 'How stable is this person's diet and body weight over recent time windows (past day, past week, past 6 months, past 5 years), and what factors have driven any changes?' Answer types: (1) ordinal categorical [gained / lost / stayed the same]; (2) continuous numeric with unit kg or lb; (3) binary yes/no with categorical reason sub-field [no change / yes-illness / yes-other reason]; (4) multi-select categorical [ill / fasting / away / other untypical diet]; (5) ordinal categorical [never or rarely / sometimes / often]. No single laterality, body-site, or subject-identity qualifier is specified; the fields reflect self-report from the study participant.

conceptGroups.concept: Difficulty noticing objects to the side while walking due to eyesight
conceptGroups.idealCde: Physical functional mobility — walking ability: A CDE capturing the degree to which an individual can perform walking and related ambulatory activities (e.g., walking, climbing stairs, carrying objects) without assistance. The question asks about the presence, severity, or independence of walking/ambulation capacity. Expected answer type: ordinal categorical scale reflecting difficulty or independence level (e.g., No difficulty / A little difficulty / Moderate difficulty / Extreme difficulty / Unable; or Yes/No for unaided walking; or a graded frequency/extent scale). Note: member fields carry heterogeneous qualifiers — some assess general walking ability (unaided ambulation, yes/no), some assess difficulty with stairs and everyday physical activities, one specifically qualifies walking difficulty as attributable to eyesight (vision-related peripheral awareness while walking), and one captures fatigue-related inability to initiate movement ('get going'); these represent distinct sub-constructs (functional mobility, vision-related mobility limitation, fatigue-related initiation) that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than collapsed into one.

conceptGroups.concept: Age at marijuana use initiation
conceptGroups.idealCde: Tobacco and marijuana use history — a composite set of substance use history fields capturing: (1) lifetime cigarette use threshold (whether the respondent has smoked ≥100 cigarettes in their lifetime; binary Yes/No); (2) age at smoking initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started smoking cigarettes; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (3) total duration of cigarette smoking (number of years the respondent has smoked; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years); (4) average daily cigarette consumption (typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, expressed as an ordinal banded count in increments up to >50 cigarettes/day, with pack equivalents noted); and (5) age at marijuana use initiation (age in whole years the respondent first started using marijuana; integer years, with a capped category for >60 years). All fields are self-reported, refer to the respondent themselves, and carry no specific time-window qualifier beyond lifetime/habitual use. Answer types: binary radio for lifetime threshold; ordinal dropdown bands (integer-anchored, self-referent) for age-at-initiation and duration fields; ordinal dropdown bands with pack-equivalent annotations for daily cigarette quantity.

conceptGroups.concept: Physician care engagement and medication adherence composite score
conceptGroups.idealCde: Healthcare Utilization and Access Pattern — captures the respondent's self-reported engagement with physician care and medications, access to and affordability of a regular primary care provider, frequency of allied health therapy visits (physical, speech, respiratory, audiology, occupational therapy) in the past 12 months, frequency of delaying or forgoing care due to perceived demographic dissimilarity (race/religion) between patient and provider, and frequency of successfully seeing providers perceived as demographically similar. The concept answers: 'How does this person access, use, and experience barriers to healthcare services?' Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.

(3) Age at first hypertension diagnosis — self-reported age category at which the participant was first told they had hypertension; question: 'About how old were you when you were first told you had hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Ordinal categorical (Child [0–11], Adolescent [12–17], Adult [18–64], Older adult [65–74], Older adult [75+]). (4) Current hypertension treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (5) Current peripheral vascular disease treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No).

conceptGroups.concept: Percent of total body mass that is fat (DXA)

The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much in past 2 weeks (PHQ-9 item)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Sleep disturbance / insomnia symptom burden: A composite domain capturing the frequency, severity, and quality of sleep problems including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much, assessed over a defined recent time window (past 1–4 weeks). The CDE answers: 'How often have you experienced trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much, and how does it affect your sleep quality?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale (e.g., never / rarely / sometimes / often / always, or equivalent Likert-type ratings ranging from 0–3 or 1–5), with sub-components optionally capturing: (1) frequency of sleep-onset latency >30 minutes (ordinal: never to 5–7 times/week), (2) duration of sleep difficulty (decimal, in weeks/months/years), and (3) overall sleep satisfaction (ordinal: very satisfied to very dissatisfied). No single laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; fields reflect self-reported sleep experience of the respondent across multiple instruments (CES-D restless sleep item, PHQ-9 sleep item, PSQI-style items).

conceptGroups.concept: Doctor-diagnosed diabetes or high blood sugar during pregnancy (gestational context)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Medical history of diagnosed health conditions: A multi-domain, provider-diagnosed condition inventory capturing whether a doctor or health care provider has ever told the respondent they have specific medical conditions across circulatory (e.g., anemia, atrial fibrillation/flutter, bleeding disorder, congestive heart failure), mental health (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety/panic disorder, ADHD, autism spectrum disorder), and metabolic/endocrine (e.g., diabetes, borderline diabetes, or high blood sugar including gestational diabetes) domains. The question asked is: 'Has a doctor or health care provider ever told you that you have [condition]?' with a pregnancy-specific variant for gestational diabetes: 'When you were pregnant, did the doctor tell you that you had diabetes, borderline diabetes, or high blood sugar?' Answer type: categorical yes/no per condition (binary: Yes/No), with multi-select checkbox format for condition-list domains; subject is the respondent (self-report); no laterality or body-site qualifier; lifetime ('ever') time window, with gestational context as a distinct qualifier for the diabetes item.

conceptGroups.concept: Frequency of consuming six or more drinks on one occasion (past year)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol Use Frequency and Quantity (AUDIT-C-style): A set of items capturing the pattern of alcohol consumption, specifically (1) how often the respondent drinks alcohol (frequency of any drinking occasion), (2) how many standard drinks they consume on a typical drinking day (typical quantity), and (3) how often they consume six or more drinks on a single occasion (heavy episodic/binge drinking frequency). Each item is answered on an ordinal frequency or quantity scale: frequency options range from 'never' through daily or almost daily (e.g., never, less than monthly/once a month or less, monthly/2–4 times a month, weekly/2–3 times a week, daily or almost daily/4+ times a week); typical quantity options are 1–2, 3–4, 5–6, 7–9, or 10 or more standard drinks; heavy-occasion frequency options are never (in the past year/month), less than monthly, monthly, weekly, or daily or almost daily. Time window varies across member fields (past 12 months or past month). Answer type: ordinal categorical (radio/select) for each sub-item. No laterality or body-site qualifier; subject is self-report.

Questions addressed: (1) Whether sleep has changed (Yes/No); (2) If changed, the specific type of change — sleeping too much (hypersomnia) or trouble falling asleep (insomnia onset) (each Yes/No); (3) Whether difficulty sleeping is currently present (Yes/No); (4) The extent to which difficulty sleeping limits usual activities (not limiting / causing avoidance, reduction, or spreading out of usual activities); (5) Duration of difficulty sleeping (less than 2 weeks / 2–4 weeks / 4–12 weeks / more than 12 weeks). Answer types: categorical single-select for each sub-component; conditionally administered (items 2–5 contingent on affirmative responses to prior items). No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier specified; context is self-reported health and wellbeing.

notComputed.reason: No stage stamps WHICH rule changed a given variable. The preparation report is per-rule counts plus a per-variable before/after diff; the join between them is inferred, not recorded. Per-field rule provenance is deferred by SPEC, so this is a product-level gap rather than a switch someone can turn on.

The M7 concept-match gate is an opt-in LLM stage and this run did not enable it, so no run paid for it. It IS wired: set the run's concept_gate option and the signal arrives as a real value. Absent here means not asked, not 'no mismatch found'.

Re-adjudication is caller-invoked with an explicit list of group ids and nothing on this run invoked it, so no record is a re-split child. The pipeline never re-splits an over-merged group on its own — the coherence flag is a suggestion for a human.

records.concept: Family history of mental health and substance use conditions (blood relatives) — screening and family-member follow-up

cde.id: Family health problems psychological history type

records.idealCde: Family history of mental health and substance use conditions (blood relatives): A multi-part CDE capturing whether any blood relative has ever been diagnosed with specific mental health or substance use disorders, and if so, which family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, or other blood relative) are affected for each condition. The screening question asks whether any blood relative has ever received a diagnosis from a defined list of conditions (e.g., alcohol use disorder, anxiety reaction/panic disorder, depression, autism spectrum disorder, and others); for each condition endorsed, a follow-up question identifies which specific biological family relationship(s) carry that diagnosis. Answer type: two-tier checkbox structure — Tier 1: multi-select categorical list of mental health/substance use condition categories (select all that apply); Tier 2: for each selected condition, a multi-select categorical list of biological family member relationship types (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent, other blood relative). No laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified. Note: the source concept also includes a separate, distinct field capturing self-reported sleeping pill use in the past 2 weeks (ordinal frequency: No / A few days [<1 day/week] / Some days [1–2 days/week] / Most days [3–4 days/week] / Every day; with a 'Decline to answer' option), which carries a different qualifier (self, past-2-week window) and measures a different construct (own medication behavior) from the family history fields.

transforms.rationale: Alcohol use disorder and drug use disorder both map to 'Substance abuse (alcohol, drugs)'. Anxiety reaction/panic disorder maps to 'Anxiety/panic disorder'. Bipolar disorder maps directly. Depression maps directly. Schizophrenia is a psychotic disorder and maps to 'Other type of psychosis' as the closest available CDE value. Autism spectrum disorder has no clear CDE equivalent (not OCD/ADD, not psychosis in the traditional sense). PMI_None, PMI_DontKnow, and PMI_PreferNotToAnswer are administrative/missing-data sentinels with no CDE equivalent.

All source codes represent alcohol use/abuse reported for different family members (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, grandparent). The CDE captures the type of psychological/health problem, not the family member relationship, so all map to 'Substance abuse (alcohol, drugs)'. The family member role is encoded in the source variable name but is not a dimension of the CDE value set. Confidence is slightly below 1.0 because 'alcohol use' could theoretically be casual use rather than clinical abuse, but in a mental health history context it is reasonable to treat it as substance abuse.

All source codes encode 'AnxietyPanic' as the mental condition type, differing only in the family member role (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent). The CDE captures the condition type (not the family member relationship), so all map cleanly to 'Anxiety/panic disorder'. The family member role information is lost in this mapping but is outside the scope of the CDE's value set.

All six source codes explicitly encode 'Depression' as the mental condition, differing only in the family member role (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent). The CDE captures the condition type, not the family member relationship, so all map cleanly to 'Depression'. The family member role information is outside the scope of this CDE's value set.

No laterality, body site, or time-window qualifier is specified. Note: the source concept also includes a separate, distinct field capturing self-reported sleeping pill use in the past 2 weeks (ordinal frequency: No / A few days [<1 day/week] / Some days [1–2 days/week] / Most days [3–4 days/week] / Every day; with a 'Decline to answer' option), which carries a different qualifier (self, past-2-week window) and measures a different construct (own medication behavior) from the family history fields.

records.concept: Physician care engagement and medication adherence composite score
records.idealCde: Healthcare Utilization and Access Pattern — captures the respondent's self-reported engagement with physician care and medications, access to and affordability of a regular primary care provider, frequency of allied health therapy visits (physical, speech, respiratory, audiology, occupational therapy) in the past 12 months, frequency of delaying or forgoing care due to perceived demographic dissimilarity (race/religion) between patient and provider, and frequency of successfully seeing providers perceived as demographically similar. The concept answers: 'How does this person access, use, and experience barriers to healthcare services?' Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.
