gencde.rationale: The three CLSA source fields (TRA_MEDTPC_HRB_MCQ, TRA_MEDTPC_MED_MCQ, TRA_MEDTPC_THR_MCQ) are parallel multi-select items sharing the same stem question but each capturing a distinct driving-related topic category: health/medical conditions (HRB), medications (MED), and driving therapy/restriction recommendations (THR). These are reconciled into three canonical permissible values. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a broader healthcare utilization construct that does not align well with this narrower driving-counseling concept; the near-miss CDEs (current driving status, drowsy driving, night driving difficulty) are related but distinct. Confidence is moderate because the source fields are text-type multi-select checkboxes and the exact permissible value labels are inferred from the variable name suffixes (HRB, MED, THR) rather than from an explicit codebook; label wording should be verified against the CLSA data dictionary.

transforms.sourceVariable: UKBB:Mental health problems ever diagnosed by a professional
transforms.rationale: Most mappings are straightforward. Social anxiety (1), panic attacks (6), and agoraphobia (17) are mapped to 'Anxiety' as the closest CDE equivalent. Schizophrenia (2) could be 'Other type of psychosis' but is a distinct diagnosis from the source's separate code 3 ('Any other type of psychosis'), so 2 is left unmapped to avoid conflation. Personality disorder (4), specific phobia (5), binge-eating (13), and autism (14) have no clear CDE equivalent. Missing-data sentinels (-818, -819) are unmapped. Bulimia nervosa (12) and anorexia nervosa (16) both map to 'Anorexia or bulimia'.

records.concept: Ever seen a general practitioner (GP) for nerves, anxiety, tension, or depression
records.idealCde: Healthcare Utilization and Access Pattern — captures the respondent's self-reported engagement with physician care and medications, access to and affordability of a regular primary care provider, frequency of allied health therapy visits (physical, speech, respiratory, audiology, occupational therapy) in the past 12 months, frequency of delaying or forgoing care due to perceived demographic dissimilarity (race/religion) between patient and provider, and frequency of successfully seeing providers perceived as demographically similar. The concept answers: 'How does this person access, use, and experience barriers to healthcare services?' Answer types vary by sub-element: (1) ordinal composite score reflecting visit regularity and medication adherence (0/5/10 scale); (2) binary Yes/No for having an affordable regular primary care provider; (3) ordinal categorical count of allied health therapy visits in the past 12 months (1, 2–3, 4–5, 6–7, 8–9, or more); (4) ordinal frequency of delaying/avoiding care due to provider demographic dissimilarity (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time); (5) ordinal frequency of successfully accessing demographically similar providers (Always / Most of the time / Some of the time / None of the time). All items are self-reported by the participant about their own healthcare experiences.

All fields are self-reported, refer to the respondent themselves, and carry no specific time-window qualifier beyond lifetime/habitual use. Answer types: binary radio for lifetime threshold; ordinal dropdown bands (integer-anchored, self-referent) for age-at-initiation and duration fields; ordinal dropdown bands with pack-equivalent annotations for daily cigarette quantity.

transforms.rationale: SmokeFrequency_EveryDay, SmokeFrequency_SomeDays, and SmokeFrequency_NotAtAll map directly to CDE codes 1, 2, and 3 respectively by exact label match. PMI_DontKnow maps to CDE code 9 (Don't know/refused) as it represents the 'Don't know' portion of that combined category. PMI_PreferNotToAnswer is a refusal/opt-out response that has no distinct CDE code of its own; while it could arguably fall under code 9 ('refused'), the CDE combines 'Don't know' and 'refused' into a single code and the source treats them separately, so it is left unmapped to avoid ambiguity.

Direct semantic alignment: Daily->Every day, Occasionally->Some days, Not at all->Not at all. The source adds 30-day timeframe specificity but the conceptual meaning matches the CDE categories precisely.

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE is a composite covering three sub-fields from AI-READI (suvpstage, suvptoage, suvpdosfr). The permissible-value set is intentionally minimal because the source fields are dropdown numerics whose full integer ranges were not enumerated in the harmonized export; only the sentinel/capped values (>60 years old, >20 years, Prefer not to say) were explicitly observed. For a production CDE, each sub-field should ideally be split into three separate CDEs (age started [integer 0–98], total years [integer 0–98], days/week [integer 1–7]) with the capped and prefer-not-to-say codes as additional permissible values. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX cigar-smoking age, years smoked) were used only to inform aliases. Confidence is moderate because the composite structure and incomplete value enumeration reduce precision.

transforms.rationale: The source variable is a simple Yes/No question about e-cigarette use, while the CDE captures frequency of use (Every day, Some days, Not at all). 'No' (0) maps cleanly to 'Not at all'. 'Yes' (1) cannot be mapped because it does not distinguish between 'Every day' and 'Some days'. '777=Prefer not to say' is closest to 'Refused' in spirit, but 'Prefer not to say' is not identical to 'Refused', so it is left unmapped to avoid overconfident mapping. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:ce4676d222726#g1): 2 of 3 source codes now map.

The source variable is a simple Yes/No question about e-cigarette use, while the CDE captures frequency of use (Every day, Some days, Not at all). 'No' (0) maps cleanly to 'Not at all'. 'Yes' (1) cannot be mapped because it does not distinguish between 'Every day' and 'Some days'. '777=Prefer not to say' is closest to 'Refused' in spirit, but 'Prefer not to say' is not identical to 'Refused', so it is left unmapped to avoid overconfident mapping. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:ce4676d222726#g1): 2 of 3 source codes now map.

The first three source codes map directly by label. PMI_DontKnow aligns with 'Don't know/Not sure'. PMI_PreferNotToAnswer is closest in spirit to 'Refused' but 'Prefer not to answer' and 'Refused' carry meaningfully different connotations, so it is left unmapped rather than forced. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:ce4676d222726#g1): 5 of 5 source codes now map.

ElectricSmokeParticipant_Yes maps to 'Some days' as the best available affirmative use option since the source is binary (Yes/No) and lacks frequency granularity — 'Every day' cannot be distinguished from 'Some days' without additional data, so 'Some days' is chosen as a conservative mapping. ElectricSmokeParticipant_No maps cleanly to 'Not at all'. PMI_DontKnow maps to 'Don't know/Not sure' and PMI_PreferNotToAnswer maps to 'Refused'. Confidence is moderate due to the loss of frequency detail in the Yes->Some days mapping.

COPE_A_197 (Yes, every day) maps cleanly to 'Every day' and COPE_A_169 (Yes, some days) maps to 'Some days'. COPE_A_94 (Not currently, but in the past) and COPE_A_131 (No, never) both represent non-current use but neither aligns precisely with 'Not at all' — which typically means never/not currently used without distinguishing past use — so they are left unmapped to avoid conflating former users with never-users. The CDE lacks a 'Former user' category, and forcing both into 'Not at all' would lose meaningful clinical distinction. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:ce4676d222726#g1): 4 of 4 source codes now map.

gencde.rationale: Two source fields from AoU were harmonized into a single CDE covering both the ever-use binary item and the current-frequency ordinal item, as they jointly define the concept. Permissible values 1–2 apply to the ever-use question; values 3–5 apply to the current-frequency follow-up question (asked only of ever-users). Missing-data sentinels (Don't know, Prefer not to answer) were excluded per instructions. Near-miss PhenX CDEs on cigar inhalation and regular cigar use were retained as aliases only, as they differ in scope or phrasing. Confidence is slightly reduced because combining two logically sequential items into one CDE is a structural compromise; implementers may prefer to split into two separate CDEs.

gencde.rationale: Harmonized from CLSA (SMK_OTREG_TRM, binary yes/no with codes 1/2) and MESA (othtob1, binary yes/no with codes 1/0). Canonical coding adopts 1=Yes, 0=No to align with the MESA convention and standard binary CDE practice; CLSA code 2=No is remapped to 0. The CLSA sub-items (SMK_TYPEOT_CG_TRM=cigars, SMK_TYPEOT_CH_TRM=chewing tobacco, SMK_TYPEOT_PI_TRM=pipe, SMK_TYPEOT_PT_TRM=smokeless/snuff, SMK_TYPEOT_SM_TRM=smokeless other) are product-specific indicators sharing the same binary value domain and the same ≥6-month regular-use qualifier; they are captured here as a single umbrella CDE with the understanding that product-type sub-elements may be represented as companion CDEs. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX pipe use, tobacco exposure duration) were consulted for alias terminology only and do not match the lifetime any-other-tobacco framing.

gencde.rationale: Two source fields were harmonized: chew1c (never/former/current) and chwcur1 (used in last 30 days, yes/no). Because chwcur1 sub-classifies 'current' users by 30-day recency, the canonical value set merges both dimensions into four mutually exclusive categories: Never (chew1c=0), Former (chew1c=1), Current–Used in Last 30 Days (chew1c=2 AND chwcur1=1), and Current–Not Used in Last 30 Days (chew1c=2 AND chwcur1=0). No answer concepts beyond those observed in the source fields were introduced. The near-miss CDEs (Tobacco product used type; Tobacco current use indicator; Tobacco use duration) informed alias selection only. Confidence is modestly reduced because the two-field merge requires a derivation rule not directly encoded in either source field alone.

transforms.rationale: NEVER→Never and FORMER→Former are exact matches. CURRENT maps to CDE code 2 (Current – Used in Last 30 Days) as the closest match, but the source does not distinguish between used/not used in last 30 days, so the mapping is ambiguous between CDE codes 2 and 3; CDE code 3 is left unmapped from the source. Confidence slightly reduced due to this ambiguity.

Source is a simple Yes/No variable, while the CDE distinguishes Never, Former, Current (last 30 days), and Current (not last 30 days). Source code 0 (NO) maps reasonably to CDE 0 (Never), but this is uncertain as 'No' could mean 'not currently using' rather than 'never used'. Source code 1 (YES) cannot be mapped because it is ambiguous between CDE codes 2 and 3 (current use within or beyond last 30 days), and possibly even 1 (former). Without additional context or time-frame information, a confident mapping is impossible.

records.concept: Weekly frequency of eating fast food meals or snacks
records.idealCde: Dietary habits composite score: A multi-item ordinal assessment capturing weekly or daily frequency of consuming specific food categories (fast food meals/snacks, fruit servings, vegetable servings, lean protein sources [beans/chicken/fish], and regular-fat snack chips/crackers) to characterize overall diet quality. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

gencde.rationale: The two source fields measure overlapping but not identical constructs: AI-READI captures a composite lean protein category (beans, chicken, fish) on a 3-level weekly frequency scale, while UKBB captures beans/pulses/lentils only with a serving-count scale (quarter, half, 1, 2, 3+). Reconciliation maps UKBB 'quarter' and 'half' to a sub-1-serving sub-weekly code (code 1), UKBB '1'–'2' to code 2, and UKBB '3+' to code 3, preserving the AI-READI 'Less than 1 time' as code 0 for zero-frequency reporters and 'Prefer not to say' as code 777. The UKBB field is narrower (pulses/lentils only, conditioned on vegetable consumption) and uses serving counts rather than weekly episodes, so harmonization introduces some conceptual imprecision. The near-miss CDEs (cooked dried beans, margarine/butter, fried eggs) were used only to confirm non-overlap and inform aliases. Confidence is moderate due to the partial construct mismatch between the two source instruments.

transforms.rationale: Source codes map to CDE frequency categories by meaning: source '0' (3 or more times) -> CDE '3' (3 or more times per week); source '1' (1-2 times) -> CDE '2' (1-2 times per week); source '2' (Less than 1 time) -> CDE '0' (Less than 1 time per week); source '777' -> CDE '777' (Prefer not to say). Confidence slightly reduced because source labels omit 'per week' qualifier, but context strongly implies weekly frequency. CDE code '1' (Less than 1 serving, quarter to half serving) has no source equivalent and is unmapped.

Source code 300='3+' maps to CDE code 3 ('3 or more times per week'). Source codes 1 and 2 both map to CDE code 2 ('1–2 times per week') as they represent 1 and 2 times per week respectively. Source codes 555='half' and 444='quarter' both map to CDE code 1 ('Less than 1 serving (quarter to half serving)') as they describe partial servings. CDE code 0 ('Less than 1 time per week') and 777 ('Prefer not to say') have no corresponding source codes. Confidence is moderate because the source codes appear to conflate frequency and serving size dimensions, making some mappings interpretive.

gencde.rationale: Source fields use heterogeneous response formats: AI-READI uses an amount scale (Very little / Some / A lot), CLSA uses a frequency scale (Rarely-Never / Per Day / Per Week / Per Month / Per Year) with a companion numeric field (NUT_BTTR_NB_COM) for the count, and MESA uses a binary yes/no indicator for butter as a cooking fat. Because these formats are not directly reconcilable into a single ordinal scale without loss of information, the canonical permissible-value set preserves the distinct conceptual anchors from each source (amount, frequency, binary) as labeled codes. Implementers should note that the CLSA numeric companion field (NUT_BTTR_NB_COM) carries the quantity associated with the frequency unit and should be stored as a paired numeric variable. The 'Per Year' CLSA option is collapsed into 'Never/Rarely/Very little' (code 0) as it is functionally equivalent to rare use. The ideal CDE anchor provided was a multi-item diet composite and was used only for contextual orientation, not for value derivation. Confidence is moderate due to the heterogeneity of response formats across source instruments.

Source 0 (Rarely/Never) maps to CDE 0 (Never/Rarely/Very little). Source 1 (Per Day) maps to CDE 3 (Per Day/A lot). Source 2 (Per Week) maps to CDE 2 (Per Week). Source 3 (Per Month) maps to CDE 1 (Some/Per Month). Source 4 (Per Year) has no equivalent in the CDE value set — it falls between 'Never/Rarely' and 'Per Month' but cannot be confidently assigned to either without more context, so it is left unmapped. CDE codes 4 and 5 (butter/margarine usage yes/no) and 777 (prefer not to say) have no corresponding source options.

The source variable is a binary YES/NO question about butter/margarine/cooking fat use. CDE codes 4 and 5 directly represent 'Yes (uses butter/margarine/cooking fat)' and 'No (does not use butter/margarine/cooking fat)' respectively, making this a clean semantic match. Codes 0-3 and 777 in the CDE have no corresponding source values.

Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

gencde.rationale: Two source fields were harmonized: AI-READI diet9 uses a daily-servings frame (<1, 1–2, 3+) while MESA addqcalciumfort5 uses a general frequency frame (never/seldom, sometimes, often/always) specific to calcium-fortified juice. The canonical permissible values map these two scales ordinally (code 0 = none/rare, code 1 = moderate, code 2 = high/frequent) since the underlying construct—low vs. moderate vs. high fruit juice consumption—is equivalent across both instruments. The 'Prefer not to say' sentinel from AI-READI is retained as code 999. Confidence is moderate because the two source fields differ in beverage specificity (all fruit juice vs. calcium-fortified juice only) and temporal framing (daily servings vs. general frequency), introducing conceptual heterogeneity. Near-miss CDEs for orange/grapefruit juice frequency and calcium-fortified juice frequency were used only to inform aliases.

transforms.rationale: Source codes 0, 1, and 2 align directly with CDE frequency/serving categories. Source code 777 ('Prefer not to say') maps to CDE 999 ('Prefer not to say') despite different numeric sentinel values. The source label '2-Jan' appears to be a data formatting artifact for '1-2', matching CDE code 1.

Source codes 0 ('DOES NOT EAT THE FOOD') and 1 ('SELDOM OR NEVER') both map to CDE code 0 ('Does not eat/drink or less than 1 serving per day / Seldom or never'), as the CDE combines non-consumption and seldom/never into a single category. Source code 2 ('SOMETIMES') maps to CDE code 1 ('1–2 servings per day / Sometimes'), and source code 3 ('OFTEN OR ALWAYS') maps to CDE code 2 ('3 or more servings per day / Often or always'). No 'Prefer not to say' (999) equivalent exists in the source. Confidence slightly reduced due to the many-to-one mapping for codes 0 and 1.

gencde.rationale: Source field is MESA addqaddsalt5, a 4-level ordinal item. Each item is answered on a 3-level ordered categorical scale reflecting low, moderate, or high frequency of consumption, with response options varying by item (e.g., for fast food: less than 1 time/week, 1–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week; for fruit/vegetables: 2 or fewer servings/day, 3–4 servings/day, 5 or more servings/day; for lean proteins: less than 1 time/week, 1–2 times/week, 3 or more times/week; for snack chips/crackers: 1 time or less/week, 2–3 times/week, 4 or more times/week). Items are scored such that healthier dietary patterns receive lower numeric values and less healthy patterns receive higher values, enabling summation into a composite dietary risk score. Answer type: ordinal categorical per item; composite integer score across items.

gencde.title: 24-Hour Dietary Recall: Servings of Specific Foods (Baked Beans, Potatoes, Coleslaw, Crumble, Dried Fruit Cereal, Fried Potatoes)
gencde.definition: A categorical assessment of the number of servings of specific foods (baked beans, boiled/baked potatoes, coleslaw or mayonnaise-dressed salad vegetables, crumble topping, dried fruit in cereal, and fried/roast potatoes) consumed by a participant in the 24 hours preceding the dietary recall interview, captured as part of the UK Biobank 24-hour dietary recall module.
gencde.questionText: How many servings of [specific food item] did you have yesterday (or: did your cereal contain dried fruit)?
aliases: dietary recall vegetable and starchy food servings
UKBB diet recall specific food quantity
relatedCdes: During the past month . . . How often did you eat COOKED DRIED BEANS, such as refried beans, baked beans, bean soup, and pork and beans?
About how often did you eat Margarine or butter on vegetables, including potatoes?
During the past month . . . Not counting what you just told me about (lettuce salads, white potatoes, cooked dried beans), and not counting rice, how often did you eat OTHER VEGETABLES?
gencde.rationale: This GenCDE consolidates six distinct 24-hour dietary recall items from the UK Biobank (Oxford WebQ) that share a common ordinal serving-count response framework. The permissible-value set is reconciled from all observed answer concepts across the six source fields: quarter, half, 1, 2, 3, 3+, 4+, Yes, and Varied. Fractional servings (quarter, half) appear only in vegetable-type items; 4+ appears only for crumble; Yes/Varied appear only for the dried fruit cereal binary item. Because the source fields are item-specific (not a single composite), this CDE is best implemented as a repeating or item-keyed structure. The ideal CDE anchor describes a different construct (weekly frequency composite diet quality score) and was used only to confirm non-match. Near-miss CDEs informed aliases for cooked dried beans and potato-related items. Confidence is moderate (0.62) because the concept spans heterogeneous response scales across items that would ideally be represented as separate CDEs per food, but are grouped here per the harmonization instruction.

cde.id: Godin Leisure-Time Exercise Questionnaire - strenuous exercise per week frequency

records.idealCde: Physical Activity Assessment: A multi-dimensional CDE capturing self-reported frequency and intensity of physical activity across multiple domains (light/home-based exercise such as stretching, calisthenics, or yoga; moderate activity such as carrying light loads, bicycling at regular pace, or doubles tennis; and vigorous activity such as hiking, jogging, heavy lifting, aerobics, or fast bicycling), as well as objective physical activity monitor data availability. The CDE answers: 'How frequently does the participant engage in physical activity at each intensity level, and was objective activity monitor data collected?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale for self-reported items (e.g., daily/almost daily, irregular/1–2 times per week, rarely/none; or days per week with duration thresholds such as ≥30 min on ≥3 days/week), binary yes/no for vigorous and moderate activity participation in the past 7 days, and binary yes/no for physical activity monitor data download status; units: categorical frequency categories or days per week, with intensity stratified into light/home-based, moderate, and vigorous tiers.

records.idealCde: Physical Activity Assessment: A multi-dimensional CDE capturing self-reported frequency and intensity of physical activity across multiple domains (light/home-based exercise such as stretching, calisthenics, or yoga; moderate activity such as carrying light loads, bicycling at regular pace, or doubles tennis; and vigorous activity such as hiking, jogging, heavy lifting, aerobics, or fast bicycling), as well as objective physical activity monitor data availability. The CDE answers: 'How frequently does the participant engage in physical activity at each intensity level, and was objective activity monitor data collected?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale for self-reported items (e.g., daily/almost daily, irregular/1–2 times per week, rarely/none; or days per week with duration thresholds such as ≥30 min on ≥3 days/week), binary yes/no for vigorous and moderate activity participation in the past 7 days, and binary yes/no for physical activity monitor data download status; units: categorical frequency categories or days per week, with intensity stratified into light/home-based, moderate, and vigorous tiers.

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE aggregates heterogeneous source fields spanning three intensity domains (light/home-based: AI-READI:dmlhex; moderate: AoU:ipaq_3; vigorous: AoU:ipaq_1; walking: AoU:ipaq_5) plus objective monitor availability (AI-READI:dvamwendwnd). Frequency response options were reconciled from the AI-READI ordinal scale and AoU Yes/No IPAQ items into a single canonical set; 'Unsure' was retained from the observed answer concepts list. MESA numeric MET-min/wk fields (exercm1c, exercm5c) and ECG/cardiac fields (ecgnum5, major7a5) were excluded from the permissible-value set as they represent continuous or unrelated constructs not expressible in this categorical schema — implementers should treat those as companion numeric elements. CLSA free-text fields (PA2_EXER_MCQ, PA2_SIT_MCQ) map to frequency categories 1–3. The 7-day recall window from IPAQ is the dominant reference period. Confidence is moderate because the source fields span genuinely distinct sub-concepts (intensity levels, monitor availability) that ideally would be separate CDEs, but the harmonization brief treats them as one concept.

records.concept: Self-reported Hispanic/Latino ethnicity and ancestry origin (free-text + structured subgroup checkbox)
records.idealCde: Hispanic/Latino Ethnicity and Ancestry Identity: Captures a person's self-reported ethnic origin and ancestry, answering 'What is your ancestry or ethnic origin, and do you identify as Hispanic, Latina/x, or of Spanish origin?' The CDE accommodates two complementary response modes: (1) a free-text field for open-ended ancestry or ethnic origin description (e.g., Italian, Jamaican, Cherokee, Korean, Nigerian), and (2) a structured multi-select checkbox for Hispanic/Latino subgroup identity with options including: No; Yes – Mexican; Yes – Puerto Rican; Yes – Cuban; Yes – Dominican Republic; Yes – Central American; Yes – South American; Yes – Chicano; Yes – Other. Answer type: composite — free-text string for ancestry narrative plus categorical multi-select enumeration for Hispanic/Latino affiliation. No qualifier for subject other than self-report (respondent is the subject). No laterality or body-site qualifier applies.

transforms.rationale: numeric variable with no declared units — cannot author a unit conversion

Most source codes map cleanly to CDE values by meaning. C41222 (No) maps to Non-Hispanic or Latino. C999 (Chicano) is a term closely associated with Mexican-American identity but is not explicitly 'Mexican' per se; mapping to 'Other Hispanic/Latino/Spanish' is safer than forcing it to 2148-5. C888 (Other) maps to 'Other Hispanic/Latino/Spanish' as the best available catch-all. C777 (Prefer not to say) is a missing-data/refusal sentinel with no direct CDE equivalent and is left unmapped. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:cfb970b5bbf3b#g0): 10 of 10 source codes now map.

gencde.rationale: Both source fields (AI-READI racetrib and AoU aian_tribe) are free-text prompts capturing self-reported tribal name, enrollment, affiliation, or descent for American Indian, Alaska Native, and broader Indigenous populations. No permissible values are defined because the domain is open-ended by design; controlled vocabulary (e.g., BIA-recognized tribe list, NCAI tribal directory) may be applied post-collection for harmonization. The near-miss CDEs address race/ethnicity categorically and do not capture this granular tribal-identity narrative. The ideal anchor CDE addresses Hispanic/Latino ancestry in a related but distinct domain; tribal affiliation is retained as a separate, standalone element per standard NIH race/ethnicity data collection guidance (2024 OMB standards).

gencde.title: Age-, Gender-, and Race-Adjusted Coronary Artery Calcium Score Quantile and Non-Zero Calcium Probability (McClelland 2006)
gencde.definition: Clinically computed statistics derived from a participant's raw coronary artery calcium (CAC) score: (1) the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted quantile of the CAC score among individuals with CAC > 0 (expressed as a probability between 0 and 1, per McClelland et al., Circulation 2006), and (2) the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted probability that a participant's calcium score is non-zero, based on the same reference population and methodology.
gencde.questionText: What is the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted quantile of the participant's CAC score among those with CAC > 0, and what is the age-, gender-, and race-adjusted probability that the participant has a non-zero CAC score, as derived from McClelland et al. (Circulation 2006)?
relatedCdes: NIH Toolbox Cognitive ? Cognition crystallized composite age adjusted scale score
NIH Toolbox Cognitive ? Cognition total composition age adjusted scale score
NIH Toolbox Cognitive ? Cognition fluid composite age adjusted scale score
gencde.rationale: Two closely related numeric statistics from MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) are captured here: CACQ1C (the age/gender/race-adjusted quantile of the CAC score, restricted to participants with CAC > 0, range 0–1) and PRCACGT01C (the age/gender/race-adjusted probability of having a non-zero CAC score, range 0–1). Both are continuous probabilities on [0,1] per the McClelland et al. 2006 Circulation reference equations. They are paired clinical computed statistics rather than raw measurements, and no existing NIH CDE covers this cardiovascular imaging-derived computed statistic. The near-miss CDEs relate to age-adjusted cognitive composite scores (NIH Toolbox), which share the 'age-adjusted scale score' structural pattern but are entirely different in domain. Confidence is slightly reduced because these two sub-measures (quantile vs. probability) are conceptually distinct and could alternatively be split into two separate CDEs; they are combined here because they share the same reference methodology, population, and value domain.

records.concept: Body Mass Index (BMI) numeric value (kg/m²)
records.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

records.concept: Assumed percent of lean body mass that is water
records.idealCde: Body composition metric expressed as a ratio or proportion of total body mass or a body mass index calculation — captures quantitative measures of body composition (e.g., BMI, percent body fat, lean body mass water fraction) or body weight, as well as the unit of measurement associated with a dose or quantity value. The concept spans: (1) a calculated or measured body composition value (BMI as kg/m², percent total body fat as %, assumed percent of lean body mass that is water as %, or body weight in kilograms); and (2) a categorical dose/quantity unit selector for concomitant medication or treatment. Because the member fields carry fundamentally different qualifiers and measurement contexts — anthropometric/body-composition indices (BMI, % body fat, % LBM water, weight in kg) versus a pharmacological dose unit (mg, mL, capsule, etc.) — these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be separated: one CDE for body composition/anthropometric value (numeric, continuous; units: kg for weight, kg/m² for BMI, % for proportional measures) and one CDE for concomitant medication dose unit (categorical dropdown; values: percent volume per volume, capsule, gram, inhalation, international dosing unit, liter per hour, liter per minute, milligram, milligram per kilogram, milliliter, milliliter per hour, milliliter per kilogram, puff, spray). As a single harmonized element these fields are heterogeneous and should not be collapsed into one CDE.

gencde.title: DXA Assumed Percent of Lean Body Mass That Is Water
gencde.definition: The assumed percentage of lean body mass composed of water, as derived from dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) body composition analysis, used as a fixed physiological constant or region-specific estimate in hydration and body composition calculations.
gencde.questionText: What is the assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water, as estimated from DXA body composition analysis?
relatedCdes: Dual X-ray absorptiometry whole body total lean value

gencde.rationale: All three source fields (DXA_AGC_WATER_LBM_COM, DXA_OI_WATER_LBM_COM, DXA_WBC_WATER_LBM_COM) from the CLSA cohort are decimal-typed and share an identical definition, differing only by anatomical region (whole body composition, osteoporosis index region, and age-gender-corrected region). The GenCDE abstracts across these regional variants into a single numeric element with percent units. The value is typically a physiological constant near 73% in standard DXA software but is retained as a continuous numeric field to accommodate software- or region-specific variation. Near-miss CDEs (DXA whole body lean value, BMI value, BMI category) were used only to inform alias vocabulary and confirm non-overlap. No categorical permissible values are warranted given the continuous decimal source type.

gencde.rationale: Sourced exclusively from MESA variable wtmodp5. The concept is a quality-control/data-integrity flag indicating whether the standard operating procedure for weight measurement was altered (e.g., participant unable to remove shoes, used wheelchair scale). Near-miss CDEs (Body weight Measured; Body weight; Body weight Stated) capture the weight value itself, not the protocol modification status. memberDetails.text: Indicates whether weight was entered into the machine directly or manually, whether weight was only measured manually or not performed

transforms.rationale: Code 1 (Direct entry) likely refers to direct/automated measurement, mapped to 'Measured'. Code 3 (Manual measurement of weight only) is a physical measurement, mapped to 'Measured'. Code 2 (Manual entry of full results) suggests the subject or a proxy entered results themselves without direct measurement in context, most closely aligned with 'Self-reported', though this is uncertain. Codes 4 (Not performed) and -1 (Question not asked) have no equivalent in the CDE value set and are left unmapped. Confidence is moderate due to ambiguity in code 2. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:ca71389fc5ed3#g7): 5 of 5 source codes now map.

records.idealCde: CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) individual item response — Concept: Self-reported frequency of a specific depressive or psychological symptom experienced by the respondent during the past week, as measured by a single CES-D scale item (e.g., feeling bothered by things, trouble concentrating, feeling depressed, effortfulness of activities, feeling fearful). Question: 'How often during the past week did you experience [specific symptom]?' Answer type: Ordinal radio-button selection scored 0–3, where 0 = Rarely or none of the time (<1 day), 1 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 2 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 3 = All of the time (5–7 days); self-report, past-7-day reference window.

gencde.title: Lifetime History of Depressed Mood Lasting at Least One Week
gencde.definition: Self-reported indicator of whether an individual has ever experienced a period of feeling depressed or down lasting at least one continuous week at any point in their lifetime, serving as the gateway criterion for further characterization of depressive episode frequency, duration, and derived major depression diagnoses.
gencde.questionText: Looking back over your life, have you ever had a time when you were feeling depressed or down for at least a whole week?
aliases: Ever depressed for a whole week
sourceVariables: UKBB:Ever depressed for a whole week
UKBB:Single episode of probable major depression
relatedCdes: Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless in last 2 weeks [Reported.PHQ]
Patient Health Questionnaire Depression (PHQ) - Depressed score
Center for Epidemiologic Studies-Depression Scale (CES-D) - depressed indicator
gencde.rationale: The concept spans five UKBB fields: a binary gateway question (F4598), two numeric follow-up fields (longest episode duration in weeks, F4609; number of episodes, F4620), and two derived categorical flags (single-episode probable major depression; recurrent moderate probable major depression). Because the IDEAL CDE anchor is a CES-D past-week symptom item and the near-miss CDEs are PHQ/CES-D current-symptom measures, this GenCDE is intentionally scoped to the lifetime binary gateway construct — the only answer concepts observed across all harmonized source fields are Yes and No. The numeric sub-fields (duration, episode count) and derived diagnosis flags are treated as companion elements rather than merged here, to preserve semantic precision. Missing-data sentinels (-1 Do not know, -3 Prefer not to answer) are excluded from the permissible-value set per instructions. Confidence is moderate (0.72) because the concept conflates a self-report screen with algorithmically derived clinical diagnoses, and no single authoritative NIH CDE or ontology term fully captures this composite lifetime construct.

gencde.rationale: Source field is UKBB 'Method of measuring blood pressure' (categorical single). Two sentinel/administrative codes from the source (-1=Question not asked due to previous answers) were collapsed into a single 'Not performed' category (code 4) as both represent absence of a valid measurement rather than a substantive answer concept; the -1 sentinel was dropped per schema instructions to exclude missing-data sentinels. 'Manual sphygmometer' label was standardised to 'Manual sphygmomanometer' (correct clinical spelling) while preserving the original concept. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a paired systolic/diastolic seated BP measurement, which is a related but distinct concept; this CDE captures only the collection-method qualifier. records.concept: Gender identity of subject/participant
records.idealCde: Sex and Gender Identity — A composite concept capturing two related but distinct self-reported attributes: (1) Sex assigned at birth: the biological sex recorded at birth, answering 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' with a categorical response (Male | Female | Intersex | Other/None of these); and (2) Gender identity: the gender the participant currently identifies with, answering 'What is your current gender identity?' with a categorical response (Man/Male [including transgender men] | Woman/Female [including transgender women] | Non-binary | Genderqueer | Genderfluid | Trans man/FTM | Trans woman/MTF | Other) — ideally collected as two separate fields: one radio/select for sex assigned at birth and one multi-select checkbox for gender identity (allowing selection of a closer descriptor), both self-reported by the participant with an 'Other' or 'None of these describe me' write-in option. Answer type: categorical (enumerated codes); no units.

transforms.rationale: Man maps to Male; Woman maps to Female; Non-binary and Other both map to 'Other, specify' as the CDE has no dedicated non-binary category. '777=Prefer not to say' is a missing-data/refusal sentinel with no equivalent CDE value, so it is unmapped (closest might be Unknown but 'prefer not to say' is a deliberate refusal rather than truly unknown identity).

Trans man (FTM) maps to Male and Trans woman (MTF) maps to Female as these align with affirmed gender identity conventions. Genderqueer, Genderfluid, Gender variant, Two-spirit, and 'None of these/specify' all map to 'Other, specify' as the CDE has no non-binary categories. 'Questioning or unsure' maps to 'Unknown'. Note: mapping Trans man→Male and Trans woman→Female is a common convention but context-dependent; confidence is moderate because the CDE's binary Male/Female may not fully capture transgender nuance, and Two-spirit is technically a sexuality/cultural identity code that was included here.

Man->Male and Woman->Female are direct matches. Non-binary, Transgender, and 'None of these/additional options' all map to 'Other, specify' as the CDE lacks dedicated codes for these identities. 'Prefer not to answer' is mapped to 'Unknown' as the closest available CDE code, though it conflates non-response with true unknown — this is a semantic compromise. Confidence is moderate due to the lossy collapsing of Non-binary and Transgender into 'Other, specify' and the imperfect mapping of prefer-not-to-answer to Unknown.

'888=Other' and '777=Prefer not to say' have no CDE equivalent; they are not the same as 'Unknown' (which implies missing/unavailable data rather than a known non-binary status or refusal). Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c3a693f1530ff#g1): 4 of 5 source codes now map.

F maps to Female and M maps to Male directly. Intersex (I) has no equivalent in the CDE value set (Male/Female/Unknown); it is a distinct biological category that should not be collapsed into Unknown without domain guidance. 99 (Not Available) is a missing-data sentinel with no clear CDE equivalent beyond Unknown, but mapping a 'not available' code to 'Unknown' could conflate missingness with true unknown sex, so it is left unmapped pending domain guidance. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c3a693f1530ff#g1): 3 of 4 source codes now map.

Male and Female map directly. Intersex has no equivalent in the CDE value set (Unknown could be argued but Intersex is a distinct biological category, not truly unknown). 'None of these describe me' and 'Prefer not to answer' are refusal/other options with no direct CDE equivalent; mapping them to Unknown would misrepresent their meaning. gencde.definition: The biological sex of the primary care recipient — the person to whom the caregiver subject provided the most assistance.
gencde.questionText: Is the person to whom you provided the most assistance male or female?
aliases: gender of person receiving most assistance
relatedCdes: Has this person done any of the following for you or helped you out [PhenX]
When considering all of the support resources you have been exposed to, is there one that stands out as being the most helpful to you so far?
Section generator PhenX
gencde.rationale: Both CLSA source fields (CAG_GNDR_COM and CAG_GNDR_TRM) use identical wording and identical two-value response sets (1=Male, 2=Female), indicating a straightforward binary sex variable as reported by the caregiver about their primary care recipient. The question wording uses 'male or female,' reflecting biological sex rather than gender identity; only two answer concepts were observed across all source fields, so no additional permissible values (e.g., Intersex, Non-binary) are introduced. The near-miss CDEs relate to caregiver support resources and social support inventories, not to care recipient demographics, and were used only to confirm non-overlap. Confidence is slightly reduced from maximum because the source instrument conflates 'sex' and 'gender' in its question wording, and the binary framing may not capture all biological sex categories.

records.idealCde: Current employment status of the participant (self-reported): captures the individual's present work situation by asking 'What is your current employment status?' Allows selection of one or more categories from a standardized set including: Employed for wages (part-time or full-time), Self-employed, Out of work for 1 year or more, Out of work for less than 1 year, Homemaker, Student, Retired, and Unable to work. Answer type: multi-select categorical (checkbox); values are mutually exclusive categories but multiple selections permitted. Qualifier: current status, self-report, participant (not proxy). Note: source concept also includes related but distinct fields — a binary current employment indicator (yes/no paid work including part-time/seasonal/contract), a work street address (work-site qualifier), and a longest-held job pay type (paid employee/self-employed/unpaid family worker, career retrospective) — which represent separate CDEs and should not be collapsed into this current-status element.

transforms.rationale: Several mappings are ambiguous: COPE_A_106 says 'part-time or full-time' but the CDE splits these; mapped to part-time as a conservative choice but full-time is equally plausible — ideally this source code should be split. COPE_A_186 (self-employed) could be part-time or full-time; mapped to part-time as a placeholder but is uncertain. COPE_A_50 (student) mapped to full-time student as default, but part-time is possible. COPE_A_128 (unable to work/disabled) has no direct CDE equivalent; 'Other specify' is the closest available option. COPE_A_30 (prefer not to answer) is a missing-data sentinel with no CDE equivalent and is left unmapped. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:cb5fc531f5c6c#g0): 9 of 9 source codes now map.

gencde.rationale: Source field (AoU employment_employmentworkaddress) presents this as a radio-type input with two options: free-text address entry and 'Prefer not to answer'. The canonical permissible-value set collapses to a free-text entry field (data_type: text) because the only substantive answer concept observed is an open address entry; 'Prefer not to answer' is a missing-data sentinel excluded per instructions. The near-miss CDEs (Participant Street Address, Full Residential Address) are residential rather than occupational, confirming this is a distinct work-site concept. Confidence is moderate (0.72) because only one source cohort contributed data and the concept is a free-text address rather than a structured categorical element, limiting harmonization validation.

gencde.title: Number of People Known Personally Through Work or School (Social Network Size)

gencde.rationale: Two source fields from CLSA (one integer, one decimal) both capture the same construct; the canonical representation is numeric with a minimum of 0 and no defined upper bound, consistent with open-ended social network enumeration. Near-miss CDEs (NHANES III telephone contact frequency, work/class acquaintances) are related but distinct: they capture contact frequency or a broader acquaintance category rather than a named-person count restricted to the work/school context. No permissible-value set is applicable for this continuous count variable.

gencde.title: Employment Status Changed Since Exam 1 Indicator
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether the participant's employment status has changed since their Exam 1 assessment, as self-reported at a subsequent examination visit.
gencde.questionText: Has your employment status changed since Exam 1?
relatedCdes: Employment Status - Specify
Employment Specify Other Status
Parent's Employment Specify Other Status
gencde.rationale: Concept is a longitudinal change indicator (relative to Exam 1 baseline), not a cross-sectional employment status measure. Both source fields (MESA empstat2 and empstat3) share identical label and value coding (0=No, 1=Yes), confirming a clean binary canonical set. The near-miss CDEs capture employment status category or free-text specification and are distinct from this change-since-baseline concept. The ideal CDE anchor describes current employment status categories (multi-select), which is a related but different construct; aliases were not drawn from it. Confidence is high given full agreement across source fields and unambiguous binary coding.

gencde.title: Employment Status at Exam 5 (Yes/No Indicator)
gencde.definition: A binary self-reported indicator of whether the participant was employed (for wages or self-employed) at the time of Exam 5, coded as Yes or No.
gencde.questionText: Are you currently employed at Exam 5?
relatedCdes: Employment Status - Specify
Employment Specify Other Status
Parent's Employment Specify Other Status
gencde.rationale: Source field MESA:empstat5 encodes employment status as a binary yes/no indicator at Exam 5, collapsing the richer multi-select categorical structure described in the ideal CDE (which includes employed, self-employed, out of work, homemaker, student, retired, unable to work) into a single employed/not-employed dichotomy. The canonical permissible-value set is therefore restricted to the two answer concepts actually observed (YES=1, NO=0). Near-miss CDEs ('Employment Status - Specify', 'Employment Specify Other Status', 'Parent's Employment Specify Other Status') were used only to inform aliases and confirm non-match. Confidence is moderate because the binary collapse loses granularity relative to standard employment-status CDEs, and the exam-visit qualifier (Exam 5) is cohort-specific to MESA.

gencde.rationale: Concept is derived solely from the UK Biobank field capturing the date an email invitation to an online occupational health questionnaire was sent to participants. The data type is Date (no permissible values or numeric range apply). The near-miss CDEs (RFQ occupation text, OT therapist name, OT focus area) are structurally and semantically distinct and were used only to confirm no existing CDE covers this administrative date concept. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes employment status content, which is the downstream questionnaire topic, not the administrative invitation date itself; confidence is slightly reduced because this is an administrative/process variable rather than a clinical measurement, and generalizability beyond UKBB-style cohort studies may be limited.

Allows selection of one or more categories from a standardized set including: Employed for wages (part-time or full-time), Self-employed, Out of work for 1 year or more, Out of work for less than 1 year, Homemaker, Student, Retired, and Unable to work. Answer type: multi-select categorical (checkbox); values are mutually exclusive categories but multiple selections permitted. Qualifier: current status, self-report, participant (not proxy). Note: source concept also includes related but distinct fields — a binary current employment indicator (yes/no paid work including part-time/seasonal/contract), a work street address (work-site qualifier), and a longest-held job pay type (paid employee/self-employed/unpaid family worker, career retrospective) — which represent separate CDEs and should not be collapsed into this current-status element.

transforms.rationale: Source age bands do not align with CDE age bands. Child (0-11) straddles CDE codes 1 and 2; Adolescent (12-17) straddles codes 2 and 3; Adult (18-64) straddles codes 3, 4, and 5 — none can be mapped to a single CDE code without loss of precision. Only Older adult (65-74) and Elderly (75+) both fall cleanly within CDE code 6 (65+), though they are collapsed into one target code. Confidence is moderate-low due to the many-to-one collapse at the high end and inability to map the majority of source codes. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c12c0a9077bbf#g3): 5 of 5 source codes now map.

gencde.title: Time to Stroke Event or Censoring from Study Baseline (Days)
gencde.definition: The number of days elapsed from study enrollment (baseline) to the occurrence of a stroke event, or to the last follow-up date for participants who did not experience a stroke during the study period (censored observation), as used in time-to-event (survival) analyses.
gencde.questionText: How many days elapsed from the participant's study start date to the date of first stroke event, or to the date of censoring if no stroke occurred during follow-up?
relatedCdes: Adverse Event Study Intervention Date and Time
Cardiovascular event after spinal cord lesion date and time
Consensus on Grading Intracranial Flow Obstruction (COGIF) - follow-up date and time
gencde.rationale: Sourced from MESA ESP_stroke_tte_or_censor, a standard survival-analysis time variable (days from baseline). The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a categorical self-report instrument (presence/absence, age bands, treatment), which is a distinct but related concept; the GenCDE is scoped strictly to the numeric time-to-event quantity actually observed in the source field. Maximum value is left null because it is cohort-duration-dependent (no universal upper bound). Near-miss CDEs (adverse event dates, COGIF follow-up) were used only to confirm non-overlap and inform alias terminology. UCUM unit 'd' (day) aligns with the source field's stated unit of days.

gencde.rationale: Source field AI-READI:icf_consent is a radio-button item capturing affirmative agreement after full form review. gencde.rationale: This is a hybrid numeric/categorical element: the primary response is an integer age in years (minimum 3, maximum = participant's current age at assessment), with a single categorical override for participants who report never having had sexual intercourse. Sentinel codes for 'Do not know' and 'Prefer not to answer' observed in the UKBB source field are treated as missing-data sentinels and excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. A confirmation prompt is recommended when the reported value is less than 12. The upper bound is left null because it is participant-age-dependent. Near-miss CDEs (hearing difficulty onset age, menarche age, kidney failure diagnosis age) share the 'age at first event' structure and inform the question phrasing pattern but represent distinct concepts.

gencde.title: Ever Had Same-Sex Sexual Intercourse (Lifetime)
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether the participant has ever engaged in sexual intercourse (defined as vaginal, oral, or anal intercourse) with a person of the same sex at any point in their lifetime, as self-reported by the participant.
gencde.questionText: Have you ever had sexual intercourse with someone of the same sex?
aliases: ever had sex with same-sex partner
relatedCdes: How many times in the last year have you been paid for having sexual relations with someone [Denver Youth Survey]
How many times in the last year have you had or tried to have sexual relations with someone against their will (other than events you just mentioned)?
Over the past 4 weeks when you attempted sexual intercourse, how often were you able to penetrate - enter your partner [PhenX]
gencde.rationale: The source fields span two distinct but related sexual history constructs from UK Biobank (UKBB F2159 and F2149). The IDEAL CDE anchor describes age at first intercourse (numeric), but the observed answer concepts across all source fields are strictly binary (Yes/No), corresponding to the same-sex intercourse item (F2159). The lifetime number of sexual partners field (F2149) is integer-valued but its only observed answer concepts submitted for reconciliation are Yes and No; no numeric partner-count values were included in the ANSWER CONCEPTS list, so no numeric permissible values are authored here. Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer) are excluded per instructions. This element should only be administered to participants who have previously confirmed ever having had sexual intercourse. Near-miss CDEs relate to paid sex frequency, non-consensual sex, and erectile penetration ability — all distinct constructs retained only for relational context.

memberDetails.id: UKBB:Length of time at current address
memberDetails.name: Length of time at current address
memberDetails.text:
ACE touchscreen question "How many years have you lived at your current address?"

The following checks were performed:

  • If answer < 1 then rejected
  • If answer > Participants age then rejected

If the participant activated the Help button they were shown the message:
If you have lived there for less than one year select Less than a year.
If you are unsure, please provide an estimate or select Do not know.
If you have lived at your current address at different times, add up
the total number of years you lived there. For instance if you lived
at your current address for 3 years, moved overseas for one year and
returned to your current address for another 5 years, then you would
enter 8 years.

gencde.rationale: This is a multi-select categorical element derived from two UKBB touchscreen fields (main assessment and pilot). Codes 1–8 represent distinct supplement types observed across both source fields; synonymous entries (e.g., Iron appearing in both fields with different codes) were merged into a single canonical code. memberDetails.name: Type of accommodation lived in
memberDetails.text:
ACE touchscreen question "What type of accommodation do you live in?"

If the participant activated the Help button they were shown the message:
Please select:

A house or bungalow for any whole, detached, semi-detached
or terraced (including end-terrace) house or bungalow.

A flat, maisonette, or apartment for any purpose-built
block of flats or tenement, part of a converted or shared
house (including bed-sits) or within a commercial building
(for example in an office building, or hotel, or over a shop).

If none of the options apply, select None of the above.

transforms.rationale: 1 maps to 'House, detached' (bungalow/house best fits detached; no semi-detached distinction available). 2 maps to 'Apartment' (flat/maisonette/apartment). 3 maps to 'Mobile home' (mobile/temporary structure is closest match, though caravan is not identical). 5 maps to 'Nursing home' (care home is closest equivalent). Code 4 (sheltered accommodation) is a supported-living arrangement not cleanly matching any CDE option. Codes -7 and -3 are non-substantive/missing-data sentinels with no CDE equivalent. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c64033417b97c#g13): 7 of 7 source codes now map.

gencde.rationale: Source is the UK Biobank pilot touchscreen questionnaire (field on progestogen-only oral contraceptive type). memberDetails.name: Cancer code, self-reported
memberDetails.text: Code for cancer. If the participant was uncertain of the type of cancer they had had, then they described it to the interviewer (a trained nurse) who attempted to place it within the coding tree. If the cancer could not be located in the coding tree then the interviewer entered a free-text description of it. These free-text descriptions were subsequently examined by a doctor and, where possible, matched to entries in the coding tree. Free-text descriptions which could not be matched with very high probability have been marked as "unclassifiable".

transforms.rationale: The source variable is a binary Yes/No indicator (likely 'does the patient have cancer?') and does not encode a specific cancer type. Neither '1' (Yes) nor '0' (No) can be mapped to any specific cancer type in the CDE value set. All source codes are unmapped.

Most specific cancer types map cleanly to CDE values. 1008 (ear cancer) and 1009 (sinus cancer) are partially covered by Nasal Cavity and Paranasal Sinus Cancer but ear cancer has no direct CDE equivalent. 1020 (large bowel/colorectal) is ambiguous between Colon and Rectal Cancer. 1025 (gallbladder/bile duct) combines two CDE entries. 1029-1033 (nerve/brain/spinal) lack precise CDE matches. 1031 (meningioma) and 1033 (spinal/cranial nerve) have no direct CDE equivalent. 1036/1037/1038 are umbrella categories. 1062 (squamous cell carcinoma) is not specifically listed. 1067 (adrenal cancer) maps to Adrenocortical Carcinoma only partially. 1070/1071/1072/1073/1085/1086 have no clear CDE equivalents. 1078 (tonsil) could be Oropharyngeal but is uncertain. 1080 (trachea) is not in CDE. 1082 (heart/mediastinum) partially maps to Cardiac Tumors but mediastinum is not covered. 1084 is too broad. Negative-coded grouping codes are not mappable to single CDE values.

transforms.rationale: The CDE specifically asks about parental history of asthma (mother/father). Mother and Father source codes map to Yes (1) when asthma is present for that parent. Sibling, Daughter, Son, and Grandparent are not parents and cannot be mapped to this CDE. The No (0) and Don't know (9) CDE values cannot be mapped because the source codes only represent presence of the condition (affirmative flags), not absence or uncertainty — those states would need to be inferred from the absence of these flags in the source data rather than explicit codes. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c9dcc02d43ed6#g4): 8 of 8 source codes now map.

cde.id: Do your legs hurt when you walk [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication screening): a structured assessment capturing the presence, characteristics, and behavior of leg or buttock pain during walking. Answers the questions: (1) Does the subject experience pain in the leg or buttock while walking? (Yes/No); (2) Does the pain include the calf/calves? (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves); (3) Does the leg pain ever disappear while continuing to walk? (Yes/No); (4) On which side is the leg pain predominant? (Right | Left | Both); (5) Does leg pain occur when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground? (Yes/No). Answer type: categorical/binary responses per sub-item, collectively forming a standardized claudication symptom questionnaire (consistent with Rose/Edinburgh Claudication Questionnaire methodology). No units; responses are nominal/ordinal coded values.

Both source codes indicate leg pain when walking — code 1 specifies calf involvement and code 2 specifies pain not including the calf. Both map to 'Yes' for the CDE question 'Do your legs hurt when you walk.' There is no source code representing absence of pain, so 'No' has no mapping. Confidence is moderate because the source appears to be a follow-up question (sub-classifying pain location) rather than a yes/no pain screener, meaning these codes may only appear in a subset already confirmed to have pain.

The source variable captures which leg(s) are affected (right, left, both), presupposing pain is already present. It does not map to a Yes/No question about whether legs hurt when walking. All three source codes imply 'Yes' in some sense, but none can be cleanly mapped to the CDE's binary Yes/No without losing critical information or making unsupported assumptions. All codes are left unmapped.

The source variable captures duration of walking (10 minutes or less vs. more than 10 minutes), which appears to be a follow-up question about how long one can walk, not a yes/no answer to whether legs hurt when walking. Neither source code maps to Yes or No for the CDE question. Both codes are unmapped.

records.concept: Leg and/or foot numbness (Michigan Neuropathy Screening Instrument item)

cde.id: Are your legs and/or feet numb?

records.idealCde: Exertional leg/buttock pain (claudication screening): a structured assessment capturing the presence, characteristics, and behavior of leg or buttock pain during walking. Answers the questions: (1) Does the subject experience pain in the leg or buttock while walking? (Yes/No); (2) Does the pain include the calf/calves? (Pain includes calf/calves | Pain does not include calf/calves); (3) Does the leg pain ever disappear while continuing to walk? (Yes/No); (4) On which side is the leg pain predominant? (Right | Left | Both); (5) Does leg pain occur when walking at an ordinary pace on level ground? (Yes/No). Answer type: categorical/binary responses per sub-item, collectively forming a standardized claudication symptom questionnaire (consistent with Rose/Edinburgh Claudication Questionnaire methodology). No units; responses are nominal/ordinal coded values.

cde.id: Are you now taking diabetic pills to lower your blood sugar [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Diabetes management modality assessment: a set of CDEs capturing the specific methods a person uses to manage blood glucose and A1C levels, covering five distinct treatment/management categories — (1) oral glucose-lowering medications (e.g., biguanides, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT-2 inhibitors, alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, meglitinides, bile acid sequestrants): Yes/No; (2) non-insulin injectable glucose-lowering agents (e.g., GLP-1 receptor agonists, amylin analogs): Yes/No; (3) insulin injections: Yes/No; (4) lifestyle modifications (regular exercise, dietary changes, consistent meal scheduling): Yes/No; (5) diabetes health education engagement frequency (consulting dietician, support groups, books, websites, apps): ordinal categorical — Regularly/at least monthly, Occasionally/every 2–3 months, Rarely/less than every 3 months, or Never. Each category is self-reported by the subject (self) regarding their own current diabetes management. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier applies. Categories (1)–(4) are binary Yes/No response type; category (5) is an ordered frequency scale.

gencde.questionText: How often would you say that you engage in diabetes health education? gencde.rationale: Derived from a single source field (AI-READI:dmledu). Original numeric codes (0, 5, 10, 777) are preserved as they carry ordinal meaning and are used in the source instrument; 777 is a non-response sentinel retained as a permissible value per source convention rather than treated as missing, because the concept explicitly includes patient preference to not disclose. Near-miss CDEs (dietician consult count, medical office visit count) are related but capture specific visit counts rather than self-reported engagement frequency across multiple education modalities. The concept aligns with DSME/S (Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support) constructs in the ADA Standards of Care.

gencde.questionText: Are you still seeing a doctor or health care provider for diabetes (prediabetes, type 1 diabetes, or type 2 diabetes)?
relatedCdes: Doctor or health care professional ever told you that you have diabetes
Medical office visit diabetes past year count
Are you taking medicine for diabetes [PhenX]
gencde.rationale: Three AoU source fields (prediabetes, type 1, type 2) each ask the same binary question about current provider engagement; they are harmonized into a single binary CDE covering all diabetes subtypes. The near-miss CDEs address ever-diagnosis, visit counts, and medication use — distinct constructs. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes management modality detail (medications, lifestyle), which is a related but separate concept; this CDE captures only the binary provider-contact status. Permissible values are restricted to Yes/No as observed across all source fields; missing-data sentinels were excluded per instructions.

records.concept: Currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for diabetes (prediabetes/type 1/type 2) (Yes/No)

cde.id: Medication diabetic current former take indicator

records.idealCde: Diabetes management modality assessment: a set of CDEs capturing the specific methods a person uses to manage blood glucose and A1C levels, covering five distinct treatment/management categories — (1) oral glucose-lowering medications (e.g., biguanides, sulfonylureas, thiazolidinediones, DPP-4 inhibitors, SGLT-2 inhibitors, alpha-glucosidase inhibitors, meglitinides, bile acid sequestrants): Yes/No; (2) non-insulin injectable glucose-lowering agents (e.g., GLP-1 receptor agonists, amylin analogs): Yes/No; (3) insulin injections: Yes/No; (4) lifestyle modifications (regular exercise, dietary changes, consistent meal scheduling): Yes/No; (5) diabetes health education engagement frequency (consulting dietician, support groups, books, websites, apps): ordinal categorical — Regularly/at least monthly, Occasionally/every 2–3 months, Rarely/less than every 3 months, or Never. Each category is self-reported by the subject (self) regarding their own current diabetes management. No laterality, body-site, or address qualifier applies. Categories (1)–(4) are binary Yes/No response type; category (5) is an ordered frequency scale.

records.concept: Respondent's highest grade or level of school completed / highest degree received (self-reported educational attainment)

cde.id: What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed or the highest degree you have received [NHANES]

records.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'

transforms.targetCdeId: What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed or the highest degree you have received [NHANES]
transforms.rationale: All source codes map directly to CDE codes. Grades 0-21 are identical in meaning. Source 777 (Prefer not to say) maps to CDE 77 (Refused) as the closest equivalent for a refusal/opt-out response. Source 555 (Don't know) maps to CDE 99 (Don't know). Minor wording differences in degree descriptions (e.g., BBA added in source for Bachelor's) do not affect the conceptual alignment.

transforms.targetCdeId: What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed or the highest degree you have received [NHANES]
transforms.rationale: Several source codes span multiple CDE grades and cannot be mapped to a single CDE code without ambiguity. HighestGrade_NeverAttended maps cleanly to CDE 0. HighestGrade_TwelveOrGED maps to CDE 13 (High school graduate) as the best single match, though it also includes GED (CDE 14) — a one-to-one mapping is forced here. HighestGrade_CollegeGraduate maps to CDE 18 (Bachelor's degree) as the closest single match. HighestGrade_OneThroughFour spans CDE 1–4; HighestGrade_FiveThroughEight spans CDE 5–8; HighestGrade_NineThroughEleven spans CDE 9–11; HighestGrade_CollegeOnetoThree spans CDE 15–17; HighestGrade_AdvancedDegree spans CDE 19–21 — none can be mapped to a single CDE code. PMI_PreferNotToAnswer is closest to CDE 77 (Refused) but the semantics differ (prefer not to answer vs. refused), so it is left unmapped.

transforms.targetCdeId: What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed or the highest degree you have received [NHANES]
transforms.rationale: Source codes represent broad grade ranges mapped to the highest grade within each range: code 1 ('Grade 8 or lower') maps to CDE 8 (8th grade) as the upper bound; code 2 ('Grade 9-10') maps to CDE 10 (10th grade) as the upper bound; code 3 ('Grade 11-13') maps to CDE 12 (12th grade, no diploma) as the closest upper bound — CDE only goes to grade 12 and code 13 is 'High school graduate', but grade 13 in some Canadian provinces is a pre-university year that does not necessarily imply graduation, so 12th grade no diploma is a reasonable but imperfect choice. Confidence is moderate because the source uses ranges and Canadian provincial equivalencies that don't map cleanly to single NHANES grade levels.

transforms.targetCdeId: What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed or the highest degree you have received [NHANES]
transforms.rationale: The source variable uses broad Canadian-style post-secondary education categories that don't map cleanly to the granular NHANES grade-level CDE. '05=Bachelor's degree' maps confidently to CDE 18. '06=University degree or certificate above bachelor's level' is ambiguous — it could be master's (19), professional (20), or doctoral (21); mapped tentatively to 19 (master's) but this is uncertain. '01=No post-secondary degree' is too broad — it could span CDE codes 0–15 depending on actual attainment. '02=Trade certificate/vocational' could be CDE 16 but the source explicitly says 'no degree' framing differs. '03=Non-university certificate/diploma' could be CDE 16 or 17 but the match is uncertain. '04=University certificate below bachelor's' could be CDE 15 or 17 but is ambiguous. '97=Other' has no CDE equivalent. High ambiguity in most mappings reduces overall confidence.

transforms.targetCdeId: What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed or the highest degree you have received [NHANES]
transforms.rationale: The source variable is a binary Yes/No question, which has no meaningful correspondence to any of the NHANES education level CDE codes. No valid mapping is possible.

records.concept: Population-level percentage of adults aged 25+ with at least a high school education (area-level education statistic)
records.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'

gencde.definition: The population-level percentage of adults aged 25 years and older residing in a defined geographic area (e.g., census tract or ZIP code) who have completed at least a high school diploma, GED, or equivalent credential, derived from census or administrative data as an area-level socioeconomic indicator.

aliases: Percent adults with high school education or higher
Census tract percent high school graduates

gencde.rationale: All four MESA source fields (educ_minhs1–educ_minhs4, likely corresponding to exam waves 1–4) are numeric percentages representing the same area-level construct at different time points. Because the concept is an aggregate/ecological statistic rather than an individual self-report, it diverges from the ideal individual-level CDE and near-miss CDEs (which capture personal educational attainment). No permissible values are defined; the value domain is a continuous percentage [0, 100]. The near-miss CDEs were used only to populate aliases. Confidence is slightly reduced because the exact geographic unit (census tract, ZIP code, county) and the census-year source are not specified in the source field metadata.

records.concept: Year the respondent ended full-time education (calendar year)
records.idealCde: Educational attainment (self-reported, no qualifier specified): captures the highest grade completed or highest degree/diploma/certificate received by the respondent. Question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have received?' Answer type: ordinal categorical, single-select; values span a continuum from never attended school/kindergarten only through primary grades (1–4), middle grades (5–8), secondary grades (9–13 or equivalent), high school diploma/GED or equivalency credential, and post-secondary credentials (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral, professional degrees, and other certificates/diplomas); expressed as a standardized ordinal code with descriptive label. No laterality, body site, or address qualifier applies; no specific time window beyond 'ever/to date.'

gencde.rationale: The primary data type is numeric (integer calendar year, UCUM unit 'a' for year). A single categorical sentinel value 'Never went to school' is retained from the source field (UKBB codes -1 'Do not know' and -3 'Prefer not to answer' are missing-data sentinels and are excluded per instructions). The numeric range 1900–2100 is a plausible real-world bound for a calendar year response. The near-miss CDEs 'Education Year Count' and 'Able work full time last date' were consulted for alias terms only. Confidence is moderate because only one source cohort (UKBB) was observed and the concept is a specific calendar-year operationalisation rather than the more common ordinal educational-attainment construct described in the ideal CDE anchor.

records.concept: CES-D positive affect item: past-week frequency of positive emotional state (hopeful/happy), 4-point ordinal scale
records.idealCde: Positive affect / well-being item from the CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) positive subscale: a single self-report item asking the respondent how often during the past week they experienced a specific positive emotional state (e.g., felt hopeful about the future; felt happy). The question is framed as 'During the past week, how often did you feel [positive state]?' Answer type: ordinal 4-point frequency scale anchored to days in the past 7 days — 0 = All of the time (5–7 days), 1 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 2 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 3 = Rarely or none of the time (< 1 day). Note: the source concept cluster contains heterogeneous fields spanning positive affect (CES-D items), sexual/gender identity (closer self-description including queer, polysexual/omnisexual/sapiosexual/pansexual, asexual, two-spirit), a general overall health descriptor, and a 0–10 numeric pain intensity rating (past 7 days average); these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than a single unified element.

gencde.title: CES-D Positive Affect Item: Past-Week Frequency of Positive Emotional State (Hopeful/Happy)
gencde.definition: A single self-report ordinal item from the CES-D positive affect subscale asking how often during the past week the respondent experienced a specific positive emotional state (e.g., felt hopeful about the future or felt happy), rated on a 4-point frequency scale anchored to number of days in the prior 7 days.
