cde.id: In general, would you say your overall health is [PhenX]

records.idealCde: Positive affect / well-being item from the CES-D (Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale) positive subscale: a single self-report item asking the respondent how often during the past week they experienced a specific positive emotional state (e.g., felt hopeful about the future; felt happy). The question is framed as 'During the past week, how often did you feel [positive state]?' Answer type: ordinal 4-point frequency scale anchored to days in the past 7 days — 0 = All of the time (5–7 days), 1 = Occasionally or a moderate amount of time (3–4 days), 2 = Some or a little of the time (1–2 days), 3 = Rarely or none of the time (< 1 day). Note: the source concept cluster contains heterogeneous fields spanning positive affect (CES-D items), sexual/gender identity (closer self-description including queer, polysexual/omnisexual/sapiosexual/pansexual, asexual, two-spirit), a general overall health descriptor, and a 0–10 numeric pain intensity rating (past 7 days average); these represent distinct constructs that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than a single unified element.

records.concept: Heart rate in beats per minute
records.idealCde: This source concept is heterogeneous and conflates multiple distinct measurements: (1) Heart Rate — the resting pulse rate in beats per minute (bpm), captured as a numeric value; question: 'What is the subject's heart rate?'; answer type: integer or decimal, units: beats per minute (bpm). (2) Eidon CFP Mosaic Image Creation — whether a color fundus photography mosaic image was created using the Eidon device; question: 'Was an Eidon mosaic CFP image created?'; answer type: boolean (Yes/No). (3) OD Autorefractor Axis — the axis of the refractive correction for the right eye (oculus dexter) as measured by autorefractor; question: 'What is the autorefractor-measured axis for the right eye?'; answer type: integer, units: degrees (0–180). (4) OD Autorefractor Cylinder — the cylindrical (astigmatic) refractive power for the right eye as measured by autorefractor; question: 'What is the autorefractor-measured cylinder power for the right eye?'; answer type: decimal, units: diopters (D). These should be represented as separate CDEs; no single ideal CDE can unify them.

gencde.rationale: Source field AI-READI:viaospsf stores the Snellen fraction as a free-text string (e.g., '20/20', '20/40', 'CF', 'HM', 'LP', 'NLP'), which is standard clinical practice for Snellen notation including near-threshold qualitative descriptors. Data type is therefore 'text' rather than numeric. No permissible values are enumerated because the Snellen fraction space is open-ended and the source field does not constrain to a fixed coded list. The IDEAL CDE anchor provided describes unrelated concepts (heart rate, Eidon CFP mosaic, OD autorefractor axis) and was disregarded; the GenCDE is based solely on the source field semantics. Near-miss CDEs relate to OCT retinal thickness laterality and were used only to confirm non-overlap. Confidence is slightly reduced from maximum due to the single source cohort and free-text representation, which may include non-standard entries.

gencde.title: ECG P-Wave Axis in Degrees
gencde.definition: The frontal plane electrical axis of the P-wave as measured on a standard 12-lead electrocardiogram, expressed in degrees, reflecting the mean direction of atrial depolarization.
gencde.questionText: What is the P-wave axis (in degrees) as measured on the electrocardiogram?
relatedCdes: Cylinder axis L eye

gencde.rationale: Both MESA source fields (paxis5 and paxis5c) measure the same concept in degrees; paxis5c is the cleaned version with sentinel value 999 recoded to missing. The valid physiological range for P-wave axis is conventionally -180 to +180 degrees, with normal sinus rhythm typically falling between 0 and +75 degrees. The near-miss CDEs (cylinder axis, ECG axis direction indicator, imaging P-values) were correctly excluded: cylinder axis pertains to ophthalmic refraction, ECG axis direction indicator is a categorical qualifier rather than a continuous measurement, and the imaging P-values CDE is unrelated. No permissible values are listed as this is a continuous numeric variable.

records.concept: Family history of specific cancer type: which biological relatives have been diagnosed (multi-select relative per cancer type)
records.idealCde: Family history of cancer by cancer type and affected biological relative: For each specific cancer type (e.g., bladder cancer, blood/soft tissue cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, and other cancer types), identifies which first- and second-degree biological relatives have been diagnosed with that cancer. The question asked is 'Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.' The answer is a multi-select checkbox response where each selectable option represents a specific biological relative relationship (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent, and potentially other relatives). Answer type: categorical multi-select (select all that apply); one such CDE per cancer type, with response options representing distinct biological relative categories (e.g., Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent).

gencde.title: Family History of Specific Cancer Type: Affected Biological Relative(s)
gencde.definition: For a specified cancer type, identifies which first- and second-degree biological relatives of the participant have been diagnosed with that cancer, captured as a multi-select response.
gencde.questionText: Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.
aliases: Family history of cancer - affected relative
relatedCdes: Past current tumors cancer illness type
Cancer diagnosis type
Other condition cancer type text
gencde.rationale: This CDE is parameterized by cancer type (e.g., bladder, blood/soft tissue, bone, brain, breast, cervical, colorectal, endocrine, endometrial, eye, head and neck) and captures a multi-select set of biological relatives. The six permissible values (Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent) are the complete set observed across all AoU source fields; sex-specific cancer types (cervical, endometrial) omit Father and Son in the source but the canonical value set is unified across all cancer types. Each cancer-type-specific instantiation of this CDE should be treated as a separate variable instance. Near-miss CDEs (past/current tumor type, cancer diagnosis type) address the cancer type dimension rather than the relative dimension and were used only to inform alias labeling.

records.idealCde: Physical functional mobility — walking ability: A CDE capturing the degree to which an individual can perform walking and related ambulatory activities (e.g., walking, climbing stairs, carrying objects) without assistance. The question asks about the presence, severity, or independence of walking/ambulation capacity. Expected answer type: ordinal categorical scale reflecting difficulty or independence level (e.g., No difficulty / A little difficulty / Moderate difficulty / Extreme difficulty / Unable; or Yes/No for unaided walking; or a graded frequency/extent scale). Note: member fields carry heterogeneous qualifiers — some assess general walking ability (unaided ambulation, yes/no), some assess difficulty with stairs and everyday physical activities, one specifically qualifies walking difficulty as attributable to eyesight (vision-related peripheral awareness while walking), and one captures fatigue-related inability to initiate movement ('get going'); these represent distinct sub-constructs (functional mobility, vision-related mobility limitation, fatigue-related initiation) that should ideally be captured as separate CDEs rather than collapsed into one.

transforms.targetCdeId:
Do you have serious difficulty walking or climbing stairs? 

(5 years of age or older)
transforms.rationale: Yes/No map directly to CDE codes 1/0. 'Prefer not to answer' has no equivalent in the binary CDE value set and cannot be mapped.

transforms.targetCdeId:
Do you have serious difficulty walking or climbing stairs? 

(5 years of age or older)
transforms.rationale: The source variable appears to measure degree of difficulty with everyday activities on a 5-point Likert scale (Completely to Not at all), while the CDE is a binary Yes/No for 'serious difficulty walking or climbing stairs.' Only 'Not at all' maps confidently to No (0). The remaining options (Completely, Mostly, Moderately, A little) all imply some level of difficulty, but the CDE threshold for 'serious' difficulty is ambiguous — it is unclear whether 'A little' or 'Moderately' would qualify as 'serious.' Without a clear cutoff definition, these cannot be confidently mapped to Yes (1), so they are left unmapped. A domain expert should define the threshold (e.g., Completely/Mostly/Moderately = Yes, A little = No).

transforms.targetCdeId:
Do you have serious difficulty walking or climbing stairs? 

(5 years of age or older)
transforms.rationale: Source codes 1 (Yes) and 2 (No) map directly to CDE Yes/No. Code 3 (Unable to do) could imply serious difficulty but is not equivalent to a simple Yes — inability may reflect a more severe limitation than 'serious difficulty,' and conflating them risks misclassification, so it is left unmapped. Code 4 (Don't do on doctor's orders) reflects a behavioral/medical restriction rather than an inherent ambulatory difficulty, and has no CDE equivalent.

gencde.title: Ability to Travel Independently to Places Out of Walking Distance
gencde.definition: A binary indicator of whether an individual can independently travel to destinations beyond walking distance (e.g., by driving their own car or using public transit or taxis alone) without assistance from another person.
gencde.questionText: Can you get to places out of walking distance without help (i.e., you drive your own car, or travel alone on buses, or taxis)?

To what extent are you able to carry out your everyday physical activities such as walking, climbing stairs, carrying groceries, or moving a chair?__2
In the past 7 days I could get in and out of a car.
gencde.rationale: Derived from a single CLSA source field (IAL_ABLTRV_TRM) with a binary Yes/No response. This item corresponds to the transportation domain of the Lawton Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) scale, which assesses community mobility as a higher-order functional independence skill. Near-miss CDEs address physical mobility (car transfers, walking, stair climbing) but not the transportation independence construct specifically. The IDEAL CDE anchor describes walking/ambulation ability, which is a related but distinct concept; this CDE captures instrumental transportation independence rather than physical ambulatory capacity.

records.idealCde: Alcohol consumption frequency by beverage type (beer, wine, or liquor) during a typical/average week; asks how many standard-serving units of a specific alcoholic beverage type (beer: 12 oz. bottles/cans; wine: 5 oz. glasses; liquor: 1.5 oz. shots/mixed drinks) the respondent usually consumes per week during a defined reference period; answer type is numeric quantity (count of standard servings per week), captured either as an ordinal-banded integer (e.g., 0=less than 1, up to 36 or more) or as a continuous decimal value; separate fields are expected for each beverage type (beer, wine, liquor), and may be further stratified by day type (weekday vs. weekend) within the reference period (e.g., past 12 months or general average week); self-reported by the study participant.

gencde.rationale: This CDE harmonizes three distinct source patterns: (1) AI-READI ordinal-banded dropdowns for beer, wine, and liquor with slightly inconsistent band boundaries across beverage types (beer: 22-28, 29-35, 36+; wine: 21-25, 26-30, 31-35, 35+); (2) CLSA continuous decimal fields split by weekday vs. weekend and by beverage subtype (red wine, white wine, beer, liquor, other); (3) MESA continuous numeric field for liquor/mixed drinks. The canonical permissible-value set retains the ordinal bands actually observed across sources, merging the wine-specific bands (21-25, 26-30, 31-35) and beer/liquor bands (22-28, 29-35, 36+) into a single reconciled ladder; the lower bands (1-6, 7-13, 14-21) are inferred as implicit intermediate values present in the continuous CLSA/MESA fields and consistent with the ordinal structure. 'Prefer not to say' consolidates AI-READI codes 999 and 777. The element is intended to be instantiated separately per beverage type (beer, wine, liquor, other) and per day-part (weekday, weekend) as needed; the qualifier fields (beverage_type, day_part, reference_period) should accompany this CDE in any data model. Missing-data sentinels (777, 999) are excluded from the permissible-value set per instructions and mapped to 'Prefer not to say'. Confidence is moderate (0.72) due to non-uniform band boundaries across beverage types and the mixed ordinal/continuous measurement approaches across cohorts.

transforms.rationale: All source codes map exactly to CDE codes by both value and label. The source is a subset of the CDE value set, with no ambiguous or missing-data-only codes.

Direct label matches for 0, 22, 29, 36. Source code 777 ('Prefer not to say') maps to CDE code 999 ('Prefer not to say') — same meaning, different sentinel value. Source is simply missing the 1–6, 7–13, and 14–21 range options that exist in the CDE, but all present source codes map cleanly.

Source code 0 and 35 (>36) map cleanly to CDE bins 0 and 36+. Source 777 maps to CDE 999 (prefer not to say). Source codes 21 (21-25), 26 (26-30), and 31 (31-35) each straddle two CDE bins and cannot be confidently assigned to a single CDE code without ambiguity, so they are left unmapped.

gencde.rationale: Sourced from MESA variable wtls5c (WEIGHT LOSS DRUGS), which uses a 0/1 numeric encoding for No/Yes. The concept is straightforward and well-supported by a single source field with unambiguous permissible values. The ideal CDE anchor provided describes a cholesterol concept and is unrelated; it was disregarded for content but confirms no existing CDE matched this weight-loss-drug concept. Near-miss CDEs (weight loss intervention type, weight loss value, weight loss counsel indicator) are related but distinct constructs and were used only to inform alias terminology. gencde.rationale: Concept is narrowly and clearly defined by the single UKBB source field (continuous, mg, 24-hour dietary recall). records.concept: Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary Yes/No
records.idealCde: This source concept clusters several distinct circulatory/medical-history elements that should ideally be represented as separate CDEs: (1) Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had high blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had high blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (2) Low blood pressure lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had low blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had low blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (3) Age at first hypertension diagnosis — self-reported age category at which the participant was first told they had hypertension; question: 'About how old were you when you were first told you had hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Ordinal categorical (Child [0–11], Adolescent [12–17], Adult [18–64], Older adult [65–74], Older adult [75+]). (4) Current hypertension treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (5) Current peripheral vascular disease treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No).

records.idealCde: This source concept clusters several distinct circulatory/medical-history elements that should ideally be represented as separate CDEs: (1) Hypertension (high blood pressure) lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had high blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had high blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (2) Low blood pressure lifetime occurrence — self-reported binary indicator of whether the participant has ever had low blood pressure; question: 'Have you ever had low blood pressure?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (3) Age at first hypertension diagnosis — self-reported age category at which the participant was first told they had hypertension; question: 'About how old were you when you were first told you had hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Ordinal categorical (Child [0–11], Adolescent [12–17], Adult [18–64], Older adult [65–74], Older adult [75+]). (4) Current hypertension treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for hypertension (high blood pressure)?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No). (5) Current peripheral vascular disease treatment status — self-reported indicator of whether the participant is currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease; question: 'Are you currently prescribed medications and/or receiving treatment for peripheral vascular disease?'; answer type: Boolean/dichotomous (Yes/No).

records.concept: Reasons contributing to decision to retire (multi-select Yes/No checklist)
records.idealCde: Retirement circumstances and decision-making: A set of CDEs capturing the context and motivations surrounding an individual's retirement and, if applicable, return to work. Covers: (1) reasons contributing to the decision to retire (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (2) reasons contributing to the decision to return to work after first retirement (multi-select checklist of contributing factors, each coded Yes/No); (3) whether health-related retirement was due to physical health, emotional/mental health (including stress), or both (single-select categorical: Physical health | Emotional/mental health including stress | Both); (4) whether the respondent contributed to an employer pension plan other than CPP/QPP prior to retirement (single-select categorical: Yes | No). All items are self-reported by the respondent about their own retirement experience. Answer types are binary Yes/No per factor for reason checklists, and single-select nominal categories for health-type and pension-plan items.

gencde.title: Reason Contributing to Retirement Decision Indicator (Yes/No)
gencde.definition: A binary indicator capturing whether a specific factor (e.g., health, mandatory termination, income, medical reasons) contributed to an individual's decision to retire, administered as part of a multi-select checklist in which each candidate reason is independently endorsed as Yes or No.

gencde.rationale: Source fields from CLSA cover at least four distinct retirement-reason domains inferred from variable suffixes: health/health-related (HL_COM, HL_TRM), income/financial (IN_TRM), and mandatory/medical termination (MD_TRM). Each is a separate checklist item sharing the same question stem and the same binary Yes/No value domain; this GenCDE represents the shared binary response element applicable to any such item. The multi-select checklist structure means one CDE instance per reason-item is expected. Codes 1=Yes and 0=No are preserved directly from source. Near-miss CDEs (retired year date; reasons for not contacting someone; social support item) were used only to confirm non-overlap and inform alias vocabulary. The IDEAL CDE anchor confirms this element belongs to a broader retirement-circumstances module.

gencde.rationale: Sourced from CLSA variable RPL_INFSP_SI_TRM, which is one item in a multi-select checklist of anticipated retirement influences. gencde.title: Anticipated Reason for Future Retirement Indicator (Pre-Retiree Checklist Item)
gencde.definition: A binary indicator capturing whether a specific factor (e.g., health-related or terminal illness) is anticipated to be a likely contributing reason for an individual's future retirement, as reported by a pre-retiree respondent on a multi-select checklist.
gencde.questionText: There are many reasons why people retire. Which of the following are likely to be the reasons that you retire? (Select Yes or No for each item)
relatedCdes: Risk Factor Questionnaire (RFQ) - retired year date

gencde.rationale: Source fields CLSA:RPL_WHYR_AR_TRM and CLSA:RPL_WHYR_HL_TRM are two checklist items (likely 'arranged/planned retirement' and 'health-related retirement' respectively) from a multi-select Yes/No battery administered to pre-retirees in the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging (CLSA). gencde.rationale: The sole source field (AI-READI icf_sign) is a file-type input capturing a participant signature on an informed consent form (ICF). The IDEAL CDE anchor describes a richer contact-attempt workflow element, but the only observed source field is strictly a signature upload, so the GenCDE is scoped to that narrower, well-evidenced concept. Near-miss CDEs (SDQ signature text, EEG ictal face sign) share the word 'signature' but are semantically unrelated; they inform aliases only. Confidence is moderate because only one source field was observed and the file-upload data type is not natively represented in the schema.

gencde.title: Digital Volume Pulse Waveform Parameters (Notch Position, Peak Position, Shoulder Position, Peak-to-Peak Time, Wave Data, Reflection Index)
gencde.definition: A composite set of measurements derived from the digital volume pulse (DVP) waveform recorded at the finger, characterizing the timing and amplitude features of the direct and reflected arterial pressure wave components, including the positions of the notch, peak, and shoulder, the peak-to-peak interval between direct and reflected components, the raw pressure-versus-time waveform data, and the reflection index expressing the ratio of reflected to direct wave amplitude.
gencde.questionText: What are the waveform parameters (notch position, peak position, shoulder position, peak-to-peak time, raw wave data, and reflection index) derived from the digital volume pulse recorded at the finger?
sourceVariables: UKBB:Position of the pulse wave peak
UKBB:Position of the shoulder on the pulse waveform
UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time
UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
relatedCdes: Perfusion index Blood Postductal Pulse oximetry
Perfusion index Blood Preductal Pulse oximetry
Echocardiogram spectral doppler ejection time
gencde.rationale: This GenCDE covers a family of six closely related DVP-derived variables all sourced from UKBB finger photoplethysmography: (1) notch position [integer, sample index], (2) peak position [integer, sample index], (3) shoulder position [integer, sample index], (4) peak-to-peak time [integer, ms], (5) raw pressure-vs-time waveform compound data [3 waveforms × 100 points each, X=ms, Y=arbitrary signal strength], and (6) reflection index [integer, (a/b)×100%]. Because these are distinct sub-parameters of the same DVP construct they are grouped here; implementers may split into individual CDEs per parameter. The ideal CDE anchor (right ventricular stroke volume) is conceptually unrelated — the match confidence is accordingly reduced. Near-miss CDEs (perfusion index, Doppler ejection time) share vascular/cardiac timing lineage but are distinct constructs. No existing NIH CDE was found to cover DVP waveform decomposition parameters.
gencde.units: ms (timing parameters); % (reflection index); arbitrary units (wave amplitude)

memberDetails.name: Position of pulse wave notch
memberDetails.text:
position of the notch

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. This is the time when when notch occurs in the waveform.

memberDetails.id: UKBB:Pulse wave peak to peak time
memberDetails.name: Pulse wave peak to peak time
memberDetails.text:
peak to peak time in milliseconds

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. peak to peak time is the difference between the peak values of direct and reflected components.

memberDetails.id: UKBB:Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
memberDetails.name: Pulse wave pressure versus time response curve
memberDetails.text:
Wave data containing 3 waveforms, each consisting of one direct and one reflected component.

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. Each waveform is actually a single pulse with 100 points. Since the heart rate is in beats per minute, a single beat takes 60seconds / Heart Rate and time between two beats is (60/Heart Rate)/100.

The data is formatted as follows:

  • The first number (i.e. digits before the first '|' character)indicate the number of points X,Y for the curve.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated by a '|' character from the preceding/succeeding pair.
  • Each pair of X,Y values is separated internally by a ',' character.
The X-axis is the time in milliseconds and the Y-axis is the Pulse signal strength in arbitrary units.

memberDetails.name: Pulse wave reflection index
memberDetails.text:
reflection index is a measure of reflection

A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. if 'b' is the height of direct wave peak and 'a' is the height of reflected wave peak the reflected index = (a/b) * 100%

records.idealCde: Cardiovascular disease history (other/unspecified cardiac conditions): A binary indicator capturing whether an individual has a self-reported or clinician-diagnosed history of any cardiac condition not elsewhere classified, including but not limited to pacemaker implantation, heart valve disease, open heart surgery, heart attack/myocardial infarction, angina/chest pain due to heart disease, or heart transplant. The CDE answers the question: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you have, or have you ever been diagnosed with or undergone treatment for, a cardiac condition (e.g., heart attack/MI, angina, heart valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant)?' Answer type: categorical/radio; values: 1=Yes, 0=No. Note: member fields span multiple distinct cardiac conditions (MI, angina, valve disease, pacemaker, open heart surgery, heart transplant) that ideally should each be captured as separate CDEs; if a single umbrella CDE is required, it represents presence of any cardiac condition history. An optional supplementary free-text or checklist field may specify the condition type, and a date field (text/date format: YYYY-MM-DD) may capture the date of the relevant cardiac event or procedure (e.g., heart transplant date).

records.concept: Alcohol drinking behavior and context (change vs 10 years ago, with meals, former drinker status, reason for reducing/stopping)
records.idealCde: Alcohol drinking behavior and context: a set of related categorical measures capturing self-reported current and historical alcohol consumption patterns, including (1) change in alcohol intake compared to 10 years previously (more/same/less), (2) whether alcohol is typically consumed with meals (yes/no/varies), (3) former alcohol drinker status among current non-drinkers (yes/no), (4) preferred hot drink temperature (very hot/hot/warm/does not drink hot drinks), and (5) reason for reducing alcohol consumption among those who drink less than 10 years ago (illness/doctor's advice/health precaution/other). Each sub-element is a single-select categorical response collected conditionally based on current drinking status. No single unified question; each answers a specific aspect of drinking behavior and context for an individual participant.

gencde.title: Alcohol Drinking Behavior and Context (Change vs. 10 Years Ago, With Meals, Former Drinker Status, Reason for Reducing/Stopping)
gencde.definition: A set of self-reported categorical measures capturing current and historical alcohol consumption patterns, including change in intake compared to 10 years previously, whether alcohol is consumed with meals, former drinker status among current non-drinkers, and the reason for reducing or stopping alcohol consumption.

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE consolidates seven closely related UKBB touchscreen fields that collectively characterize alcohol drinking behavior and context. The permissible-value set merges synonymous pilot and main-wave labels (e.g., 'Illness' and 'Illness or ill health' are unified as 'Illness or ill health'; 'Doctor's advice' and 'Health precaution' are retained as distinct concepts present in main-wave fields but absent from pilot). Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer, -6=It varies as a sentinel in some codings) are excluded as non-substantive response options, except 'It varies' which is a genuine substantive answer for the meals question and is retained. Because the concept spans multiple sub-questions administered conditionally (to current drinkers, to those drinking less than 10 years ago, and to former drinkers), implementations should treat this as a composite domain and apply appropriate routing logic. Confidence is modestly reduced from 1.0 because the concept bundles distinct sub-constructs that could alternatively be represented as separate CDEs; the bundled representation reflects the source harmonization intent.

gencde.rationale: Both source UKBB fields (F5890 for diabetes-related eye disease and F5934 for other serious eye conditions) share an identical three-option permissible-value set (Right eye / Left eye / Both eyes), enabling direct harmonization into a single canonical CDE. Near-miss CDEs (other eye condition text, vision affected indicator, medical history eye condition other text) were used only to inform alias terminology and confirm non-overlap. The IDEAL CDE anchor text appears to describe an unrelated alcohol-behavior concept and was disregarded as likely a metadata error in the prompt; the GenCDE is grounded solely on the SOURCE FIELDS and ANSWER CONCEPTS provided.

records.idealCde: Sleep disturbance / insomnia symptom burden: A composite domain capturing the frequency, severity, and quality of sleep problems including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much, assessed over a defined recent time window (past 1–4 weeks). The CDE answers: 'How often have you experienced trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much, and how does it affect your sleep quality?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale (e.g., never / rarely / sometimes / often / always, or equivalent Likert-type ratings ranging from 0–3 or 1–5), with sub-components optionally capturing: (1) frequency of sleep-onset latency >30 minutes (ordinal: never to 5–7 times/week), (2) duration of sleep difficulty (decimal, in weeks/months/years), and (3) overall sleep satisfaction (ordinal: very satisfied to very dissatisfied). No single laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; fields reflect self-reported sleep experience of the respondent across multiple instruments (CES-D restless sleep item, PHQ-9 sleep item, PSQI-style items).

records.idealCde: Sleep disturbance / insomnia symptom burden: A composite domain capturing the frequency, severity, and quality of sleep problems including difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much, assessed over a defined recent time window (past 1–4 weeks). The CDE answers: 'How often have you experienced trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much, and how does it affect your sleep quality?' Answer type: ordinal frequency scale (e.g., never / rarely / sometimes / often / always, or equivalent Likert-type ratings ranging from 0–3 or 1–5), with sub-components optionally capturing: (1) frequency of sleep-onset latency >30 minutes (ordinal: never to 5–7 times/week), (2) duration of sleep difficulty (decimal, in weeks/months/years), and (3) overall sleep satisfaction (ordinal: very satisfied to very dissatisfied). No single laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; fields reflect self-reported sleep experience of the respondent across multiple instruments (CES-D restless sleep item, PHQ-9 sleep item, PSQI-style items).

gencde.rationale: Derived from a single MESA source field (dzlnch1) representing one item of the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS), specifically the post-lunch sitting scenario. The near-miss CDEs address sleep-onset difficulty at night (insomnia domain) rather than daytime sleepiness propensity, confirming this is a distinct construct. No permissible values were added beyond those observed in the source field. The qualifier 'without alcohol' is preserved from the source to control for alcohol-induced sedation.

records.concept: Self-perceived weight status (overweight / underweight / just about right)
records.idealCde: Self-reported height and weight perception — a cluster of two related self-report measures collected from the respondent about themselves: (1) Self-perceived weight status: the question 'Do you consider yourself overweight, underweight, or just about right?' answered as an ordinal categorical variable with values: Overweight | Underweight | Just about right; (2) Self-reported standing height without shoes: the question 'How tall are you without shoes on?' answered as a categorical/ordinal variable encoded in foot-and-inch bands with corresponding centimeter ranges (e.g., 1'0"–1'11", 2'0"–2'11", 3'0"–3'11", 4'0" and above), spanning the full plausible human height range, with each response band representing approximately 2.5 cm increments. Answer type: (1) nominal categorical (3-level); (2) ordinal categorical height band (feet/inches with cm equivalents).

gencde.title: Self-perception of body weight
gencde.definition: This term represents a patient's self-perception of their body weight in terms of being overweight or underweight. The term is based on, but not limited in use to, one of the questions in a two-item measure for an individual's weight change goals used in the Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS), is a national school-based survey conducted by CDC and state, territorial, tribal, and local education and health agencies as part of the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS). The YRBSS monitors health-related behaviors that contribute to the leading causes of death and disability among youth and adults.[https://www.cdc.gov/healthyyouth/data/yrbs/] For the other question item on what the individual is trying to do about their weight, use Body weight goal [LOINC: 90734-5].
gencde.rationale: The existing CDE already contains 'About the right weight', 'Slightly overweight'/'Very overweight', and 'Slightly underweight'/'Very underweight', which fully subsume the three source-field values (Overweight, Underweight, Just about right); no new permissible values are needed — the CDE's broader value set already covers the concept, so only the relation is noted as broadMatch (CDE is more granular than the source fields, not the reverse).

memberDetails.name: Reason for skipping standing height
memberDetails.text:
Reason standing height measurement was not performed (entered as free-text by a UK Biobank Staff member).

This field was created by post-hoc coding the free-text reasons entered during the assessment centre visit. The encoding used was constructed after the data had been examined to determine suitable representative groupings.

transforms.rationale: The CDE offers only two codes: 'Not applicable' and 'Unknown'. 'Unknown'/'Reason not known' maps to codes 300 and 506. The vast majority of source codes represent specific, known reasons (declined, equipment failure, health conditions, nurse-advised, etc.) that do not align with 'Not applicable' (which implies the measurement was irrelevant by design) or 'Unknown' (which implies the reason is genuinely not known). These specific reason codes have no valid CDE equivalent and must remain unmapped. Confidence is low because the CDE value set is far too narrow to capture the richness of the source variable. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:ca6a95b87e578#g2): 40 of 41 source codes now map.

records.concept: DASH Diet score including sodium (0-9 points)
records.idealCde: Dietary pattern and food preference assessment: captures both overall dietary quality (via a composite diet score) and individual food/beverage liking preferences. Specifically measures (1) adherence to a dietary pattern on a scored index (e.g., DASH Diet score including sodium, 0–9 integer points, where higher scores indicate greater adherence) and (2) hedonic liking for specific foods and beverages (diet fizzy drinks, dried fruit, fruit, grapefruit) each rated on a 9-point bipolar hedonic scale (1 = extremely dislike to 9 = extremely like, with special codes for 'never tried' and 'do not wish to answer'). No specific laterality, body site, or subject qualifier is specified; context is self-reported dietary quality and food preference.

gencde.rationale: All eight UKBB source fields share an identical 9-point bipolar response structure (codes 1–9) plus two non-substantive sentinels (never tried, do not wish to answer). Sentinel codes -121 and -818 from the source are remapped to clean sequential codes 88 and 99 respectively, as they are not part of the hedonic continuum and should not be treated as ordinal values. The CDE is intentionally item-agnostic (parameterised by food/beverage item) to serve as a reusable template across all specific food liking fields. Near-miss CDEs (overall diet health scale, beverage consumption at meals, upper-extremity peel-fruit ability) were reviewed and confirmed non-matching; 'hedonic rating scale' and '9-point hedonic scale' are retained as aliases drawing on sensory science and food science ontology usage.

records.concept: Annual household income from all sources (ordinal range brackets)
records.idealCde: Annual household income from all sources: Total gross income received by all members of the respondent's household during the past 12 months (calendar year), combining wages, salaries, self-employment earnings, investments, retirement, government transfers, and any other income sources. Question asked: 'What is the total gross annual income for all members of your household from all sources in the past 12 months?' Answer type: Ordinal categorical (income range brackets), e.g., Less than $5,000 | $5,000–$9,999 | $10,000–$14,999 | $15,000–$19,999 | $20,000–$24,999 | $25,000–$34,999 | $35,000–$49,999 | $50,000–$74,999 | $75,000–$99,999 | $100,000 or more; units: US dollars (pre-tax/gross); reported by self for household unit.

gencde.title: Annual Household Income Range
gencde.definition: A demographic parameter indicating the amount of earnings made by a family.
gencde.questionText: What is your annual household income from all sources within family, not including roommates?
gencde.rationale: The only missing value was the 'Prefer not to answer' option (PMI_PreferNotToAnswer) present in the AoU source field; all income brackets already match, so adding this single permissible value is the minimal change needed.

memberDetails.name: income_annualincome
memberDetails.text:
One of the things we're trying to understand is how people's income may affect their use of health services.  Household income includes your income plus the income of all family members in your household for the last calendar year.  Include all wages and other sources of income.

What is your annual household income from all sources?

transforms.rationale: All nine income bracket source codes map directly to their CDE equivalents by label (minor whitespace differences are inconsequential). PMI_PreferNotToAnswer ('Prefer not to answer') has no corresponding permissible value in the CDE and is therefore unmapped. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c5620d7244f5d#g0): 10 of 10 source codes now map.

gencde.rationale: Derived from CLSA variable RPL_STDLIV_TRM. The concept is distinct from objective household income measures (e.g., annual gross income brackets) and from household size CDEs identified as near-misses. The three-level ordinal scale (Adequate / Barely adequate / Inadequate) represents the full observed answer space across source fields; no additional response options were present. Codes are assigned in ascending order of perceived inadequacy. This element captures a prospective, subjective financial outlook rather than a current income amount, aligning with retirement planning and financial well-being domains in aging cohort studies.

cde.id: Patient Health Questionnaire Depression (PHQ) - Little interest score

records.idealCde: PHQ-12 Somatic Symptom Scale (PHQ-12 SS) — individual somatic symptom bother items assessed over the past 3 months. Each item asks: 'During the past 3 months, how much have you been bothered by [specific somatic symptom]?' covering distinct symptoms including back pain, chest pain, dizziness, palpitations (feeling heart pound or race), and headaches. Answer type: ordinal Likert scale per item (e.g., 0 = Not bothered at all, 1 = Bothered a little, 2 = Bothered a lot), with one response per symptom; time window qualifier: past 3 months; instrument qualifier: PHQ-12 SS. Note: member fields represent separate item-level CDEs within the same scale, each scoped to a distinct somatic symptom domain rather than a single unified measure.

transforms.rationale: The PHQ 'little interest' item uses a 4-point scale (0=Not at all, 1=Several days, 2=More than half the days, 3=Nearly every day). The source has only 3 severity levels: 'Not bothered at all' maps to 0, 'Bothered a little' maps to 1 (several days). 'Bothered a lot' is ambiguous between 2 and 3 but most conservatively maps to 3 (nearly every day/most severe) since there is no intermediate option. -818 (Prefer not to answer) has no CDE equivalent and is unmapped. Confidence is moderate due to the collapsed scale and different framing ('bothered' vs. frequency). Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:c50c30a562107#g0): 4 of 4 source codes now map.

records.concept: IBS global impact: degree to which abdominal pain/discomfort or altered bowel habits interfere with life in general (0–10 slider)
records.idealCde: PHQ-12 Somatic Symptom Scale (PHQ-12 SS) — individual somatic symptom bother items assessed over the past 3 months. Each item asks: 'During the past 3 months, how much have you been bothered by [specific somatic symptom]?' covering distinct symptoms including back pain, chest pain, dizziness, palpitations (feeling heart pound or race), and headaches. Answer type: ordinal Likert scale per item (e.g., 0 = Not bothered at all, 1 = Bothered a little, 2 = Bothered a lot), with one response per symptom; time window qualifier: past 3 months; instrument qualifier: PHQ-12 SS. Note: member fields represent separate item-level CDEs within the same scale, each scoped to a distinct somatic symptom domain rather than a single unified measure.

gencde.rationale: Sourced exclusively from UK Biobank field implementing IBS-SSS Item 3 (Francis et al., Aliment Pharmacol Ther 1997;11:395-402). The response scale is an 11-point integer slider (0–10); data_type is set to numeric because the instrument intends a continuous VAS/slider, though values are integer-coded. The missing-data sentinel '-818 = Prefer not to answer' is excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. The ideal CDE anchor (PHQ-12 SS) is a near-miss measuring somatic symptom bother rather than IBS-specific life interference; it was used only to confirm no alias overlap. Near-miss CDEs (ROME I pain type; PROMIS pain interference items) confirm this is a distinct IBS-domain construct.

memberDetails.text:
Question asked: "Please indicate how much abdominal pain or discomfort or altered bowel habits are affecting or interfering with your life in general."

Participants were asked to move a slider to choose a number between 0 to 10, with 0 meaning "not at all" and 10 meaning "completely". Participants using an older browser were asked to select a button from 0 to 10.

The question in this field was taken from the IBS Severity Scoring System used with the authors' permission.

Francis CY, Morris J, Whorwell PJ. The irritable bowel severity scoring system: a simple method of monitoring irritable bowel syndrome and its progress. Alimentary Pharmacology & Therapeutics 1997;11(2):395-402

records.concept: Anxiety symptom profile and functional impact during worst period of anxiety (DSM-aligned Yes/No and ordinal items: concentration difficulty, sleep disturbance, keyed up, irritability, restlessness, muscle tension, role impairment, professional help-seeking)
records.idealCde: Generalized anxiety symptom profile during worst period of anxiety: a set of categorical (Yes/No or ordinal severity) items assessing the co-occurrence of specific DSM-aligned anxiety symptoms — including difficulty concentrating, sleep-onset/maintenance disturbance, feeling keyed up or on edge, and increased irritability — as well as functional impairment in normal roles (study/employment, childcare, housework, leisure) during the worst period of anxiety. Each symptom item is answered as a binary categorical (0=No, 1=Yes); the functional impairment item is answered on an ordinal scale (0=Not at all, 1=A little, 2=Somewhat, with additional severity levels implied). All items are conditioned on the respondent having endorsed persistent worry/anxiety (either confirmed anxiety episode or worry duration ≥6 months). Qualifier: worst period of anxiety (peak severity epoch, not current or lifetime general status).

gencde.title: Anxiety Symptom Profile and Functional Impact During Worst Period of Anxiety
gencde.definition: A multi-item assessment capturing the presence of DSM-aligned anxiety symptoms (difficulty concentrating, sleep disturbance, feeling keyed up or on edge, irritability, restlessness, muscle tension), the degree of role impairment, and professional help-seeking behavior during the individual's worst or most severe period of anxiety or worry.
gencde.questionText: When you were worried or anxious during your worst period, were you also experiencing the following: (1) difficulty keeping your mind on what you were doing; (2) often having trouble falling or staying asleep; (3) feeling keyed up or on edge; (4) being more irritable than usual; (5) feeling restless; (6) having tense, sore, or aching muscles? Additionally: (7) How much did these problems interfere with your normal roles (study/employment, childcare, housework, leisure)? (8) Did you ever tell a professional about these problems?

gencde.rationale: This GenCDE represents a composite multi-item instrument rather than a single variable; each named symptom facet (concentration, sleep, keyed up, irritability, restlessness, muscle tension, role impairment, professional help) is a distinct sub-item sharing a common administration context (worst anxiety period). Binary symptom items use codes 0=No and 1=Yes; the role-impairment ordinal item uses codes 2–5 (Not at all through A lot). Missing-data sentinels (-121=Do not know, -818=Prefer not to answer) observed in source fields are excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. The near-miss CDEs (OSQ stress item, PROMIS concentration item, Kessler-6 professional contact item) share overlapping constructs but differ in time window, response scale, or population context, confirming no existing CDE fully captures this DSM-aligned worst-period anxiety profile as operationalized in UK Biobank.

records.concept: Visual acuity under mesopic (low-light) conditions, right eye (OD): letter score and LogMAR
records.idealCde: Visual acuity measured separately under two luminance conditions (mesopic [low-light] and photopic [standard/bright-light]) for each eye independently (right eye [OD] and left eye [OS]); answers the question 'What is the patient's visual acuity under mesopic or photopic conditions in the specified eye?'; recorded as both a raw letter score (integer count of letters read correctly, text entry) and a derived LogMAR score (continuous numeric, calculated from letter score); qualifier: laterality (OD vs OS) and luminance condition (mesopic vs photopic) are both required dimensions of each measurement instance.

gencde.title: Visual Acuity Under Mesopic (Low-Light) Conditions, Right Eye (OD): Letter Score and LogMAR
gencde.definition: A paired measurement of visual acuity obtained under mesopic (low-light) luminance conditions for the right eye (OD), recorded as both the raw integer count of letters correctly identified on a standardized chart and the derived continuous LogMAR (logarithm of the minimum angle of resolution) score calculated from that letter count.
gencde.questionText: Under mesopic (low-light) conditions, how many letters did the patient correctly identify with the right eye (OD), and what is the corresponding LogMAR score?
relatedCdes: Woodcock Johnson III (WJ-III) ? Letter-word indentification score
Echocardiogram left ventricle mass z-score value
Graeb intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) scale - left lateral ventricle score
gencde.rationale: Two source fields from AI-READI were harmonized: 'viaodmlog' (free-text letter score, integer 0–100 on a standard ETDRS-style chart) and 'viaodmscore' (calculated LogMAR, a continuous numeric derived from the letter score via the standard formula LogMAR = 1.0 − (letters/50) or equivalent). Because both fields jointly define a single clinical measurement event (same eye, same luminance condition, same visit), they are represented as a single CDE with dual numeric representations. The letter score serves as the primary raw datum; LogMAR is the derived analytic value. Minimum/maximum reflect the ETDRS letter-score range (0–100 letters); LogMAR range correspondingly spans approximately −0.3 (best) to 1.0+ (worst), but is not separately bounded here. Near-miss CDEs (WJ-III letter-word identification, LV mass z-score, Graeb IVH scale) were used only to confirm non-overlap and contributed no aliases. Luminance condition (mesopic) and laterality (OD) are fixed qualifiers embedded in this CDE; separate CDEs should be authored for OS and for photopic conditions.
gencde.units: LogMAR (dimensionless) for derived score; letter count (integer) for raw score

gencde.rationale: Two source fields from AI-READI were harmonized: 'viaodplog' (free-text letter count, integer) and 'viaodpscore' (calculated LogMAR, continuous numeric). These represent two representations of the same underlying measurement — raw letter score and its LogMAR transform — for the right eye under photopic luminance. LogMAR range set to -0.3 (20/10, superior acuity) to 3.0 (20/20000, near-total loss), consistent with standard ETDRS conventions. Letter score range is typically 0–100 (ETDRS) but is captured here as free text. Near-miss CDEs (WJ-III letter-word identification, CAMPHOR) are linguistically adjacent but conceptually unrelated (cognitive/literacy vs. ophthalmologic measurement). No existing NIH CDE was found that captures the photopic + laterality (OD) + dual-representation (letter + LogMAR) qualifier combination. Recommend storing as two linked sub-elements (letter score: integer text entry; LogMAR: calculated numeric) under a single CDE umbrella, with laterality (OD) and luminance condition (photopic) as required qualifiers.

gencde.rationale: Concept is anchored by two AI-READI source fields: a raw letter score (viaosmlog, text entry) and a derived LogMAR score (viaosmscore, calculated). The GenCDE captures the derived continuous numeric (LogMAR), which is the clinically canonical representation; a companion CDE for the raw letter-count integer is warranted. LogMAR range of -0.3 to 3.0 reflects standard clinical limits (20/10 to 20/20000 equivalent). Mesopic luminance is typically defined as 0.001–3 cd/m². Near-miss CDEs (WJ-III letter-word identification, CAMPHOR breathlessness, Graeb IVH scale) share 'score' terminology but are unrelated in domain; no aliases were borrowed from them. Laterality (OS) and luminance condition (mesopic) are both encoded in the preferred name and title as required qualifiers per the ideal CDE specification.

records.concept: Transit stop within 10-15 minute walk from home (neighborhood walkability item)

cde.id: It is within a 10-15 minute walk to a transit stop (such as bus, train, trolley, or tram) from my home. Would you say that you . . .

records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability perception scale: a multi-item self-report instrument assessing the respondent's perceived walkability of their home neighborhood, capturing attributes such as sidewalk presence and maintenance, proximity and density of destinations within easy walking distance, availability of shops/markets within walking distance, and access to public transit stops within a 10–15 minute walk from home. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with an optional 'Does not apply to my neighborhood' response permitted where relevant. The construct reflects the respondent's subjective assessment of their immediate residential neighborhood environment as conducive to walking for transportation and daily errands.

records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability perception scale: a multi-item self-report instrument assessing the respondent's perceived walkability of their home neighborhood, capturing attributes such as sidewalk presence and maintenance, proximity and density of destinations within easy walking distance, availability of shops/markets within walking distance, and access to public transit stops within a 10–15 minute walk from home. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with an optional 'Does not apply to my neighborhood' response permitted where relevant. The construct reflects the respondent's subjective assessment of their immediate residential neighborhood environment as conducive to walking for transportation and daily errands.

records.concept: People observed being physically active in neighborhood (neighborhood walkability item)
records.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability perception scale: a multi-item self-report instrument assessing the respondent's perceived walkability of their home neighborhood, capturing attributes such as sidewalk presence and maintenance, proximity and density of destinations within easy walking distance, availability of shops/markets within walking distance, and access to public transit stops within a 10–15 minute walk from home. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree), with an optional 'Does not apply to my neighborhood' response permitted where relevant. The construct reflects the respondent's subjective assessment of their immediate residential neighborhood environment as conducive to walking for transportation and daily errands.

The 4-point Likert scale (1–4, no neutral midpoint) is consistent with the AI-READI source field and the broader walkability perception scale context described in the ideal CDE anchor. Near-miss CDEs address individual physical activity behavior or functional limitation, not neighborhood-level observation of others being active, confirming this is a distinct construct. gencde.rationale: Derived exclusively from UKBB field F2936, administered to participants who reported past daily smoking (F1249) and a prior cessation episode exceeding six months. records.concept: Maternal smoking around time of participant's birth
records.idealCde: Tobacco smoking behavior assessment: a set of related categorical items capturing multiple dimensions of an individual's smoking history and family smoking exposure. The concept encompasses: (1) Current tobacco smoking status — question 'Do you smoke tobacco now?' with response options: Yes on most or all days / Only occasionally / No; (2) Ever stopped smoking for more than 6 months (among former regular daily smokers) — question 'In the time that you smoked, did you ever stop for more than 6 months?' with response options: Yes / No; (3) Lifetime light smoking threshold (among occasional or minimal smokers) — question 'In your lifetime, have you smoked a total of at least 100 times?' with response options: Yes / No; (4) Likelihood of resuming smoking (among former regular daily smokers who previously stopped for 6+ months) — question 'Do you think you may start smoking again?' with categorical response options indicating probability of resumption; (5) Maternal smoking exposure around time of participant's birth — question 'Did your mother smoke regularly around the time when you were born?' with response options: Yes / No. Each item is a single-select categorical variable. Items 2, 3, and 4 are conditionally collected based on responses to prior items. Item 5 pertains to the participant's mother (not the participant themselves) and reflects perinatal secondhand smoke exposure. Answer type: categorical (single-select) for each sub-item; no continuous units.

records.concept: Self-reported weight change direction and magnitude over past 6 months
records.idealCde: Dietary pattern stability and recent weight change: A composite concept capturing (1) self-reported directional change in body weight over the past 6 months (gained / lost / stayed the same), (2) magnitude of that weight change in pounds or kilograms over the past 6 months, (3) whether major changes to diet have occurred in the past 5 years and the reason for any such change (illness vs. other), (4) whether the participant's diet on a reference day was atypical and, if so, the reason (illness, fasting, travel/away, or other), and (5) week-to-week variability of the habitual diet (never/rarely, sometimes, often). The ideal CDE set answers the question: 'How stable is this person's diet and body weight over recent time windows (past day, past week, past 6 months, past 5 years), and what factors have driven any changes?' Answer types: (1) ordinal categorical [gained / lost / stayed the same]; (2) continuous numeric with unit kg or lb; (3) binary yes/no with categorical reason sub-field [no change / yes-illness / yes-other reason]; (4) multi-select categorical [ill / fasting / away / other untypical diet]; (5) ordinal categorical [never or rarely / sometimes / often]. No single laterality, body-site, or subject-identity qualifier is specified; the fields reflect self-report from the study participant.

gencde.title: Self-Reported Weight Change Direction and Magnitude Over Past 6 Months
gencde.definition: A self-reported assessment capturing both the direction (gained, lost, or stayed the same) and the magnitude (in pounds or kilograms) of body weight change experienced by the participant over the preceding 6 months.
gencde.questionText: Compared with 6 months ago, have you gained weight, lost weight, or stayed about the same? If you gained or lost weight, how much weight did you gain or lose in the past 6 months?
relatedCdes: Weight gain 6 month value
Weight loss 6 month value
Abnormal unintentional weight gain 6 month status
gencde.rationale: Two source fields were harmonized: NUR_GLSWT_MCQ captures the directional component (gained/lost/stayed the same) and NUR_WTGL_MCQ captures the magnitude component (amount gained or lost). Because the schema requires a single data_type and the directional question is the primary categorical anchor, the permissible values reflect the direction codes. The magnitude sub-component (a numeric value in lbs or kg) is a companion element that should ideally be represented as a linked numeric CDE (data_type: numeric, units: kg or lb). Near-miss CDEs 'Weight gain 6 month value' and 'Weight loss 6 month status' were used to inform aliases but were not adopted as the canonical CDE because they capture only one direction or only the magnitude, not the combined directional-plus-magnitude concept. Missing-data sentinels and refusal codes present in source fields were excluded per instructions.

gencde.rationale: Canonical permissible values reconcile two UKBB source fields: the main field uses Never/rarely, Sometimes, Often; the pilot field uses Never/rarely, Sometimes, Usually, Always. All five distinct substantive answer concepts are preserved in sequential ordinal order (Never/rarely < Sometimes < Often < Usually < Always). Missing-data sentinels (-1=Do not know, -3=Prefer not to answer) are excluded per instructions. 'Often' and 'Usually' are treated as distinct ordinal steps rather than synonyms because both appear in the source data and represent meaningfully different frequencies. Confidence is slightly below 1.0 because the two source fields do not share a fully overlapping scale, requiring a merged five-point ordinal that no single source field fully instantiates.

transforms.rationale: Clear matches exist for heart failure, coronary heart disease, high cholesterol, hypertension, sickle cell disease, and stroke. Pulmonary embolism/DVT maps to Thrombotic Disorders. TIA is mapped to Stroke as the closest CDE equivalent (cerebrovascular event), though it is not identical. 'Other heart or blood condition' maps to 'Other chronic diseases/specify' as a catch-all. Anemia, atrial fibrillation, bleeding disorder, heart attack (acute event rather than chronic condition), heart valve disease, and peripheral vascular disease have no direct CDE equivalents and are left unmapped. Confidence is moderate due to TIA/Stroke approximation and several unmappable circulatory conditions. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:cb9a72569ba2b#g0): 16 of 16 source codes now map.

Most mental health conditions map to the broad CDE category 'Psychological and/or psychiatric disease or disorder' which explicitly includes anxiety, depression, and bipolar disorder; PTSD, schizophrenia, social phobia, personality disorder, and eating disorder are mapped there as best fits. Alcohol use disorder and drug use disorder map to 'Other substance use disorder'. ADHD and autism spectrum disorder are neurodevelopmental conditions that do not clearly fit the psychiatric/psychological bucket or any other specific CDE code, so they are left unmapped. 'Other mental health or substance use condition' is mapped to 'Other chronic diseases/specify' as a catch-all. The 'no condition' option maps to 'None of the above'. Confidence is moderate because several source codes require collapsing into a single broad CDE category. Extended against the refined element (REFCDE:cb9a72569ba2b#g0): 14 of 14 source codes now map.

records.concept: Fasting plasma glucose concentration (numeric, mg/dL)

cde.id: Fasting glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

records.idealCde: Fasting plasma glucose concentration measured after an overnight fast; answers 'What is the participant's fasting blood glucose level?' Expected answer type: numeric continuous value in units of mg/dL. Companion categorical classification field applies the 2003 ADA fasting criteria to categorize the result as: 0=Normal, 1=Impaired Fasting Glucose (IFG), 2=Untreated Diabetes, 3=Treated Diabetes. gencde.rationale: Source is a single UKBB Health and Wellbeing online follow-up question (Field 28688), asked conditionally when the respondent confirmed current difficulty sleeping. Missing-data sentinels (-1 Do not know, -3 Prefer not to answer) are excluded from the canonical permissible-value set per instructions. The four duration bands align broadly with clinical thresholds used to distinguish acute (<2 weeks), subacute (2–4 weeks), short-term (4–12 weeks), and chronic (>12 weeks) insomnia, but the labels are retained verbatim from the source rather than mapped to clinical terminology to avoid over-interpretation. Near-miss CDEs (PhenX longest sleep-problem period, EPDS unhappiness-related sleep item, clock-watching behavior item) address related but distinct constructs and were used only to inform aliases.

records.concept: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire event date (invitation sent, module started, or module completed)
records.idealCde: Online mental health/well-being questionnaire administration date: captures the date associated with a participant's online mental health or well-being questionnaire event (invitation sent, module started, or module completed). Question answered: 'What is the date of the specified online mental health/well-being questionnaire event (invitation dispatch, start, or completion) for this participant?' Answer type: Date (ISO 8601 format, YYYY-MM-DD). Note: member fields carry distinct event-type qualifiers (invitation sent, questionnaire completed, module started, module completed) and module-level qualifiers (general health module, mental health module); the ideal CDE should be instantiated separately for each combination of event type and module scope rather than collapsed into a single undifferentiated date field.

gencde.title: Online Mental Health / Well-Being Questionnaire Event Date
gencde.definition: The calendar date associated with a specified event in the administration of an online mental health or well-being questionnaire, where the event type may be invitation dispatch, overall questionnaire completion, or the start or completion of a named module (e.g., General Health, Mental Health).

gencde.rationale: All six source fields from UK Biobank share the same underlying concept — a date value tied to an online mental health/well-being questionnaire lifecycle event — but carry distinct event-type qualifiers (invitation sent, questionnaire completed, module started, module completed) and module-level qualifiers (General Health module, Mental Health module, overall). Because the concept is purely a date, there are no permissible values to enumerate; the canonical format is ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD). Implementers should pair this CDE with a companion qualifier variable capturing the specific event type and module name. Near-miss CDEs (SPMSQ date items, self-rated mental health question) were used only to confirm non-overlap and to inform alias terminology; no answer concepts from those CDEs were imported.

transforms.rationale: The source variable captures only whether someone is covered (yes/no) or unknown/refused, with no information about the TYPE of insurance. The TARGET CDE requires mapping to specific insurance types (employer, direct purchase, Medicare, Medicaid, TRICARE, IHS, other, uninsured). While '0=Not Covered' might conceptually align with 'Uninsured', the source code '1=Covered' cannot be mapped to any single CDE category without knowing the type of coverage. Mapping '0' to Uninsured alone would be misleading without the full context. All codes are left unmapped to avoid incorrect harmonization.

Mapping '0' to Uninsured alone would be misleading without the full context. All codes are left unmapped to avoid incorrect harmonization.

Most source codes map cleanly to CDE values. The main ambiguity is InsuranceTypeUpdate_VA (VA health care specifically) and InsuranceTypeUpdate_Military (TRICARE/military), which both map to the same CDE option 'TRICARE or other military health care, including VA health care' — the CDE consolidates these into one category. InsuranceTypeUpdate_None ('self-pay / no insurance') maps to 'Uninsured' as the closest equivalent, though self-pay is not strictly the same as uninsured. Confidence slightly reduced due to these two consolidations.

records.idealCde: Diabetes status and diabetes-related emotional burden: a cluster of fields capturing (1) diabetes diagnosis type — whether the subject has Type I diabetes (yes/no), Type II diabetes (yes/no), or pre-diabetes (yes/no); and (2) diabetes-specific psychosocial distress items assessing the degree to which living with diabetes causes depression ('Feeling depressed when thinking about living with diabetes') and daily mental/physical energy depletion ('Feeling that diabetes is taking up too much mental and physical energy every day'), each rated on a 5-point ordinal scale (0=Not a problem, 1=Minor problem, 2=Moderate problem, 3=Somewhat serious problem, 4=Serious problem). Diagnosis fields: binary yes/no per diabetes subtype. Distress fields: ordinal integer 0–4 per item, self-reported by the subject.

gencde.title: Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID) Scale — Psychosocial Distress Item (Depression / Energy Depletion / Fear)
gencde.definition: A single ordinal item from the Problem Areas in Diabetes (PAID) scale that quantifies the degree to which a specific diabetes-related emotional burden — feeling depressed when thinking about living with diabetes, feeling that diabetes consumes too much mental and physical energy daily, or feeling scared when thinking about living with diabetes — constitutes a problem for the respondent, rated on a 5-point scale from 'Not a problem' to 'Serious problem'.
gencde.questionText: How much of a problem is [feeling depressed when you think about living with diabetes / feeling that diabetes is taking up too much of your mental and physical energy every day / feeling scared when you think about living with diabetes] for you?
aliases: Problem Areas in Diabetes questionnaire item
relatedCdes: Are you feeling bothered, upset, or worried at this point in your pregnancy about the effect of ongoing health problems such as high blood pressure or diabetes on your pregnancy [NuPDQ]
Doctor or health care professional ever told you that you have diabetes
Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD-7) - worry too much scale
gencde.rationale: Three source fields (paid_dpr, paid_eng, paid_scrd) from the AI-READI cohort all share an identical 5-point ordinal response scale and represent distinct PAID scale items targeting depression, energy depletion, and fear as diabetes-specific psychosocial distress constructs. The canonical permissible-value set (codes 0–4) is drawn directly from the pooled observed answer options with no additions. This GenCDE describes the shared response-scale template; individual instantiations should specify the item stem (depression / energy / fear) as a qualifier. The PAID scale is a validated 20-item instrument (Welch et al., 1997); these items correspond to the emotional burden subscale. Near-miss CDEs (pregnancy worry, general diabetes diagnosis, GAD-7) were excluded as conceptually distinct. Confidence is slightly below 1.0 because the concept spans three related but distinct item stems that could alternatively be modeled as three separate CDEs.

records.concept: Number of activities prevented by pain or discomfort (ordinal: none/a few/some/most)
records.idealCde: Pain/Discomfort Activity Limitation: Captures the extent to which pain or discomfort prevents participation in activities, including both a summary frequency/severity rating and identification of specific activity types affected. Primary question: 'How many activities does your pain or discomfort prevent?' with ordinal response options (none, a few, some, most); supplemented by a multi-select checklist or free-text enumeration of specific prevented activities (e.g., sitting, bending/crouching, handling objects, and other activities), allowing multiple responses. Answer type: composite — (1) ordinal categorical scale [none / a few / some / most] for overall activity limitation count, and (2) multi-select categorical list of specific activity types prevented, coded as binary indicators per activity domain.

gencde.title: Number of Activities Prevented by Pain or Discomfort (Ordinal)
gencde.definition: An ordinal measure of the extent to which pain or discomfort prevents participation in activities, rated on a four-level scale from none to most activities affected.
gencde.questionText: How many activities does your pain or discomfort prevent? Would you say none, a few, some, or most?
relatedCdes: In the past 7 days How would you rate your pain on average?
Does your health now limit you in pursuing your hobbies or other leisure activities?
In the past 7 days How much did pain interfere with your ability to participate in leisure activities?
gencde.rationale: Derived from a single CLSA source field (HUP_PRVACT_MCQ). The four ordinal response options (none, a few, some, most) are preserved verbatim from the source and assigned sequential integer codes 0–3 reflecting increasing limitation. No numeric or binary alternatives were observed across cohorts. Near-miss CDEs (pain intensity ratings, leisure activity limitation, pain interference with leisure) address related but distinct constructs (intensity, domain-specific interference) and were used only to inform aliases. The ideal CDE anchor suggested a composite instrument including a multi-select activity checklist; however, no source field expresses that supplementary component, so only the ordinal summary item is encoded here. Confidence is moderate (0.82) given single-cohort sourcing and the straightforward, well-defined ordinal structure.

records.rationale: No candidate asks about the number (count) of activities prevented by pain/discomfort using the none/a few/some/most ordinal scale; the closest candidates either ask about specific activities, days prevented, or interference intensity rather than a count of activities prevented.

records.concept: Specific activity types prevented by pain or discomfort (multi-select checklist)
records.idealCde: Pain/Discomfort Activity Limitation: Captures the extent to which pain or discomfort prevents participation in activities, including both a summary frequency/severity rating and identification of specific activity types affected. Primary question: 'How many activities does your pain or discomfort prevent?' with ordinal response options (none, a few, some, most); supplemented by a multi-select checklist or free-text enumeration of specific prevented activities (e.g., sitting, bending/crouching, handling objects, and other activities), allowing multiple responses. Answer type: composite — (1) ordinal categorical scale [none / a few / some / most] for overall activity limitation count, and (2) multi-select categorical list of specific activity types prevented, coded as binary indicators per activity domain.

gencde.title: Specific Activity Types Prevented by Pain or Discomfort (Multi-Select Checklist)
gencde.definition: A multi-select checklist identifying the specific types of activities (e.g., sitting, bending/crouching, handling objects, communicating/listening, and other activities) that a respondent reports being prevented from performing due to pain or discomfort.
gencde.questionText: What were these activities? (Do not read list; multiple responses allowed — code all that apply.)

gencde.rationale: Source fields from CLSA (PA2_SIT_BIN_MCQ, PA2_SIT_COM_MCQ, PA2_SIT_CRO_MCQ, PA2_SIT_HAN_MCQ, PA2_SIT_LIS_MCQ) each represent one response option in a multi-select checklist administered after a filter question about whether pain prevents activities. The five canonical permissible values are derived directly from the five observed source field suffixes: SIT=Sitting, CRO=Bending/Crouching, HAN=Handling objects, COM=Communicating/Listening, BIN=Other/Binary catch-all. Because this is a multi-select item, each code may be independently endorsed (1=yes, 0=no) per respondent; the CDE represents the full set of selectable options. Near-miss CDEs (difficulty with hobbies, active sports, leisure activities) were used only to inform aliases. Confidence is moderate (0.78) because the exact label text for each source field was inferred from variable-name suffixes rather than confirmed codebook text.

Spent without very much physical activity
I mostly did things like watching television, reading or playing cards. Most weekends I was able to get outdoors for some light exercise
going for walks, playing a round of golf (without motorized carts), or doing some active chores around the house.

Three times per week, on the average, I engaged in some moderate activity

records.concept: Family history of circulatory/cardiovascular conditions (which blood relatives have had specific heart/blood conditions)

cde.id: Family health problems cardiovascular history type

records.idealCde: Family history of circulatory/cardiovascular conditions: captures which first-degree biological relatives (mother, father, sibling, daughter, son, and potentially other blood relatives) have been diagnosed with specific heart and blood conditions. The question asked is: 'Who in your family (related by blood) has had [specific circulatory condition]?' or equivalently 'Has anyone in your family ever been diagnosed with the following heart and blood conditions?' Conditions covered include congestive heart failure, coronary artery/coronary heart disease (including angina), heart attack (myocardial infarction), heart valve disease, aortic aneurysm, atrial fibrillation, anemia, and other circulatory conditions. Answer type: multi-select checkbox matrix — for each condition, one or more affected relative types are selected from: Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, and other blood relatives; responses are categorical (select all that apply), yielding a set of [condition × relative-type] Boolean indicators per respondent. Subject qualifier: biological family members (not self); no laterality or body-site qualifier applies.
